title: Director, Food & Beverage
description:
ABOUT ORCHESTRA

Orchestra is a strategic communications and marketing company built for today’s complex and fragmented world. From decoding audiences to designing bold strategies, Orchestra integrates people, platforms, and stories that stick to help clients build lasting influence. The company offers programs that span from the highest level strategic business counsel through to tactical execution. Orchestra brings together 700+ people with experience across consumer and lifestyle, technology, nonprofit and philanthropy, real estate, sports, travel, hospitality, and more. Made up of leading firms BerlinRosen, Civitas Public Affairs Group, Derris, Glen Echo Group, Inkhouse, M18, Message Lab, Onward and Small Girls PR. It also launched Brightmode, a talent acquisition firm for communications professionals, and Versus Media Group, a strategy-first political media team. Learn more at .

People of all backgrounds and abilities are strongly encouraged to apply. Orchestra is committed to building and maintaining a diverse staff, and recognizes that its continued success depends on hiring and retaining high-quality creative professionals with a variety of backgrounds and experiences. Opportunities for advancement exist, and we are committed to helping all staff develop and grow.

ABOUT THIS ROLE

Orchestra is looking for a Director who knows the food & beverage world and has strong instincts for what makes people want to taste, try, visit and talk about something. You’ll lead integrated communications strategies for food, beverage and lifestyle brands, turning what’s happening across media and culture into stories, experiences and campaigns that get noticed. You’ll counsel senior clients, develop creative ideas and guide teams across earned media, influencer marketing, partnerships and brand experiences. We’re looking for someone who genuinely knows this space, from the media shaping the conversation to the trends, people and places everyone will be talking about next.

Note: This role is based in our NYC office, working two-three days a week in the office on a hybrid schedule.

ACCOUNTABILITIES AND QUALIFICATIONS

As a Director, you will...

  • Set communications strategy across food & beverage and lifestyle accounts, from big-picture planning through execution
  • Serve as a senior client partner, bringing proactive counsel, creative ideas and solutions to the table
  • Lead earned media strategy and help teams turn client goals, trends and cultural moments into stories people want to cover
  • Develop integrated campaign ideas that can come to life across PR, influencer marketing, partnerships, events and experiences
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with food, beverage and lifestyle media and other influential voices in the space
  • Help bring launches, tastings, dinners, partnerships, activations, festivals and other brand experiences to life
  • Stay close to what’s happening across food, hospitality, media and culture and turn those insights into opportunities for clients
  • Lead major client presentations, strategic planning and high-stakes moments with confidence
  • Lead and develop account teams while maintaining a high bar for strategy, creativity and execution
  • Identify opportunities to deepen client relationships and grow the work
  • Understand how F&B fits into the broader hotel or destination experience, developing strategies that support individual venues and overall property/placemaking goals
  • Bring a broad understanding of the F&B landscape, from CPG and QSR brands to Michelin-starred restaurants, with spirits and cocktail industry experience a plus
  • Be an active presence in the hospitality scene, building relationships with chefs, restaurateurs, bartenders and tastemakers through regular engagement in the field

Essential skills:

  • 7-9+ years of PR, strategic communications or integrated marketing experience; agency experience strongly preferred
  • Deep experience working with food & beverage, culinary, hospitality and/or lifestyle brands
  • Strong media relations expertise and established relationships with relevant reporters and editors
  • Experience developing integrated campaigns that extend beyond traditional earned media
  • Understanding of influencer marketing and how it can complement PR, events, partnerships and brand experiences
  • Strong creative instincts and the ability to turn cultural and category trends into relevant ideas for clients
  • Excellent client counsel, writing and presentation skills
  • Experience leading and developing teams across multiple accounts or workstreams

WORKING AT ORCHESTRA

Salary range: $110,000 - $125,000, commensurate with experience

#LI-Hybrid

Orchestra is the first communications company built for today’s media landscape. Since 2022, it’s acquired nine firms, including: BerlinRosen, Civitas Public Affairs Group, Derris, Glen Echo Group, Inkhouse, M18, Message Lab, Onward and Small Girls PR. It also launched Brightmode, a talent acquisition firm for communication professionals. Learn more at: .

title: Managerial Assistant III
description:
Office of the Illinois Secretary of State
Alexi Giannoulias

Job Title: Managerial Assistant III
Division: Planning & Development
Union: N/A
Location: 501 S. 2nd St., Springfield, IL – Sangamon County
Salary: Range from $68,844 to $78,000 annually – commensurate with experience.
Benefits:

Overview:

Performs highly technical and responsible administrative duties by participating in complex investigations of hazardous materials in the buildings in the Capitol Complex; ensures that all levels are in compliance with state guidelines; performs administrative duties by providing assistance and judgment in budgetary matters for hazardous material programs for removal and preventative maintenance; serves as project coordinator for assigned construction projects in the Capitol Complex; performs extensive liaison duties between the Executive IV and state investigators, outside contractors, architects, Capitol Development Board, etc.; relays information to the Executive IV and other management staff on construction project status; develops long and short range goals relating to the area of assignment.

Duties and Responsibilities:
  • Subject to administrative approval, reports to the Executive IV, performs highly technical administrative duties including complex investigations of hazardous materials in the Capitol Complex and three Chicago Metro Facilities. Ensures that workplace environments are in accord with State and Federal codes.
  • Establishes design criteria and develops scope statements for the purposes of bidding design contracts for environmental contracts. Works closely with the Exec. IV to determine appropriate actions and procedures for environmental projects. Develop long and short-term goals relating to the assignment.
  • Participates in complex studies investigations of hazardous materials such as asbestos, lead based paint, etc. in the Capitol Complex; analyzes current levels of hazardous materials through major site evaluations of the Capitol Complex; ensures that all levels are in compliance with State and Federal guidelines. Coordinates with outside contractors for the removal of hazardous materials. Develops and prepares confidential and highly sensitive reports on hazardous material measurements and removal procedures.
  • Manages and coordinates construction projects on the Capitol Complex, including developing project priorities and scopes for submittal to the Executive IV for approval. Assist in the development of project budgeting from various appropriations. Meet with and coordinate with Design Architects and Engineers to develop project design and bidding documents for the bidding and implementation of construction projects on the Capitol Complex. Coordinate construction projects with SOS Trades, Custodial Staff, and other Agencies on the Capitol Complex. Develop and maintain highly technical project files and documents including pay request logs, change order logs, and other construction related documents. Provide field reports to the Executive IV on all construction activities on a weekly basis.
  • Participate in the development of Hazardous Materials and workplace environment programs required by State and Federal Regulatory Agencies and the timely submittal of these plans to these agencies.
  • Participates in the development of long- and short-term goals related to environmental activities and construction projects including assisting in implementing of said goals.
  • Attends various professional workshops and meetings in order to obtain knowledge and insight necessary to assist the Executive IV in the decision-making process regarding hazardous materials and workplace environments.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.
Education and Experience:

Requires knowledge, skill and mental development equivalent to the completion of four (4) years of college, preferably with courses in public or business administration AND three (3) years of professional experience in a public or private organization. Additional requirements may need to be met for applicants to be deemed qualified for individual positions within the class; this may include specific licenses, certification or credentials as related to the position's duties and responsibilities as defined by the Department of Personnel.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:
  • Requires extensive knowledge of administrative practices and methods.
  • Requires working knowledge of departmental operations.
  • Requires ability to express complex ideas clearly both orally and in writing.
  • Requires ability to develop and maintain satisfactory working relationships with management, other agency representatives and the general public.
  • Requires ability to analyze operational and administrative problems and to adopt an effective course of action.
  • Requires ability to deal tactfully with matters of a confidential, sensitive or controversial nature.
  • Requires ability to exercise independent judgment in dealing with operational and personnel management problems and to take appropriate course of action to correct such problems.
  • Requires willingness to travel and possession of a valid Illinois driver’s license as required by individual positions within the class.
  • Require lifting and carrying 0 to 25 pounds.
Application Process:
  • Please visit to apply by completing the online application; you may also upload a resume or other attachments as needed.
  • Preference will be given to Illinois residents in the hiring and selection process, in accordance with the Illinois Secretary of State Merit Employment Code.
  • Questions regarding this posting or Illinois Secretary of State employment practices may be directed to Job Counselors at our Personnel offices in Chicago (312-793-5515) or Springfield (217-782-4783).
Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. Applicants must be lawfully authorized to work in the United States.
Applicants are considered for all positions without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital or veteran status, or the presence of a non-job-related medical condition or disability.

title: Beauty Counter Manager - Bobbi Brown - Cherry Creek Shopping Center
description:
Job Description

In the Nordstrom Beauty Department, we strive to make our customers feel their best. As a member of the Beauty community, you'll create personalized beauty experiences for customers and be part of a passionate team that values your unique skills.

The Beauty Counter Manager plays a dual role – part salesperson, part teacher – while maximizing sales in their assigned beauty brand. Ideal candidates are results-oriented and thrive in a commissioned sales environment, are passionate about beauty trends and can build a customer following both in-store and digitally.

A day in the life…

  • Collaborate with team members to create a welcoming and inclusive environment for all customers
  • Set and achieve personal and counter sales goals, utilizing both in-store and digital selling tools (inclusive of text and social media)
  • Manage the scheduling and execution of vendor events and promotions
  • Build and maintain strong vendor relationships to maximize business results
  • Keep department customer-ready through organization and cleanliness
  • Keep up with the latest beauty trends, products, and industry knowledge through trainings provided by Nordstrom and luxury brand partners

You own this if you have…

  • Empathy and respect for all customers, providing a supportive environment during makeup and skincare application
  • Strong multitasking, organization, and follow-through skills
  • Drive to achieve sales goals, with interest in using networking and technology
  • The ability to work a flexible schedule based on business needs, including evenings and weekends

title: Guide, Exercise Physiology & Sports Performance
description:
Salary Range: $93,000.00- $118,000.00
About Sensei

Founded by Dr. David Agus and Larry Ellison, our ecosystem of products and experiences is designed with one intention: to empower you to grow well and lead the world toward greater wellbeing.

Based on Dr. Agus’ philosophy, Sensei believes we can guide our guests to greater wellbeing by offering experiential movement, rest and nourishment classes and programs. The launch of the Retreats wellness brand took place on Lana’i, Hawaii in partnership with Four Season’s lodging and food offerings by Nobu. In this location, Sensei Porcupine Creek, Sensei is operating the lodging operation, as well as world-class golf, tennis, spa, fitness, movement, nutrition, meditative, enrichment and body assessment facilities. In addition, Sensei will run the F&B operation, as part of a licensing agreement with Nobu. Sensei programs and continuing learning sessions are high-touch, evidence-led and supported by the latest technology. You can read our story here.

Position Description

Exercise Physiologist will work in conjunction with nutritionists, mindfulness coaches, spa and wellness practitioners in a luxury resort setting, while leveraging evidenced-based content and technology, deliver the best practices in exercise physiology. At Sensei, we balance purpose with play. Guests enjoy health coaching, 1:1 nutrition, fitness, meditation and mindset sessions, body treatments, educational lectures and a variety of outdoor activities – all designed to expand awareness and connection. The Sensei guide leverages data, self-awareness, self-efficacy and safety to deliver our guest experience through guided sessions with our guests. Combining spaces and environments to imbue feelings of safety and ease; domain expertise to interpret objective data and craft a personalized wellness plan; and health coaching to communicate this information in an empowering, affirming manner. Sensei has designed the guide program to support our guest in achieving greater wellbeing.

  • Passion to empower individuals seeking to optimize health and lifestyle
  • Passion for continuing education, professional development and personal growth

  • Works well with people and possesses a friendly and outgoing personality

title: Senior Full-Stack Software Engineer, Integrations
description:
Ready to accelerate your career?

Cardata is where driven people make an outsized impact. We’re a small but mighty team transforming how businesses manage vehicle reimbursement — replacing outdated programs with smart, automated solutions.

Our vision is bold: to provide the most comprehensive, intelligent, and automated software and services for creating ideal vehicle programs. And we’re building toward that vision every single day.

Join us and you’ll find challenge, growth, and the chance to deliver real impact — helping hundreds of companies and thousands of drivers across North America focus on the work that matters most to them.

We’re searching for a Senior Full-Stack Software Engineer to help build our new Integrations pod. Our Portal connects with the HR, payroll, driver safety, and expense management systems our customers already use. These integrations keep driver information current and support some of our most important customer workflows.

When an integration fails, the impact can be difficult to spot: a new hire never appears, a former employee stays active, or information falls out of sync. You’ll build connections customers can trust and make sure we catch problems before they do.

Reporting to the Manager of the team, you’ll own integrations end to end, from a partner’s API to the screens customers use to connect and configure them. As one of the pod’s first engineers, you’ll help establish its technical standards, delivery practices, and approach to keeping integrations healthy in production.

What You’ll Do

  • Own integrations from design through launch and ongoing production health, partnering with Product, QA, and the other Portal engineering teams.
  • Work with Product and partners to clarify requirements, resolve gaps in API documentation, agree on scope, and deliver against committed dates.
  • Build backend services, data models, APIs, background jobs, and customer-facing interfaces for connecting and configuring integrations.
  • Design data mapping, synchronization, retries, and reconciliation within established platform patterns, documenting key decisions in architecture decision records.
  • Build syncs, webhooks, and scheduled jobs that handle rate limits, duplicate events, partial failures, and partner outages without creating unnecessary manual cleanup.
  • Create shared building blocks and clear adapter interfaces for authentication, data mapping, synchronization, and error handling, making each new integration easier to deliver.
  • Build monitoring, alerts, and runbooks that help the team detect failures early and recover reliably.
  • Help customers connect, configure, and check the health of their integrations independently.
  • Protect partner credentials and personal information through secure token handling, encryption, least-privilege access, safe logging, and reliable separation of customer data.
  • Use AI coding agents to accelerate development and testing while carefully reviewing their output. Help shape how the pod uses AI for integration work.
  • Strengthen the pod’s standards for design reviews, code reviews, testing, documentation, and production support.
  • Hold launches that don’t meet agreed standards for data correctness, security, and monitoring, working with the Lead Mobile Engineer and Product on go/no-go decisions.

In your first 30 days, you’ll learn how our existing integrations work and ship changes to at least one in production. Within three months, you’ll have designed, scoped, and delivered your first new integration by its agreed deadline. Within six months, several integrations you’ve contributed to will be live and meeting their quality goals, and you’ll be a go-to expert for the other Portal teams.

What You Bring

  • 7+ years building production software, including at least 3 years building and running third-party integrations. Your track record matters more than your title.
  • Strong full-stack experience across backend services and product interfaces, with ownership spanning data models, APIs, background jobs, and customer-facing screens.
  • Experience designing, shipping, and operating integrations that customers depend on, including syncs, webhooks, and scheduled jobs.
  • A practical understanding of retries, duplicates, partial failures, rate limits, and partner outages. You can explain an integration failure you handled and what you changed afterward.
  • Experience designing reusable integration architecture, including adapter interfaces and shared capabilities for authentication, mapping, synchronization, and error handling. You know when an abstraction helps.
  • A track record of delivering large features or products against firm deadlines by breaking down work, sequencing delivery, raising risks early, and making deliberate scope decisions.
  • The ability to turn a goal and incomplete information into clear requirements, working directly with Product and partners to close gaps and move delivery forward.
  • Experience using AI coding agents such as Cursor or Claude Code to deliver faster, with sound judgment about context, verification, and the mistakes AI-assisted development can introduce.
  • Production experience protecting credentials and personal information, including OAuth, token handling, encryption at rest, least-privilege access, safe logging, and separation of customer data.
  • The ability to improve the work of other engineers through thoughtful design and code reviews.

Our current stack includes TypeScript, NestJS, Next.js, React, PostgreSQL with Prisma, BullMQ, Redis, Vitest, Playwright, GitHub Actions, Datadog, and Flagsmith feature flags.

Compensation

In line with Ontario’s Pay Transparency legislation, the salary range for this role is $150,000 – $175,000 CAD annually, based on experience, skills, and alignment with the role requirements. This is a vacant position, and we are hiring with intention and seeking someone who will bring new perspective, contribute meaningfully to the team, and grow with the organization.

Why you’ll love working at Cardata:

We’ll be honest — Cardata isn’t for everyone. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, take extreme ownership, and constantly push yourself (and your work) to be the best, you’ll fit right in.

You’ll be surrounded by driven teammates who genuinely care — about the work, about our customers, and about helping each other succeed. Together, we take on ambitious goals and celebrate the wins along the way.

What we offer in return for you bringing your best:

  • Remote work and flexible working hours
  • Mentorship and development opportunities (to help you achieve your career goals!)
  • Extended medical & dental benefits
  • Healthcare spending account
  • $3,000 annual Health and Wellness Spending Account to support your overall wellbeing
  • Employee assistance program (EAP)
  • Flexible (Unlimited) Time Off: No annual cap on vacation, supported by a trust-based, flexible approach to time away.

Cardata is an equal opportunity employer. All candidates will be equally considered without regard to race, ancestry, place of origin, colour, ethnic origin, language, citizenship, creed, religion, gender/gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, physical and/or mental handicap or financial ability. We are dedicated to creating an inclusive environment where everyone feels welcome to bring their authentic selves to work.

If you require accommodations during the recruitment process, please let us know.

title: To-Go
description:

description:

Joining AdventHealth is about being part of something bigger. It’s about belonging to a community that believes in the wholeness of each person, and serves to uplift others in body, mind and spirit. title: Network Based Systems Analyst IV
description:
Title: Network Based Systems Analyst IV

Description:
Solutions³ LLC is supporting a U.S. Government customer to provide support for on- and offsite incident response to government agencies and critical infrastructure owners who experience cyber-attacks. Solutions³ LLC delivers advanced technical assistance, proactive hunting, rapid onsite incident response, and immediate investigation using host- and network-based cybersecurity analysis capabilities. Personnel perform investigations to characterize the severity of breaches and develop mitigation/remediation plans.

Solutions³ LLC is seeking a Network Forensics Analyst with deep expertise in one or more edge device technologies (Cisco, Ivanti, Palo Alto, Ciena, Juniper) to support this critical customer mission.

Salary Range: $112,000 - $131,000
Location: Arlington, VA
Job Type: Onsite

Eligibility:
  • Must be a US Citizen
  • Must have an active TS/SCI clearance
  • Must be able to obtain DHS Suitability prior to starting employment
  • 8+ years of directly relevant experience
Responsibilities Include:
  • Serves as a hunt and incident response subject matter expert (SME), applying in-depth knowledge of threat actor tools, techniques, and procedures (TTPs), with a focus on network centric and edge device compromises.
  • Serves as an incident response expert in support of a technology insertion team, evaluating and integrating new network forensic and monitoring capabilities.
  • Assists the Government lead in coordinating teams for preliminary incident response investigations, including onsite and remote engagements.
  • Assists the Government lead by interfacing with the customer while onsite, clearly communicating status, findings, and recommendations.
  • Characterizes and analyzes network traffic (including PCAP, flow, and device logs) to identify anomalous activity and potential threats to network resources.
  • Identifies and analyzes anomalies in network traffic using metadata (e.g., flow records, DNS logs, proxy logs) to detect and scope malicious activity.
  • Reconstructs malicious attacks or activities based on network traffic, including timelines, attacker paths, and data exfiltration patterns.
  • Examines network topologies to understand data flows, trust boundaries, and potential choke points; uses this understanding to inform hunt and response activities.
  • Assesses network topology and device configurations, identifying critical security concerns and providing security best practice recommendations, especially for Cisco, Ivanti, Palo Alto, Ciena, and Juniper platforms.
  • Determines appropriate courses of action in response to identified and analyzed anomalous network activity, including containment, eradication, and hardening actions.
  • Applies knowledge of defense-in-depth principles and general attack stages to evaluate and improve network security architecture and edge-device configurations.
  • Applies knowledge of network device integrity concepts and methodologies to validate device state, detect unauthorized modification, and recommend remediation.
  • Leads analysis of device logs, configurations, and telemetry from routers, switches, firewalls, VPNs, and remote access appliances to identify, scope, and reconstruct intrusions.
  • Provides expert support, analysis, and research with only broad direction into exceptionally complex problems and processes relating to hunt and incident response activities.
  • Serves as a technical expert on high-level incident response teams, providing technical direction, interpretation, and alternatives for network-centric incidents.
  • Exercises considerable latitude in determining technical objectives and independently develops technical solutions to complex problems requiring ingenuity and creativity.
  • Analyzes incident data and victim environments to recommend targeted mitigations, including network segmentation, policy updates, and device hardening.
  • Advises technical personnel on countermeasure implementation and customization (e.g., firewall rules, IPS signatures, access control lists).
  • Supports internal stakeholders on containment and eradication missions, on-site and remotely.
  • Ensures evidence integrity is preserved according to standard operating procedures or national standards when collecting network data, device artifacts, and logs.
  • Assists with the writing and publishing of Computer Network Defense (CND) guidance and detailed reports on incident findings to appropriate constituencies.
  • Distills analytic findings into executive summaries and in-depth technical reports suitable for both leadership and highly technical audiences.
  • Documents analysis, TTPs, and device specific incident handling procedures in a standardized knowledge base for sharing and publication.
  • Assists in maintaining branch process and procedure documentation and guides the completion of hunt and incident response activities.
Required Skills:
  • 3+ years of experience related to the evaluation and implementation of new cyber response or network forensic capabilities.
  • Hands-on experience with incident response or network operations involving enterprise edge devices from at least two of the following vendors: Cisco, Ivanti, Palo Alto, Ciena, Juniper.
  • Strong understanding of network architecture and security, including routing, switching, VPNs, firewalls, segmentation, and defense in depth.
  • Knowledge of Computer Network Defense (CND) policies, procedures, and regulations relevant to U.S. government or similar environments.
  • Ability to:
    • Characterize and analyze network traffic to identify anomalous activity and potential threats.
    • Identify and analyze anomalies in network traffic using metadata (flow, DNS, proxy, etc.).
    • Reconstruct malicious activity based on network traffic and device logs.
  • Understanding of general attack stages (reconnaissance, initial access, lateral movement, exfiltration, etc.) and how they manifest across the network.
  • Understanding of system and application security threats and vulnerabilities and how they are observed in network traffic.
  • Understanding of proactive analysis of systems and networks, including establishing trust levels of critical resources and detecting anomalous behavior.
  • Proficiency with common operating systems (e.g., Linux/Unix, Windows).
  • Experience performing cyber incident response (scoping, containment, eradication, recovery) in operational environments.
  • Ability to think independently, make sound decisions under pressure, and work with limited guidance.
  • Superior written and oral communication skills, including the ability to clearly explain technical issues to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Ability to work collaboratively across physical locations and within distributed teams.
  • Skilled in identifying different classes of attacks and attack stages and translating findings into actionable recommendations.
  • Rapid Network & Tapping Setup: Ability to quickly configure network TAPs, packet brokers, SPAN ports, and unmanaged/managed switches without disrupting live production or air-gapped traffic.
Desired Skills:
  • Experience leading and mentoring technical teams in incident response, network operations, or security engineering.
  • Network and system administration experience in large or complex enterprise or service-provider environments.
  • Strong understanding of adversarial TTPs (including MITRE ATT&CK) and different operational threat environments (e.g., script kiddies, non nation state adversaries, nation state actors).
  • Knowledge of defense-in-depth and zero trust principles and their application to network and edge-device architectures.
  • Knowledge of system and application security threats and vulnerabilities (e.g., buffer overflow, mobile code, cross-site scripting, injections, race conditions, covert channels, replay, ROP, malicious code).
  • Knowledge of network device integrity verification and monitoring approaches.
  • Hands-on skill in host/network intrusion detection and event correlation across multiple telemetry sources (firewalls, IDS/IPS, endpoint, SIEM).
  • Experience with malicious activity analysis, including network beaconing, C2, and data exfiltration detection.
  • Experience with Identity and Access Management (IAM) tools and their integration into network/edge security architectures.
  • Ability to review and analyze Enterprise Architecture (EA) from a security perspective and recommend architecture-level improvements.
  • Ability to collaborate with stakeholders at multiple levels within an organization (technical staff, management, senior leadership).
  • Field Diagnostics & Cyber Forensics: Skills in running preloaded analysis stacks, protocol parsers (e.g., Modbus, DNP3, OPC UA), vulnerability scanning, and local packet capture at line rate.
  • Compact Pack & Weight Management: Packing, securing, and transporting ruggedized cases (such as Pelican or Nanuk) that fit standard weight and carry-on/air-transport limits
Desired Certifications:
  • IASAE II, CSSP Analyst, GCIA, GCIH, CSSP Incident Responder, CEH, SANS GIAC GCIA or GNFA (preferred for network forensics), SANS GRID, GICSP, or GCIP (plus).
  • Vendor / network certifications (highly desired):
    • Cisco CCNA (or higher: CCNP Security, CCNP Enterprise).
    • Vendor certifications for Palo Alto, Juniper, Ciena, or Ivanti (e.g., PCNSE, JNCIS/JNCIP, etc.).
Required Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Cyber Security, Computer Engineering, or related degree; or High School Diploma and 10+ years of technical experience in the area of expertise

title: Drainage Design Segment Manager
description:

Overview:

Ferrovial is seeking a Drainage Design Segment Manager to support the I-285 Eastside Express Lanes Project in Atlanta, Georgia. The successful candidate will lead the development and delivery of hydrologic, hydraulic, and drainage designs for a major segment of this transportation infrastructure project, for both Phase 1 & Phase 2, working within a multidisciplinary team. Responsibilities include managing drainage studies and analyses, developing stormwater solutions, preparing technical reports and construction documents, coordinating with other disciplines, and overseeing drainage design schedules and deliverables. We are looking for candidates with over 8 years of experience who demonstrate strong technical expertise, leadership skills, and experience delivering drainage solutions for complex transportation projects.


Responsibilities and Duties:

  • Lead and oversee the development of drainage engineering deliverables, including studies, hydraulic and hydrologic analyses, design calculations, plans, specifications, and technical reports.
  • Manage drainage design activities, including flood studies, stormwater management, and evaluation of engineering alternatives to develop practical and compliant solutions.
  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to younger engineers, designers, and CAD staff, ensuring quality, consistency, and adherence to project requirements.
  • Coordinate with project management, clients, consultants, and multidisciplinary teams to support project delivery, schedules, and design integration.
  • Plan, prioritize, and monitor drainage design tasks and resources to ensure timely completion of deliverables and compliance with contractual and regulatory requirements.
  • Lead drainage teams and apply engineering best practices to manage flooding risk, stormwater management, and overall drainage design performance.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Civil Engineering or a related field.

  • 8+ years of experience in transportation drainage design, including freeways, highways, and interchanges.
  • Experience serving as Engineer of Record (EOR) and leading drainage design teams.
  • Proficiency with industry-standard drainage design software, including OpenRoads, MicroStation, StormCAD, HEC-RAS, HEC-HMS, HY-8, and ProjectWise.
  • Strong understanding of construction documents, specifications, and engineering design practices.
  • Excellent leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work in a fastpaced environment.
  • Demonstrated commitment to quality, integrity, and professional ethics.

title: Clinical Abstraction Specialist
description:
SUMMARY:

The Clinical Abstraction Specialist reports to the Manager of Clinical Abstraction Services. Under general supervision and within Brown University Health established policies and procedures, manages coordination and implementation of duties associated with the abstraction of clinical quality data for public and other reporting through the national quality initiatives for all Brown University Health affiliates.

Responsible for accessing medical records information for the purposes of completing clinical abstraction.

Manages abstraction workflow and monitors abstraction and reporting deadlines including but not limited to data submission due dates for The Joint Commission (TJC) core measure reporting and CMS requirements.

Monitors changes and additions in quality reporting measures, specifications, and rules of abstraction to ensure measurement standards of Hospital quality program, The Joint Commission (TJC), Centers for Medicare and Medicaid (CMS) and other regulatory agency requirements are met.

Supports the care team and Medical Staff in the identification of care opportunities and facilitates improvement activities. Serves as liaison between certified related vendors and/or outsourced abstraction services.


Brown University Health employees are expected to successfully role model the organization's values of Compassion, Accountability, Respect, and Excellence as these values guide our everyday actions with patients, customers and one another.


RESPONSIBILITIES:

Accesses vendor abstraction tools, including reporting options, and the clinical warehouse for data reporting to ensure accuracy of data reports through rate verification during preview periods and the validation process. Submits corrections or appeals as directed.
Supports the clinical data abstraction and management process for clinical quality measures, i.e. vendor issues and deadlines, system maintenance, training and scheduling, monitoring data for accuracy and verification. Completes and supports work assigned to the project team for specific task assignments including data management, medical record coordination, and abstraction, in accordance with HIPAA regulations.
Facilitates team activities such as team meetings to communicate indicator changes, data collections issues, specification updates and interpretation, medical record changes or additions. Must stay abreast of all concurrent and ongoing changes to abstraction rules, populations, public reporting requirements, and adherence to outlined information flow both internally and externally.
Serves as a resource for internal customers to understand data collection specifications, documentation requirements, data interpretation to facilitate improvement activities. Participates in group and project activities for process improvement as directed.
Notifies manager of changes in trends or results associated with performance levels and/or compliance with evidenced-based care in real-time.
Assists in identifying gaps in documentation that impact accuracy or measured performance on required measures of performance. Aligns goals of abstraction services with upstream documentation and clinical services workflows, identifies gaps as opportunities for improvement.
Supports technical training programs aimed at performance improvement. Ensures that all abstraction work is accurate and complete, and communicates, coaches and trains as required to standards to assist peers. Implements processes (as directed) aimed at measuring accuracy of completed abstraction of assigned measures and completes audits that measure effectiveness of teamwork flow and accuracy as required.
Facilitates and coaches teams working to improve performance.

Coordinates and supports the implementation of improvement tactics in alignment with organizational priorities.
Notifies the Manager of Abstraction Services when issues arise and takes corrective action as needed.
Performs other duties as assigned.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

Bachelor's Degree or equivalent in nursing or other healthcare related field is required.
Master's Degree in health care or health science discipline preferred.
Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality (CPHQ) is preferred.
Certification in Lean/Six Sigma (Green Belt or Black Belt) and TapRoot methodologies is required or must be attained within first 24 months of working in position (provided on-site).


EXPERIENCE:
Two or more years of relevant experience in chart abstraction, measurement support, technical training, education, facilitation and best practice identification preferably in a large complex healthcare organization.
Knowledge of problems, activities and causes related to provision of clinical care and of methods of quality assessment.
Knowledge of federal, state and voluntary quality management regulations and standards.
Must possess excellent verbal and written skills, ability to be self-directed and obtain current quality initiative and specification details from federal and state manuals.
Expertise with access and understanding to of data sources such as medical records, financial data, department/service specific data, and various Brown University Health-wide manual and automated data systems.
Demonstrates technical knowledge of the Specification Manual for National Hospital Quality Measures and other data specification manuals as relevant to assigned areas of abstraction responsibility.


WORK ENVIRONMENT AND PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:
Work is performed in a typical office setting, requiring extensive periods of sitting, with arms extended as well as walking and standing.


INDEPENDENT ACTION:
Performs independently within the department policies and procedures; refers specific problems to the Director where clarification of departmental policies and procedures or workload may be required.

None.

  • LinkedIn Top Startup (2022) · Glassdoor Best Places to Work, #6 (2022)

The role

Pacaso buyers are high-net-worth individuals making a considered purchase over months, sometimes years. They move between our site, email, messaging, and our Sales team, and today each of those runs on its own tools with its own picture of the customer. We believe one personalized system that follows each customer from first interest to purchase, and keeps serving them as an owner, will shorten the path to purchase and make our growth product-led.

We're hiring a principal-level technical product manager to own that system and its outcome. You'll own the system-level design: the components, how they fit together, what the system decides and why, and how the AI agents behave. You'll own the roadmap, and you'll do hands-on work yourself: working prototypes built with AI tooling, UI design, and the prompts behind the agents. Engineering owns the technical design and implementation, and you shape and review it with them as it goes to production.

This is a technical product leadership role, not a backlog-management role and not a production engineering role. You'll make product calls with Sales, Marketing, and leadership, work through system tradeoffs with senior engineers, and be accountable for the outcome.

Some of this is already moving. AI agents talk to our customers today, and parts of the data and decisioning exist. None of it runs end to end on its own yet. You'll take what's there, decide what to keep, and design the system that can.

What you'll own

  • The system-level design. One design for new leads, dormant leads, and stalled buyers first, then owners who add a share, so the same person is served by one system instead of separate tools for each stage. You own the components, how they fit together, what the system decides and why, and the agent behavior and prompts. Engineering owns the technical design and implementation, and you shape and review it with them.
  • The customer intelligence layer. What the system knows about each customer across channels and how it acts on it: signals, shared memory and context, scoring, eligibility and frequency caps, and the next-best-action logic that decides what happens next.
  • Agent and workflow design. Which agents exist, what each one is allowed to decide, how they hand off to each other and to Sales, and the prompts, tools, and orchestration behind them.
  • Trust and reliability. Evaluation frameworks, guardrails, observability, cost and latency budgets, and kill switches, in place before anything reaches a customer.
  • The path to autonomy. What the system decides on its own, what still needs a person, and the evidence we need before we take that person out of the loop.
  • The roadmap. What gets built in what order, and why. You set priorities across the site, email, messaging, the CRM, and Sales handoffs, and work with Engineering on build-versus-buy decisions.
  • The outcome. Funnel velocity (time from first interest to high intent, and to purchase) and the measured lift in qualified actions and closed sales.

Two examples of the work:

  • An AI agent engages a new lead in the channel they prefer, qualifies them, and hands them to Sales at the right moment with the context Sales needs to close.
  • A customer reads an email, chats with us, and comes back to the site a week later. They get one continuous experience, because the system remembers what we've already said and done.

Who you are

  • Customer-obsessed. You start from the customer's experience, not the org chart or the backlog. When you have to choose between channels, surfaces, or features, the tiebreaker is what improves that experience. Our customers value clarity and discretion, and you design for both.
  • A systems thinker who still builds. You think at the system level, and you still do the hands-on work: prototypes, UI design, and prompts. You're expert at getting AI to do real work through prompting, tool use, and orchestration.
  • Technically deep. You can read a data model, question an integration design, reason about latency, cost, and failure modes, and be a credible partner to senior engineers as they make design decisions.
  • Rigorous about autonomy. You design systems to run on their own, and you know how to prove they're ready. Evals and guardrails go in before launch, not after an incident.
  • Accountable for outcomes. You measure yourself on results, not tasks shipped. You've stopped your own work when the impact wasn't there, and you can tell us about it.
  • Fluent in business and technical. You can frame and defend a tradeoff with Sales, Marketing, and leadership, then go deep with engineers on the build. You own the product and system decisions, and you can follow and shape the technical ones.
  • A multiplier. You raise the bar for how Product, Engineering, and Data build with AI, through your designs, your reviews, and the patterns you leave behind.
  • A partner. Marketing and Sales are core stakeholders, and you'll co-own the buyer journey with our product owner for new-lead acquisition. When the path to impact runs through another team's area, you work with the owner to move it.
  • Fast at context. You go deep on systems you didn't build and turn a lot of information into a plan quickly.

What you'll bring

We'll ask for specific evidence of each of these. If you can't point to all six, this probably isn't the right fit yet.

  1. Customer obsession. You take customer insights and translate them into real product features that deliver results.
  2. A production agentic system. You've designed and shipped an autonomous or agentic system that runs end to end with minimal human intervention. You can show us what it decides on its own and how you knew it was making the right calls before you trusted it with real customers.
  3. A measurable growth outcome. You've owned a growth, conversion, lifecycle, or re-engagement result. You can give us the baseline, what you changed, the lift, the time frame, and how you knew your work caused it.
  4. Decisioning and intelligence layers. You've designed signals, identity, scoring, context, eligibility and caps, or next-best-action logic.
  5. Prototype to production. You've built working prototypes yourself with AI tooling, beyond specs and slides, and taken at least one to production with engineers. You can tell us what you owned and what they owned.
  6. Cross-team system design. You've owned the system-level design for a product that multiple teams built on or integrated with, and shaped the technical design with the engineers who owned it.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with long-consideration, high-value purchases such as real estate, luxury, or financial services.
  • Experience putting AI into a human sales team's workflow, including CRM integration.
  • An earlier career as a software engineer, data architect, or solutions architect.

This role isn't for you if

  • You want to execute against a defined spec, or manage a backlog someone else shaped.
  • You want to manage a team right now. This is a principal IC role.
  • You want to own the technical architecture and implementation. Engineering owns those here.
  • You see this as an email or campaign program, or measure success in opens, clicks, or campaigns shipped.
  • Your AI experience is mostly using it to write docs and emails faster.
  • You need a full team and a clean data stack before you start. Some pieces exist today and don't talk to each other yet.

How we work

We start with AI. It's one of our core values. We design processes with automation and intelligence in mind from the start, and our product team already has AI agents talking to customers.

Small team, real ownership. Product at Pacaso works closely with Engineering, Design, Data, Sales, and Marketing. If you see a problem worth solving, you're trusted to solve it. We ship weekly and demo working software, not slides.

We move fast and play the long game. We make decisions and change course quickly. "Embrace an infinite mindset" is one of our values: a quarterly number is information, not a verdict, and we'd rather send nothing than send the wrong thing.

We pick up the phone and empty the dishwasher. When async isn't enough, we get on a call. No task is beneath anyone, and we keep bureaucracy to a minimum. We're a distributed Crew.

Compensation

  • Around $200,000- $225,000k depending on location and experience with equity (RSU's)

Why You'll Love Working Here

We invest in our Crew the way we invest in our homes — thoughtfully, generously, and with care.

  • Competitive base salary and meaningful equity — every Crew member shares in what we're building
  • Discretionary time off — take the rest you need, when you need it
  • Premium medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your family
  • Sponsored memberships to One Medical, Peloton, and WellHub for whole-person, modern healthcare
  • 401(k) to help you build long-term security
  • Paid parental leave for primary and secondary caregivers
  • Home office stipend and a monthly internet and cell phone reimbursement to set you up for great remote work
  • Quarterly team gatherings and ongoing learning and development investment

Our Commitment

Pacaso is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, ability, and background — including veterans and individuals with disabilities. We believe a Crew as diverse as the owners we serve makes Pacaso stronger, and we're committed to building a workplace where every voice belongs.

title: HRIS Data Conversion Analyst (UKG to Workday)
description:
At Connect Centric, we are more than just consultants—we are partners committed to our clients' success. We take a hands-on approach, working closely with our clients to transform strategies into measurable, real-world outcomes. As a strategy execution team, we take full ownership of every initiative from start to finish, ensuring that our clients see tangible results, not just ideas.

Position Description
Connect Centric is seeking an HRIS Data Conversion Analyst to provide subject matter expertise and hands-on support for the extraction, preparation, validation, conversion, and testing of Human Capital Management (HCM) data from UKG to Workday in support of our client’s Workday implementation.

You will partner with HR, finance, IT, and Workday implementation partners to support end-to-end data conversion activities, including data readiness, conversions, validation, and testing. You will also support routine UKG reporting throughout the implementation period.

What You Will Do
• Review existing UKG data structures, tables, and historical records used for Core HR, Recruiting, Benefits, and Talent data.
• Identify data quality risks, gaps, and dependencies early in the conversion process.
• Extract data from UKG using People Analytics reporting through IBM Cognos Analytics.
• Clean, standardize, and transform data to align with Workday data models and load requirements, applying business rules for data mapping and translation.
• Prepare the load-ready data templates required for Workday conversion.
• Develop and maintain detailed data mapping documents from UKG fields to Workday objects and fields.
• Document transformation logic, assumptions, exclusions, and data ownership, and support creation of a data dictionary.
• Support conversions and test loads into Workday tenants.
• Perform data validation and reconciliation between UKG and Workday, and prepare validation and reconciliation summaries.
• Identify and troubleshoot data load errors and exceptions; maintain issue logs and track conversion defects through resolution in partnership with functional leads.
• Support user acceptance testing by validating converted data against business expectations.
• Assist with final data loads and cutover planning, and provide post-load validation support during go-live readiness activities.
• Support ongoing scheduled and ad hoc reporting needs in UKG during the implementation period.
• Collaborate with functional and technical teams to identify, document, and manage reporting dependencies that may shift as reporting sources transition from UKG to Workday.

Required Qualifications
• Demonstrated experience with HR data conversions for Workday implementations.
• Hands-on experience extracting and preparing data from UKG Pro, including Core, Recruiting, Onboarding, and Learning.
• Strong understanding of UKG and Workday HCM data structures.
• Advanced Excel skills, including data validation, lookups, and transformation logic.
• Strong attention to detail and data accuracy.
• Ability to document complex data logic clearly for functional and technical stakeholders.
• Experience working in cross-functional implementation teams.
• Ability to manage multiple conversion activities under tight timelines.

Position Type: W2
Location: Fully Remote
Pay Rate: $115,000 - $125,000/per year
Must be permitted to work in the U.S. without sponsorship.

title: Electronics Project Leader III
description:
Job Description

Apply by November 24th

Power a world of ideas.

Curitiba-PR

At Electrolux Group, a leading global appliance company, we strive every day to shape living for the better for our consumers, our people and our planet. We share ideas and collaborate so that together, we can develop solutions that deliver enjoyable and sustainable living.

Come join us as you are. We believe diverse perspectives make us stronger and more innovative. In our global community of people from 100+ countries, we listen to each other, actively contribute and grow together.

Join us in our exciting quest to build the future home!

About the role:

For more than one hundred years now, the Electrolux Group has been working at shaping living for the better, developing products that meet people’s demands in terms of taste, care and wellbeing. But as consumer needs and wants continue to evolve, we have even more work to do. It's our R&D teams that ensure our company stays at the forefront of innovation, investigating and making use of the latest technology in order to enable our company to keep delivering outstanding experiences.

What you’ll do:

The Senior Electronics Project Leader drives the development of electronic systems in home appliance products, leading cross-functional teams – including system engineering, hardware, software and testing laboratories through design, development, testing, and production stages, ensuring high-performance, energy-efficient, and reliable consumer appliances hit the market on time and within budget. This role involves applying robust project management techniques to design and execute detailed plans, ensuring all technical and commercial goals are met within defined timelines and budgetary boundaries. Regular status updates will be provided to senior management to maintain visibility into progress, risks, and achievements throughout the product development cycle.

In detail, you will:

- Lead electronic module development and system integration projects from idea to market readiness using the Electrolux project development processes and tools.

- Collaborate with stakeholders to gather, analyze, refine and document business requirements for a project scope definition.

- Develop detailed project plans, including milestones, resource allocation, and risk mitigation strategies.

- Collaborate with Systems Engineering to translate customer insights and marketing needs into actionable technical specifications and project deliverables.

- Coordinate project deliverables and milestones with internal teams (Product Architecture, Labs, Product Line, Manufacturing, Quality, Purchasing) and external suppliers.

- Conduct cost analysis, pricing estimates, and feasibility studies to align with target product costs.

- Identify cost drivers and opportunities for optimization in processes, materials, or resources.

- Manage and report on schedule, cost, quality, and capital expenditure (CAPEX) KPIs at critical project checkpoints.

- Chair or participate in all key project meetings including design reviews, checkpoint gates, and periodic cross-functional team meetings.

- Ensures the timely preparation and execution of engineering project documentation (change notices, BOMs, drawings, specifications, etc).

As part of the culture of continuous improvement, you will be involved in Lean Thinking projects and activities (EMS/EAI).

Who you are:

- Bachelor of Science degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field.

- Minimum of five years of demonstrated experience in new product development with a demonstrated track record of launching successful and innovative products.

- Strong understanding of embedded systems, power electronics, and product lifecycle management.

- Understanding of digital product development lifecycles, connectivity systems (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, IoT, etc.), system updates over the air and cybersecurity.

- Familiarity with reading technical schematics and a solid grasp of embedded systems architecture is advantageous.

- Strong project management and interpersonal skills leading cross functional project teams.

- Advanced English

Where you’ll be:

You will be based at the Guabirotuba plant in Curitiba. One of the focal points for all Latin American Electrolux operations, this plant is the base for over 3200 collaborators, all focused on transforming the way the world lives by shaping lives for the better with their work.

In order to create a culture of inclusion and care for everyone's wellbeing, we offer the following benefits:

  • Flexible work hours/hybrid work environment (4x1);
  • Profit share bonus;
  • Discounts on our award-winning Electrolux products and services;
  • Family-friendly benefits such as extended paternity leave (4 weeks);
  • Insurance policy plan;
  • Extensive learning opportunities and flexible career path.

As part of Electrolux Group, we will continuously invest in you and your development. There are no barriers to where your career could take you.

Plan and coordinate complex executive travel arrangements, VIP meetings, leadership offsites, and other high-profile business engagements, including destination research, VIP protocols, ground transportation, and logistical execution.

  • Change Management & Influence: Demonstrated ability to lead change, influence stakeholders at all levels, and drive adoption of new travel policies, processes, and technologies.
  • Ownership & Problem-Solving: High degree of accountability and ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment while remaining a collaborative team player.
  • Language & Communication: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills and experience working with cross-cultural teams. Bilingual is a plus.
  • Flexibility: Willingness to work flexible hours across time zones as needed to support executive travel and global handoffs.
  • Discretion & Confidentiality: Demonstrated adherance to handle highly sensitive executive, business, and personal information with absolute discretion, professionalism, and sound judgment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Program Building Potential: A growth mindset with the vision and adaptability to move from hands-on execution to setting up a structured US corporate travel program.

title: Contract Hardware Senior Project Manager

Required Skills/Abilities:
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Excellent interpersonal and customer service skills.
  • Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Excellent time management skills with a proven ability to meet deadlines.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to prioritize tasks and to delegate them when appropriate.
  • Ability to function well in a high-paced environment.
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office Suite and Adobe.

Education and Experience:

description:

I further attest that all information I submit in my employment application is true to the best of my knowledge.

Job Description

About the role:

In this role, you will help shape the future of analytical technology across Takeda’s global Quality Control laboratories. You will play a key role in defining the long-term analytical technology strategy and multi-year roadmap, identifying emerging technologies that advance scientific innovation while supporting compliance, operational excellence, and business value.


Your work will contribute to building scalable, scientifically robust analytical capabilities that strengthen pharmaceutical quality and prepare laboratories for the future. You will partner across Quality, Manufacturing, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Research and Development, Regulatory, Engineering, Digital and Information Technology, Data Science, Procurement, and Supply Chain to advance innovation. You will also help connect Takeda with universities, technology providers, start-ups, and industry groups to identify emerging developments and strengthen analytical innovation across the organization.


How you will contribute:


  • Global analytical technology strategy & vision: Define and own the global analytical technology strategy and future technology vision for QC laboratories, aligned to Takeda’s quality, manufacturing, and business strategy. The role is not responsible for QC site adoption or routine laboratory operations associated with the analytical technology strategy.
  • Multi-year technology roadmap: Develop and maintain a multi-year analytical technology roadmap, sequencing innovation and deployment to keep the QC network at the scientific and digital frontier.
  • Technology scouting & horizon scanning: Lead global technology scouting, horizon scanning, and scientific trend analysis to identify emerging and disruptive analytical technologies and evaluate their applicability to Takeda.
  • Innovation pipeline & evaluation: Own the innovation pipeline — establishing technology-evaluation teams, proof-of-concept, and qualification pathways that move technologies from scouting to validated, deployable capability.
  • Advanced & digital laboratory technologies: Drive the evaluation and adoption of advanced analytical, AI-enabled, and digital laboratory technologies — automation, robotics, PAT, rapid microbiological methods, spectroscopy, imaging, advanced sensors, digital twins, predictive analytics, and connected, cloud-enabled smart-laboratory ecosystems.
  • Investment prioritisation & portfolio management: Prioritise technology investments and manage the innovation portfolio, developing robust business cases and quantifying return on investment and business value.
  • Technology governance, standardisation & lifecycle: Establish technology governance, standardise analytical technologies across the global network, and own technology lifecycle management from introduction through obsolescence.
  • Global deployment & transformation: Lead enterprise-wide technology transformation and Laboratory-of-the-Future programmes, ensuring scalable, compliant global deployment and realisation of targeted benefits.
  • Product lifecycle & new product introduction support: Support product lifecycle management and new product introductions with fit-for-future analytical technology capability.
  • External innovation & partnerships: Scout globally and build strategic partnerships with universities, technology suppliers, start-ups, and industry consortia; monitor regulatory expectations; and represent Takeda at scientific conferences and external forums.
  • Innovation capability building: Build innovation capability across the organisation, leading scientific communities of practice and embedding a culture of technology foresight and experimentation.
  • Leadership of global innovation programmes & teams: Lead global innovation programmes, cross-functional project teams, technology-evaluation teams, and strategic vendor relationships, managing complex stakeholder relationships across Quality, Manufacturing, Pharmaceutical Sciences, R&D, Regulatory, Engineering, Digital & IT, Data Science, Procurement, and Supply Chain.

Minimum Requirements/Qualifications:


  • Typically requires a minimum of 15+ years of pharma industry experience (quality, mfg, tech ops)
  • A minimum of 10 years of experience in leading teams (preferably global teams) is required
  • Science related degree is preferred
  • Relevant managerial experience required
  • Excellent communication, interpersonal and organizational skills.
  • Proven experience in implementing processes including building capabilities.
  • Proven experience in pharmaceutical manufacturing support and governance at a site level.
  • Knowledge and experience in bio-pharmaceutical technology.
  • Profound knowledge and experience with Quality Management and systems in a regulated industry.

title: Second Assistant Golf Professional
description:
Second Assistant Golf Professional.
Plantation Golf & Country Club | Venice, Florida.
Position: Second Assistant Golf Professional.
Department: Golf Operations.
Reports To: Director of Golf / Head Golf Professional.
Employment Type: Full-Time.

Position Summary:

Plantation Golf & Country Club is seeking a motivated, enthusiastic, and service-oriented Second Assistant Golf Professional to join our Golf Operations team.

This position plays an important role in delivering an exceptional golf experience to our membership while supporting the daily operations of our 36-hole private country club. The ideal candidate will demonstrate professionalism, strong communication skills, attention to detail, and a genuine passion for golf and member service.

The Second Assistant Golf Professional will assist with golf shop operations, tournament administration, member engagement, golf instruction, and the overall presentation and efficiency of the golf operation.

Key Responsibilities:

Golf Operations & Member Experience:
  • Deliver exceptional, personalized service to members and guests.
  • Assist in overseeing daily golf operations, ensuring a professional, organized, and welcoming environment.
  • Manage daily tee sheet operations, including reservations, cancellations, member requests, and coordination of play.
  • Monitor tee time availability, pace of play, and course utilization to enhance the member golf experience.
  • Support the outside golf operations team to ensure consistent service standards.
  • Assist with daily opening and closing procedures for the Golf Shop.
  • Maintain a professional presence throughout the Club and proactively engage with members.

Tournament & Event Management:
  • Assist in planning, coordinating, and executing member tournaments, leagues, outings, and special golf events.
  • Prepare tournament materials, pairings, scorecards, rules sheets, and results.
  • Utilize golf tournament software to manage registration, scoring, and event administration.
  • Coordinate with Golf Course Maintenance, Food & Beverage, and other departments to ensure successful events.
  • Support men's, women's, couples', and mixed golf programming.
  • Assist with tournament communications and post-event follow-up.

Golf Shop & Retail Operations:
  • Assist with daily Golf Shop operations, including merchandising, sales, and inventory management.
  • Provide knowledgeable assistance with golf equipment, apparel, and accessories.
  • Support merchandise displays, product presentation, and retail promotions.
  • Process member transactions accurately through the Club's point-of-sale system.
  • Assist with inventory counts, special orders, and maintaining an organized retail environment.

Golf Instruction & Player Development:
  • Provide individual and group golf instruction as assigned.
  • Assist with member clinics, junior golf programs, and player development initiatives.
  • Support instructional programming designed to encourage participation and enjoyment of the game.
  • Promote golf activities and help create opportunities for members of all skill levels to participate.

Teamwork & Professional Standards:
  • Assist in training and mentoring outside golf operations personnel.
  • Maintain consistent communication with the Golf Professional staff and other Club departments.
  • Ensure Club policies, dress code standards, and golf etiquette are communicated and consistently upheld.
  • Respond promptly and professionally to member questions, concerns, and requests.
  • Demonstrate ownership, accountability, and follow-through in all assigned responsibilities.
  • Support a positive team culture focused on hospitality, professionalism, and continuous improvement.

Qualifications:

  • Previous experience in golf operations at a private country club, resort, or comparable golf facility preferred.
  • PGA Associate status or active pursuit of PGA membership preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of the game of golf, rules, etiquette, and tournament operations.
  • Experience with tee sheet management, golf tournament software, and point-of-sale systems preferred.
  • Excellent interpersonal, communication, and organizational skills.
  • Strong commitment to member service and attention to detail.
  • Ability to multitask and perform effectively in a fast-paced golf environment.
  • Professional appearance, positive attitude, and willingness to take initiative.
  • Availability to work weekends, holidays, and flexible hours based on Club operations.

What We Are Looking For?

We are looking for an individual who understands that exceptional golf operations extend beyond managing tee times and tournaments. Our goal is to create memorable experiences, build relationships with our members, and consistently deliver the level of service expected at a premier private country club.

The successful candidate will be someone who takes pride in their work, anticipates member needs, supports their teammates, and looks for opportunities to enhance the overall golf experience.

About Plantation Golf & Country Club.

Located in Venice, Florida, Plantation Golf & Country Club is a private, 36-hole golf and country club featuring the Panther and Bobcat golf courses, extensive practice facilities, racquet sports, dining, fitness, and a vibrant membership community.

Managed by Concert Golf Partners, Plantation is committed to providing exceptional member experiences, maintaining outstanding facilities, and fostering a positive, professional team environment.

title: Process Designer
description:
Are you an experienced Process Designer who enjoys applying your technical knowledge to a variety of engineering projects? Encorus Group is looking for a knowledgeable Process Designer to join our growing Design team. You'll work closely with process engineers and project managers to develop process layouts, drawings, and design documentation from initial concepts through final deliverables.

If you're looking for an opportunity to put your process design experience to work, contribute to a collaborative team, and take on a variety of projects, we'd like to hear from you! A successful and qualified candidate can work from our Depew, NY, or Springville, NY, office.

Responsibilities
  • Responsible for developing, modifying, and coordinating process design drawings and documentation in support of engineering projects.
  • Serve as a technical resource to engineers and project managers by applying process design knowledge and experience to interpret engineering requirements and develop practical design solutions.
  • Work closely with engineering staff to understand project needs, anticipate design requirements, and identify potential design conflicts or improvements.
  • Coordinate design drawings and documentation across multiple engineering disciplines to ensure accuracy, consistency, and completeness.
  • Apply knowledge of applicable engineering codes, industry standards, and project specifications to support compliant design deliverables.
  • Manage multiple projects and assignments, working independently while maintaining established schedules, quality standards, and project requirements.
  • Follow established company drafting and design standards and assist in developing or improving procedures and practices as needed.
  • Provide technical guidance, mentorship, and support to other drafting and design staff.
  • Participate in field visits as needed to gather project information, verify existing conditions, and support design development.
  • Review design deliverables for accuracy, completeness, and coordination prior to submission.
  • Assist project managers and engineering staff with design development, project documentation, and other project-related responsibilities as assigned.
Qualifications
  • High school diploma required; associate degree in Design Technology, Drafting, or a related field preferred.
  • Minimum of 7 years of professional drafting experience, including at least 3 years in process design.

title: Seasonal Retail Stock - Pine Ridge Square Rack

Are you ready to thrive in a fast-paced, high-energy environment? As a Nordstrom Rack team member, you'll be continuously moving and collaborating with teammates to create a welcoming and inclusive atmosphere for all customers. You’ll ensure a quick and easy customer experience and keep the store clean and clutter free. Flexibility is key, as you may occasionally work in different areas of the store to maintain the cleanliness of the floor and stockrooms and help customers find great deals.

We have roles available in Sales, Customer Service, Stock, and Fulfillment departments. Apply now and discuss which role interests you most during the interview process.

A day in the life for Sales and Customer Service …

  • Prepare and ship customer’s orders following quality, packing and shipping standards
  • Utilize inventory management systems to scan, process and research merchandise shipments in accordance with our inventory control processes

  • Provide general support to the store, e.g. set up special events, organize backroom, markdowns, and relocate store fixtures

title: Team Leader - Sunshine Coast
description:
Join an Organisation dedicated to Closing the Gap in Indigenous Health

About Us?

The Institute for Urban Indigenous Health Ltd was established by its founding members to provide a coordinated/integrated approach to the planning, development and delivery of comprehensive primary health care services for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander populations within the Southeast Qld Region.


The focus of IUIH Aged Care team is to work with the local indigenous community and relevant key stakeholders to increase access to comprehensive care and provide well-coordinated, quality in home care services and eligible aged care clients.


About the Role?

As Team Leader Aged Care, your role is to in accordance with the clients’ assessed needs manage the contract relationship and arrangements with the Client/Carer and review ongoing service needs, coordinate a team of care workers in the delivery of the agreed suite of services ensuring quality, timeliness and effectiveness of service delivery. The role will be required to perform in accordance with Client Care plans, the Aged Care Standards and the IUIH Policies and Procedures.


Your day-to-day duties will include:


  • Liaise with the Assessor and Community Nurses to ascertain Client needs.
  • Identify a range of services that enhance inclusion for elderly Indigenous persons who are residing in their own homes within the community.
  • Collaborate with other service providers to ensure effective service delivery and increase community networks.
  • Coordinate and review service arrangements with Service Providers.
  • Assist in the planning, implementation, review and evaluation of programs.

About You?

  • Current C Class Drivers Licence (QLD)
  • Current Criminal History Check.
  • Current Disability Worker Screening Check (Qld Yellow Card).
  • Current First Aid and CPR Certificates

Desirable, but not mandatory:

  • Demonstrated experience working with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and /or communities

What Can we Offer?

At IUIH we recognise that we operate in a diverse community and welcome and encourage applications from all ages and genders, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, culturally and linguistically diverse groups, the LGBTIQ+ community, veterans, refugees, and people with disability.

  • At IUIH ‘Our Collectivity is Our Strength’.
  • We are a diverse and inclusive workplace that invites applications from all people.
  • Be part of Australia’s largest community controlled Aboriginal Health Service.
  • Access to “Growing Our Own Opportunities” through in-house training and programs.
  • Weekly Staff Wellness activities and all staff ‘Gather and Grow’ yarns and award ceremonies.
  • Opportunities to attend community events such as NAIDOC, Rugby League Carnivals and more.

Demonstrated commitment to creating culturally safe environments where children and young people are respected, heard, and protected against harm.

title: Retail Donation Attendant at Mason
description:
Ohio Valley Goodwill Industries, founded in 1916, is one of the largest providers of rehabilitation services in the State of Ohio. Utilizing our retail store network, we generate sales revenue to support thousands of individuals with disabilities and homeless local veterans.

The Donation Attendant provides excellent customer service to Ohio Valley Goodwill donors and customers inside and outside of retail locations. Greets donors, receives donations, and supplies donors with receipts. Prepares donations for the production processing area and works to efficiently expedite merchandise in a fast-paced environment.

As a member of Ohio Valley Goodwill you will be required to work a flexible schedule in support of the store opening, production, and closing operations. This schedule will include work on weekends and holidays.


Positions Needed:

1 Full-Time
