1. A minimum of six months of previous work experience, or the equivalent educational or vocational experience preferred.
2. Ability to provide exceptional customer service to all of our customers and donors.
3. Ability to understand English and interact with customers and employees.
4. Ability to effectively communicate verbally with associates and customers.
5. Ability to perform continuous walking, stooping, standing, bending, lifting, kneeling and climbing for prolonged periods of time.
6. Ability to lift 35 pounds frequently.
7. Ability to be trained and safely use big joe stacker and pallet jack (age 18 +).

1. Ability to motivate the team.
2. Previous experience working in a warehouse environment.
3. Previous pallet packing and forklift experience.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

4. Sort donated items into designated categories.
5. Comply with safety and security practices including reporting safety hazards and injuries to the Retail General Manager or Retail Assistant Manager or Retail Supervisor on duty.
6. Maintain a professional appearance adhering to Goodwill uniform standards.

8. Demonstrate ethical behavior and comply with Corporate Compliance.
9. Adhere to work schedule set by supervisor.

OTHER DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
1. Help truck drivers and their assistants load/unload donations into company vehicles for transport to/from other store locations.
2. Maintain a professional appearance adhering to Goodwill standards, including compliance with OVGI dress code.
3. Perform general housekeeping duties as needed including janitorial tasks such as cleaning restrooms or removing trash from the parking lot.
4. Communicate OVGI’s mission and vision effectively to our donors and customers.

This position has no supervisory responsibilities

title: Operations Intern
description:
David Zwirner has galleries in New York, Los Angeles, London, Paris, and Hong Kong, and represents more than eighty artists, estates, and foundations. Beyond its global exhibition program, the gallery is also active across publishing, print editions, podcasts, artist projects, and advisory services, offering team members exposure to the full breadth of its work.

Who will work well with us:

  • The ideal candidate is someone who is passionate and interested in the arts/larger creative arena or is eager to learn. Previous experience and a background within the commercial art world is not required.
  • We welcome all individuals entering the workforce, those moving into a new stage of their career or vocation, making a change, returning to work, and those wanting to learn and grow within the industry, to apply.

About the Opportunity

Operations Intern

David Zwirner is seeking an Operations Intern to work alongside our Operations team. Qualified candidates should be highly organized, responsible, and motivated, with an interest in gaining experience in the day-to-day functions of a professional office environment.

What you’ll do:

  • Mail Distribution: Receive, sort, and distribute incoming mail and packages to the appropriate departments and individuals.
  • Inventory Management: Monitor and restock office supplies. Track inventory levels and ensure that necessary items are ordered and maintained.
  • Kitchen Supplies: Manage the ordering, tracking, and restocking of food and beverages for shared kitchen areas. Ensure that kitchens are consistently stocked and organized.
  • Front Desk Support: Greet and assist visitors and staff as they enter the office. Direct guests to their destinations and provide a welcoming atmosphere at the front desk.
  • Administrative Support: Assist with various administrative tasks as needed to support the operations team.

What we would like you to have:

  • Organizational Abilities: Strong skills in managing and organizing tasks, with attention to detail in inventory tracking and mail distribution.

  • Customer Service: Ability to provide a positive and professional front desk experience, addressing inquiries and directing visitors appropriately.
  • Problem-Solving: Proactive in identifying and resolving issues related to office supplies, kitchen inventory, and general administrative tasks.
  • Technical Proficiency: Proficient in Google Suite and comfortable using office equipment (e.g., printers, phone systems).

The Winter/Spring internship runs from January through April. The hours are 10AM – 6PM, 2-3 days a week. To ensure that our interns have a well-rounded and educational experience, we ask for a commitment of at least 3 months, with the possibility of an extension into the next season. All interns are paid NYC minimum wage of $17/hour. All candidates must be residents of NY, NJ, or CT. No lodging or commuting expenses will be provided.

title: Area Supervisor
description:
Must apply on Ross Careers Website. Please apply at Ross--

In-Store position.
Welcome to Ross Stores, Inc., where our differences make us stronger… At Ross and dd’s, inclusion is a way of life. We care about our Associates and the communities we serve and we value their differences. We are committed to building diverse teams and an inclusive culture. We respect and celebrate the diversity of backgrounds, identities, and ideas of those who work and shop with us. Come join us as we continue our diversity, equality, and inclusion journey!

General Purpose:
The Area Supervisor is a member of the Store Leadership who is responsible for a specific, assigned area of the Store as well as the general operations and supervision of the Store when functioning as the Manager on Duty. Area Supervisors are responsible for opening and closing the Store, supervising Associates, and maintaining a friendly, easy-to-shop environment. They ensure proper merchandise presentation and maintain a clean work area at all times. Area Supervisors are also responsible for executing and supervising Company operational processes as needed.

Essential Functions:
Maintaining Safe & Secure Environments:
  • Understands that safety is the number one priority and practices safe behaviors in everything they do.
  • Maintains a high level of awareness on the sales floor to create a safe and secure shopping environment for everyone. Immediately corrects or reports any unsafe conditions or practices to Store Leadership.
  • Responsible for security of the building including entrance/exit control (Associate entry/egress, receiving door, daily trash removal, etc.), Electronic Article Surveillance (EAS) devices daily function check, Cash Office security, armored carrier pick-ups and register area.
  • Removes clutter and ensures safe, clear egress to emergency exits.
  • Responsible for Customer safety including accident prevention, accident reporting and emergency procedures.
  • Tests all fire alarm systems as scheduled. Responds to after-hours alarms when requested.

Customer Service:
  • Treats all Customers, Associates, and other leaders with respect.
  • Demonstrates courtesy, friendliness, and professionalism at all times. Recognizes Associates using Company recognition programs.

Personal and Store Brand:
  • Represents and supports the Company brand at all times.
  • Maintains a professional appearance, in accordance with Company Dress Code. Ensures all Associates adhere to the Company Dress Code at all times.
  • Keeps all areas of the Store clean, well-maintained, and merchandised to standard.
  • Responsible for daily trash removal.

General Merchandising:
  • Ensures recovery, sizing, and markdowns are completed to Company standards through teaching, assigning tasks, and following up per Company best practices.
  • Responsible for receiving merchandise trucks when needed.
  • Processes all merchandise with a sense of urgency.
  • Responsible for receipt of all non-merchandise inbound deliveries (i.e., signs, supplies, special deliveries, etc.).
  • Responsible for cleanliness and organization of all Stockrooms.
  • Helps deliver and place merchandise on the sales floor when all merchandise is processed.
  • Responsible for ensuring any back-stock is secured and processed to Company policy.
  • Responsible for merchandising of the department including the back stock.
  • Responsible for the reduction of loss due to damage.
  • Ensures compliance to the monthly presentation guidelines in the assigned area.
  • Responsible for floor moves and signing including promotional signing as needed.
  • Responsible for re-wraps as needed.

Loss Prevention:
  • Understands and complies with the Loss Prevention Awareness Program and is responsible for Store Loss Prevention which includes maintaining a large Customer service presence on the sales floor, Customer and Associate engagement, and heightened Loss Prevention awareness.
  • As a representative of Ross Leadership demonstrates integrity and honesty in all interactions with Associates and Customers. Safeguards confidential information, cash and credit card information, and merchandise.
  • Ensures Public View Monitor (PVM) system is maintained properly.
  • Conducts "Code 50" package inspections.
  • Executes all Company Best Practices and maximizes productivity by minimizing steps and touches while working.

Front-End Supervision and Operations:
  • Executes all Company Best Practices and maximizes productivity by minimizing steps and extra touches when working. Ensures Associates are executing to Company standards at the Front End.
  • Maintains pace, energy, and "presence" at the Front End, managing the line to expedite Customers' wait time.
  • Trains and coaches Associates on cash registers, shortage control policies, and other Front End procedures. To meet friendly and productivity standards.
  • Controls Retail Associates' break schedule for backups, lunches, and breaks.
  • Ensures all equipment is working properly.
  • Maintains proper supplies and recovery for the Front End area.
  • Ensures go-backs are expedited, properly scanned, security tagged, and ticketed.
  • Teaches all Associates the "Scan and Bag" best practice.
  • Ensures salability of merchandise on the Front End, aisle tables, Men's/Women's 4-way features, and specialty racks.

Fitting Rooms:
  • Responsible for the maintenance and cleanliness of the Fitting Rooms.
  • Ensures all Fitting Room garment tags are audited and accounted for to Company policy.
  • Ensures go-back compliance throughout the day. All merchandise returned to the sales floor must be ticketed, scanned, nubbed and security tagged as needed.

Administrative Duties as Assigned by Store Manager:
  • Ensures Cash pulls and bank deposits are conducted to Company policy.
  • Responsible for Front End control when needed. Understands and adheres to the policies and procedures that refer to refund approval, Associate purchase approval, securing tills and cash in safe, registering Paid Outs/Ins, void approval, registering media and break schedules.
  • Responsible for payroll administration including daily punch edits, Associate scheduling compliance, Sunday payroll transmission, and Payroll reporting as needed.
  • Other duties as assigned by the Store Manager.

Competencies:
  • Manages Work Processes.
  • Business Acumen.
  • Plans, Aligns & Prioritizes.
  • Builds Talent.
  • Collaborates.
  • Leading by Example.
  • Communicates Effectively.
  • Ensures Accountability & Execution.

Qualifications and Special Skills Required:
  • Excellent verbal communication skills.
  • Fluency in English.
  • Prior Customer Service and supervisory experience preferred.
  • Familiarity with point-of-sale equipment and applications.
  • Ability to perform basic mathematical calculations commonly used in retail environments.
  • Ability to work evenings and weekends.

Physical Requirements/ADA:
  • Ability to use all Store equipment, including PDTs, registers and PC as required.
  • Ability to spend up to 100% of working time standing, walking, and moving around the Store.
  • Ability to regularly bend at the waist, squat, kneel, climb, carry, reach, and stoop.

title: Sanitation Manager
description:
About CookUnity:

Food has lost its soul to modern convenience. And with it, it has lost the power to nourish, inspire, and connect us. So in 2018, CookUnity was founded as the first-of-its-kind platform that connects the world with the source of truly great food: chefs. Today, CookUnity delivers 50 million meals a year from the industry’s best chefs to homes all over the country. Fresh. Ready-to-eat. And crafted with the passion that nourishes body and soul.

Unwilling to stop there, CookUnity is expanding beyond delivery to become an ever-innovating marketplace focused on our singular mission: empower Chefs to nourish the world.

If that mission has you hungry in more ways than one, you’ve found the right job posting.

About the Team:

Our Food Safety & Quality Assurance (FSQA) and Operations teams are dedicated to upholding the highest standards of cleanliness and safety across CookUnity’s facilities. The Sanitation Manager will be an integral part of this effort, working hands-on with hourly teams on the ground to ensure compliance, accountability, and excellence every day.The role:

We seek a proactive and detail-oriented Sanitation Manager to lead sanitation operations at our New York facility. This is a full-time, on-site position responsible for managing a large hourly workforce (80+ direct reports) across multiple shifts.

The Sanitation Manager will ensure food safety, cleanliness, and compliance with regulatory requirements while fostering a culture of accountability, teamwork, and continuous improvement. The Sanitation Manager will manage the daily tasks performance of our dish and cleaning teams.

This role requires flexibility to be present on-site during weekdays, weekends, and occasionally night/overnight shifts, depending on operational needs.

Responsibilities:

  • Oversee and lead all personnel devoted to sanitation activities, ensuring adherence to master sanitation schedules, SSOPs, GMPs, and HACCP.
  • Serve as the primary operational contact for 3rd-party cleaning services and manage vendor relationships including chemical provider and linen service.
  • Collaborate with FSQA to enhance program and procedures, taking the lead on implementation.
  • Manage Sanitation staffing, schedules, time keeping and performance evaluations
  • Monitor and enforce compliance with regulatory standards for cleanliness, hygiene, and safety across all production areas and equipment.
  • Lead on implementation of sanitation corrective actions assigned through audits, pest deficiency reports, inspections or program improvements.
  • Collaborate with FSQA and Operations teams to maintain and improve food safety and quality standards.
  • Collaborate with maintenance to coordinate deep cleans, emergency clean ups and sanitation preventive maintenance.
  • Manage chemical usage, storage and safety in accordance with OSHA and manufacturer guidelines.
  • Provide sanitary expertise on operation, cleaning and light maintenance of dish washing machines, floor scrubbing machines and other equipment.
  • Maintain accurate records of sanitation procedures and cleaning logs
  • Ensure compliance with applicable regulations and company-specific food safety protocols

Qualifications:

  • 3 - 5 years of Sanitation leadership experience in a food processing environment
  • Bilingual in English and Spanish.
  • Strong knowledge of food processing sanitation standards in FDA/USDA regulated facilities, and knowledge of GMP, SSOP & HACCP
  • Proven leadership and team management skills.
  • Must be available to work weekends, nights, and across multiple shifts as required by facility operations.
  • Positive, driven, solution-oriented mindset.
  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Excellent communication, problem-solving, and organizational abilities.
  • Comfortable working in wet, cold/hot, and potentially noisy conditions for extended periods.
  • Flexibility to manage personnel as needed across three shifts, including overnights and weekends

Benefits

🩺 Health Insurance coverage

🌅 401k Plan

📈 We grow, you grow: Stock Options Plan granted on Day 1

🌟 Eligible for a bi-annual performance bonus

⛱ PTO policy and paid sick days

🗓️ 5- year Sabbatical: After 5 years with CookUnity, you get a 4-week paid sabbatical

🐣 Paid Family leave

🕯 Compassionate Leave: 3-5 days each time the need arises

🥘 A generous amount of CookUnity credits to enjoy our amazing meals, added to your account, monthly

🧘🏽‍♀️ Wellness perks: access to a nutritional coach and fitness subsidies to build a healthy lifestyle

👩🏾‍🏫 Personalized Spanish coach

🌟 Awesome opportunity to join a company that is looking to change how we eat and how chefs work!

Compensation

All final pay rates will be determined by candidates experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities of the applicant, internal equity, and alignment with market data.
Pay Range for this position
$86,000—$100,000 USD

If you’re interested in this role, please submit your application, and if we think you might be a fit, we'll get in touch with you. Thank you for your time!

CookUnity is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are dedicated to creating a community of inclusion and an environment free from discrimination or harassment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, citizenship status, protected veteran status, genetic information, or physical or mental disability.

A quick note for all candidates
We’ve recently seen an increase in recruitment scams across the industry, and we want to make sure you (and your data) stay safe while applying to CookUnity. We also want you to know that we take this seriously — sometimes, as part of our process, we may ask for a brief “proof of humanity” to confirm that we’re connecting with a real person, not an impersonator. Here are a few tips to help you protect yourself and know what to expect from us:

  • Apply only through our official channels. All open roles are listed on our official careers page:
  • Our recruiters are real people — and easy to verify. You can always find them on LinkedIn with verified profiles. If you’re unsure, feel free to reach out to us on our official LinkedIn Company Page.
  • We only communicate through official CookUnity channels. That means emails ending in @cookunity.com and interviews held through official company platforms (Google Meet or Zoom) — never WhatsApp, Telegram, or SMS.
  • We’ll never ask for payment or personal financial details. If anyone does, please don’t share any information and let us know right away.

If something ever feels off or you’re unsure about a message, we’d much rather you double-check with us. You can always contact us directly through any of our social media channels. We appreciate your interest in joining CookUnity — and we care about keeping your experience (and safety) as genuine as possible.

title: Kitchen Aide | School | Clementi
description:
A. Training/Induction by NFS Teachers

Use and general maintenance of the cookers / ovens / grill / microwave ovens / refrigerators.

Use and general maintenance of small kitchen appliances, such as blenders, cake mixers, food processors, electric steamers, etc.

Use and general maintenance of washing machine.

Kitchen terminology and familiarisation with common utensils, such as palette knives, patty tins, vegetable peelers, etc.

Food preparation, quantity and portioning for practical lessons.

Kitchen and food hygiene (includes proper food handling and storage).

Kitchen safety (handling electrical appliances and sharp objects and keeping them safe).

Provide updates of perishables and dry goods to teachers ordering for the classes.

Provide updates of kitchen utensils of each unit and main storage areas to teachers.

B. Daily Duties

For Practical Lessons and Examinations:

General cleaning of kitchens including cleaning tabletops, sinks, cookers, sweeping and mopping the floor and emptying dustbins.

General cleaning of NFS classrooms including cleaning desks, sweeping and mopping the floor and emptying dustbins.

Refill washing detergent, and check and ensure all equipment is in place for each work bench.

Teachers to brief the week’s practical and recipe with sample of layout given so that the kitchen helper can start preparations for the classes.

Preparation of food trays must be done before the lesson, at least half an hour beforehand.

Assist teachers during lessons, help to replenish items, clear teachers’ centre tables, assist students with cookers/ovens/grill/blenders/steamers, mop spills etc.

After lessons, kitchen helper to help clean up and store food properly. Any leftover ingredients that are still fresh and safe to use can be kept for use in other classes. Prepare food trays for next lesson if needed.

After lessons, check that all gas taps are turned off and cookers are switched off, cookers and sinks are clean, rubbish is disposed of, and clear/clean the centre store table.

Laundry for kitchen towels/aprons: Wash them in the washing machine and dry them on the rack. Once they are dry, fold them and place on the laundry shelf.

Track and record any breakages.

Arrange tables and chairs neatly in classrooms.

Check all lights, fans and air-conditioner are switched off in all rooms.

Assist teachers in any other duties assigned.

C. Weekly Duties (Preferably at the end of the week):

Thoroughly clean the cookers and ovens.

Thoroughly clean and clear any chokes in sinks.

Clear refrigerators of unwanted/spoilt ingredients and clean/sanitise refrigerators with baking soda solution.

Clear and clean centre store tables in both kitchens.

Check supply of washing detergents, aluminium foil, polythene film wrap, etc and inform teachers if they need to replenish.

Mop the floor of both kitchens and NFS classrooms.

Inform teachers if any utensils or equipment are spoilt or damaged.

Ensure teachers’ preparatory room is swept and mopped, and furniture is wiped clean.

D. Prior to School Holiday Duties:

Before the start of each term holiday, check:

a. left-over ingredients in the refrigerator are used up, given away or disposed of;

b. teachers’ work benches are clean and all equipment kept properly;

c. students’ work benches are clean and all equipment with correct quantity in each work bench. If there are any missing equipment, make a written list and inform the teachers;

d. all food at the store table are kept in the refrigerator where possible;

e. cookers, ovens, grills and sinks are thoroughly cleaned;

f. taps, electrical points and gas mains are turned off;

g. all empty delivery boxes are disposed of;

h. kitchens and classrooms are mopped with bleach to sanitise them; and

i. ensure teachers’ preparatory room is swept and mopped, and furniture is wiped clean.

Cover all cooker tops with newspaper and masking tape after cleaning.

Take out all cutlery, crockery and equipment from cupboards and wash and dry. Clean inside cupboards and shelves before putting back the equipment.

Wipe shelves of centre store tables clean.

Help with stock take and update records where equipment is kept. Start with the list in order and tick against each item in pencil. State the quantity as well.

Check with the teachers if unsure.

title: Specification Sales Engineer
description:
IPEX is one of the North American leading providers of advanced plastic piping systems. Our mission is to shape a better tomorrow by connecting people with water and energy.


We currently have an exciting opportunity as a Specification Sales Engineer! This role will report to the Applications Engineering Manager and cover the Eastern US territory which includes the following States: North Carolina; South Carolina; Virginia; West Virginia; Maryland; Delaware; New Jersey; Pennsylvania; New York; Connecticut; Vermont; New Hampshire; Rhode Island; Massachusetts; and Main.


Do not miss the opportunity to join a diverse group of people-centric professionals, thought leaders and rapid thinkers, entrepreneurs in spirit and status quo-fighters!

Job Summary


The Specification Sales Engineer serves as a technical sales and market development professional responsible for driving the specification, acceptance, and adoption of IPEX industrial, plumbing, and mechanical piping systems throughout the United States. The Specification Sales Engineer will serve as a trusted technical resource and partner with consulting engineers, design firms, contractors, and distributors, to influence project design decisions and secure specification positions, that drive long-term business growth.


Leveraging strong technical expertise and relationship-building skills, the Specification Sales Engineer will position IPEX as the preferred thermoplastic piping solutions provider while creating demand, generating project opportunities, and supporting strategic growth initiatives across key vertical markets, including infrastructure and data centers.

This position will require regular travel up to 50% within the United States to meet with Customers.


Principal Responsibilities

  • Drive specification development and secure inclusion of IPEX products and systems within project specifications, engineering standards, and owner design guidelines.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with consulting engineers, engineering firms, architects, contractors, OEMs, and distributors to influence project design decisions and promote IPEX solutions.
  • Identify, develop, and manage specification opportunities from concept through project award, creating a pipeline of future business opportunities.
  • Collaborate with engineering consultants, contractors, distributors, and hyperscale customers to drive product adoption, gain specification preference, and increase market share.
  • Promote IPEX solutions within strategic growth markets, including mission-critical facilities, data centers, water infrastructure, industrial processing, healthcare and mechanical systems.
  • Conduct lunch-and-learn presentations, technical seminars, continuing education programs, and product training sessions to educate industry stakeholders and increase specification activity.
  • Provide technical consultation during project design and specification development to ensure proper system selection and application of IPEX products.
  • Support the development of owner standards, master specifications, basis-of-design specifications, and approved manufacturer lists.
  • Obtain and maintain product approvals, listings, and acceptance with engineering firms, and key end users.
  • Act as the technical and commercial liaison between consultants, owners, sales teams, and internal stakeholders to ensure opportunities are effectively developed and transitioned to sales execution.
  • Work closely with Sales, Marketing, Product Management, Engineering, Innovation, R&D, and Operations teams to support market growth initiatives and strategic business objectives.
  • Monitor market activity, construction trends, engineering standards, building codes, and competitive solutions to identify growth opportunities and emerging specification trends.
  • Represent IPEX at industry associations, engineering organizations, trade shows, conferences, and customer events to strengthen market presence and technical leadership.
  • Develop and maintain technical resources, specification tools, application guides, engineering content, and educational materials that support specification growth.
  • Track and measure specification activity, project influence, design wins, and opportunity conversion to support business planning and growth objectives.
  • Provide advanced technical expertise and support for strategic projects and key accounts where specification influence is critical to project success.
  • Provide technical field support to contractors and owners, including installation training, application guidance, and troubleshooting assistance to ensure successful project execution
  • Act as the primary liaison between Sales, Customer Service, Quality, and end users to investigate product complaints, coordinate resolution activities, and communicate findings through formal customer reports.
  • Support engineer and contractor technical inquiries while identifying and developing specification opportunities to drive future project growth.


Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, P. Eng required in certain locations
  • Minimum of 2 years of relevant industry experience, preferably within technical sales, applications engineering, construction products, piping systems, mechanical systems, or related industries
  • Experience in data centers is a plus
  • Strong communication and presentation skills with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear, customer-focused solutions
  • Customer-focused mindset with excellent problem-solving and interpersonal skills
  • Self-motivated and capable of working independently while contributing effectively within a collaborative team environment
  • Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities
  • Willingness and ability to travel up to 50% throughout the United States

title: VP of Operations
description:
The role

You own how work gets scoped, staffed, and run at Movers+Shakers. That means four things: resourcing, the PMO, how we build our scopes, and the workflow our content moves through.

Movers+Shakers is a social-first creative agency tracking to grow revenue more than 50% in 2027. The work we do is strong and demand is high. What we are missing is an operator with a bird's-eye view of capacity, staffing, and margin, who sees problems 90 days out instead of the week they land.

This is a hands-on seat. You will lead the project managers and the resourcing team, and you will also be deep in the work itself… building scopes, reworking staffing plans, and standing up new client teams. We are not looking for someone to design an operating model from scratch. The foundations exist: we run on EOS, we have a PM team, a resourcing function, and a finance practice. Your job is to connect these pieces as one system and tighten what is loose.

  • Reports to: Our Integrator
  • Team: You will sit on our executive leadership team
  • Leads: the Director of Project Management and the PM team, and the Associate Director of Resourcing
  • Peers: Business Partnership (aka Account), Integrated Production, Creative, Finance, People, AI Leadership

What you'll own

1. Resourcing and capacity

  • Lead the resourcing team and own who is staffed on what, across full-time staff and freelancers.
  • Maintain a rolling 90-day capacity view of the agency, tied to the revenue forecast and the new business pipeline.
  • Turn our revenue goals and projections into hiring requests early enough that we can recruit ahead of need (3-6 month time horizon).
  • Make the calls on full-time versus freelance, with the margin impact visible.

2. The PMO

  • Lead and develop our project managers.
  • Hold one standard for how projects are planned, tracked, and reported, so any leader can see the health of any workstream.
  • PMs own the project from kickoff to close-out. Integrated Production owns the production; your team owns the plan, the timeline, the budget, and the contribution margin planning.

3. Delivery Economics

  • Strong partner to Finance to manage and execute on contribution margin targets for each Pod
  • Run the scope-to-actuals learning loop: what we sold, the hours we delivered, and how we scope differently next time.
  • Call it early when a workstream is over-servicing or under-staffed, and work the fix with the pod lead.
  • Interpret, communicate, and provide actionable insights on the agency-wide view of contribution margin, resource capacity and P&L supported hiring plans to the Integrator

4. Scoping & team building

  • You are the owner of how we build scopes: the staffing model, and the hours behind every new and existing scope, renewal, and pitch.
  • Finance is your counterpart. You build the scope; together you make sure it ties to the rate card, margin goals, and the revenue forecast.
  • Give the capacity and margin read on each new business opportunity before we decide to pursue it.
  • Stand up the team for a new client win quickly, without pulling the floor out from under existing clients.

5. Workflow, tools, and the content supply chain

  • Lead and champion the rollout of our content supply chain and Workfront integration: the connected AI-enabled workflow that moves content from brief to approval to publish.
  • Partner with our head of Innovation and Technology on every technology and AI rollout. They choose and build the tools; you make them part of how each team works day to day.
  • Bring them the operational problems worth solving with AI, and report back on what is actually being used.
  • Own adoption of agency-wide workflow and project tools, and retire duplicate tools and manual steps as the new workflow takes hold.

What success looks like

In your first 90 days

  • The rolling 90-day capacity view is live and leadership uses it to decide which new business to pursue.
  • Every active workstream has a current staff plan, and every pod lead has a margin view they trust.
  • The PMO works from one project standard.

In your first year

  • No surprise hiring: roles are requested from the forecast, months ahead of need.
  • Every scope is built one way, and we can explain every gap between what we scoped and what we delivered.
  • The content supply chain runs across all retainer clients.
  • A new client team goes from signed scope to staffed and running in weeks.

Who you are

  • 12+ years in agency operations, project management, or resourcing, in creative, social, or content agencies.
  • You have run a PMO and a resourcing function at the same time, at an agency of 50 to 200 people that was growing fast.
  • You have helped client leads move workstream margin, and you can tell us the number before and after.
  • You build scopes and staff plans yourself. You are fluent in rate cards, utilization, and the full-time versus freelance trade-off.
  • You have rolled out a workflow or project platform across an agency and can show the adoption numbers.
  • You manage managers and still are deep in the work. Senior enough to lead the function, not too senior to live & breathe the spreadsheets.
  • You use AI tools extensively in your own daily work and have a view on how they change agency workflow.
  • You say the hard thing early, with the data, and you bring the joy while doing it.
  • EOS experience is a plus.

title: Google Apps Engineer
description:
Job Title: Google Apps Engineer

Experience Requirement:

  • 7 years of software/application engineering experience with at least 3 years developing solutions using Google Cloud and/or Google Workspace technologies.
  • Must demonstrate proficiency with Google Workspace APIs, Apps Script, JavaScript/TypeScript, REST, OAuth 2.0, IAM, Google Cloud services, enterprise integrations, Git and CI/CD​​

Certification & Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent combination of education, professional training, certifications, and relevant technical experience.
  • Google Cloud Professional Cloud Developer certification required.

Project Background:
The IT Compliance organization, Compliance Operations, Legal Systems Section, supports the Office of Chief Counsel (OCC), is the chief legal officer of the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and serves as counsel and legal advisor to the IRS Commissioner on all matters pertaining to the administration and enforcement of the Internal Revenue laws and related statutes, as well as non-tax legal questions. The IT Enterprise Operations Group (EOPS) and User and Network Services (UNS) teams operate and maintain a nationwide technical infrastructure in support of the OCC’s mission- critical automation activities.

The scope of this support effort for the Office of Chief Counsel systems and components, also referred to as the Counsel Automated Legal Systems - CALS:

  • Counsel Automated Systems Environment Management Information System (CASE-MIS).
  • Chief Counsel Macros (CCMACROS).
  • Chief Counsel Check (CCACHECK).
  • Electronic Tax Court Services (eTCS).
  • Electronic Word (eWord).
  • electronic Counsel Inventory Tracking Environment (eCITE).
  • Intelligent Document Management System (IDMS).

For each of the applications outlined above as part of the CALS project, the support team will collaborate with the CALS government team, IT partners, Business Systems Planning (BSP), and Chief Counsel end users to provide application maintenance and change request support.

This includes the following for each application:

  • Break-fix: Analyze, remediate, test, and support deployment of any application Production defects.
  • IT Mandates: Support hardware and software upgrades as dictated by IT to remain in compliance, including Product upgrades of Oracle, Windows, Linux, Documentum, and .NET. This also includes application/platform modernization efforts deemed necessary by IT and Chief Counsel constituents.
  • Tax Reform Updates: Support software upgrades, including design, development, and testing, in support of any mandated tax law or tax code changes. Several changes are initiated annually by US Tax Court and require updates to the eTCS application.
  • Technical Lead: Collaborate with the CALS Government management team to provide support in the following areas: scheduling, Scrum Master activities, One Software Development Life Cycle OneSDLC activities including annual milestone reviews, and Agile, DevOps, and CI/CD methodology and tool adoption.
  • Risk Management: Collaborate with the CALS Government management team to review, prioritize, remediate, and mitigate and project risks. Document and support, as needed, any required Risk Based Decisions (RBDs).
  • Security Management: Collaborate with the CALS Government team and BSP Security Program Management Officer (SPMO) to review monthly security audit scans, prioritize findings, and work with the appropriate IT partners to remediate and validate the fixes.

As a world leader in creating comfortable, sustainable, and efficient climate solutions for buildings, homes and transportation, it's our responsibility to put the planet first. For us at Trane Technologies, and through our businesses including Trane® and Thermo King, sustainability is not just how we do business—it is our business. Do you dare to look at the world's challenges and see impactful possibilities? Do you want to contribute to making a better future? description:
Program Manager
About Richardson
Richardson Sales Performance helps global B2B revenue teams Sell Forward. We equip sellers and managers with the capabilities that move buyers to confident decisions, built on consultative selling, which we brought to market in 1978, and the insight-led Challenger sales methodology. More than 100 facilitators worldwide have trained two million sellers in 50 countries and over 23 languages.

Most sales training fades once the event ends, so we treat training as the start. Sellers keep practicing in the flow of work, and managers get a practical system to coach what was learned. Our AI-powered tools reinforce priority behaviors and show leaders what is actually changing in real opportunities. The same care we put into our clients’ growth shapes how we develop our own people, and it has made Richardson a place where strong careers take off.

The Program Manager is responsible for implementing Richardson's products and services for clients and serves as a critical business contact for the client and internal team during implementation. title: Major Gifts Officer
description:
Working at Moffitt is both a career and a mission: to contribute to the prevention and cure of cancer.

As the only National Cancer Institute-designated Comprehensive Cancer Center based in Florida, Moffitt employs some of the best and brightest minds from around the world. Join a dedicated team of nearly 11,000 who are shaping the future we envision. Moffitt has been recognized as a Best and Brightest Company to Work For in the Nation and is continually named one of the Tampa Bay Times’ Top Workplaces.

Summary

The Major Gifts Officer (MGO) will play a critical fundraising role in the Individual and Family Giving program, successfully managing their own portfolio of individual donors and prospects. This work will ultimately lead to an increase in the MGO’s year-over-year individual attainment, thereby increasing the collective dollars raised by the Individual and Family Giving Team. The MGO will be responsible for developing and maintaining a strong, multi-year roadmap of solicitations, supported by a robust pipeline, by focusing on effective qualification and cultivation strategies. This will enable accurate financial forecasting of the Foundation’s goals at both mid-level and major gift levels.The Major Gifts Officer will work across the specific disease sites at Moffitt in collaboration with Senior Major Gifts Officers assigned as liaisons to those disease areas. In addition, the MGO will build a broad understanding of disease site priorities and institutional fundraising priorities to support the growth of the grateful patient fundraising program and maximize the overall philanthropic revenue. The MGO will also support the Director and AVP in the development and execution of strategies and accompanying tactics, including portfolio development and the use of advanced donor analytics in advance donor base growth and engagement.


What You'll Do

  • Build meaningful donor relationships. Manage an assigned portfolio of major gift prospects and donors, developing individualized strategies that deepen engagement and philanthropic support above and beyond $1M.
  • Drive philanthropic growth. Build a robust pipeline, prepare and present major gift solicitations, and consistently move qualified prospects through the fundraising cycle.
  • Connect donors to Moffitt's mission. Develop a broad understanding of disease-specific and institutional priorities and help donors identify opportunities that align their passions with Moffitt's greatest needs.
  • Partner across Moffitt. Collaborate with physicians, researchers, clinical leaders, Senior Major Gifts Officers and Foundation colleagues to identify and advance philanthropic opportunities.
  • Support Moffitt's future. Help build philanthropic support for Moffitt's continued growth and expansion, including priorities connected with Speros and Moffitt's expanding locations and services.
  • Deliver exceptional stewardship. Create meaningful engagement experiences, facilitate connections between donors and institutional leaders, and ensure thoughtful, timely follow-up.
  • Use data strategically. Monitor portfolio and pipeline activity, leverage donor analytics, and adjust strategies to strengthen donor engagement, forecasting and fundraising outcomes.
  • Deliver results. Work closely with Foundation leadership to achieve annual and multi-year fundraising goals and performance measures.

The Ideal Candidate

You are a strategic fundraiser who knows that major gift philanthropy is about more than securing a contribution. It's about understanding what matters to a donor, earning trust, and connecting that passion to an opportunity capable of making a meaningful difference.

You'll bring demonstrated success managing donor relationships and closing significant gifts, along with the confidence and diplomacy needed to partner with senior leaders, physicians, researchers, prospects and other key stakeholders. You are equally comfortable developing a long-term donor strategy, analyzing your pipeline, preparing a solicitation and engaging with a donor one-on-one.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in a relevant field.
  • Minimum of six (6) years of professional experience working with nonprofit or development-related teams in areas such as fundraising, prospect management, donor relations, gift administration, research, or other revenue-generating activities.
  • Experience must include at least four (4) years of frontline fundraising.
  • Demonstrated ability to successfully close five- and six-figure gifts.
  • Proven success identifying, qualifying, cultivating, soliciting and closing gifts.
  • Strong understanding of the full fundraising cycle and experience managing a large, dynamic portfolio of prospects at different stages.
  • Excellent planning, goal-setting, written and verbal communication, relationship-building and collaboration skills.
  • Experience interacting effectively with senior executives, major gift prospects and other high-level stakeholders.
  • Experience with fundraising databases, CRM systems or similar donor-management technology.

Preferred Experience

  • Six years of frontline fundraising experience within a healthcare organization or higher education environment.

Experience

title: Sr. Manager, Advanced Manufacturing Engineering
description:
MicroAire Surgical Instruments LLC

As a part of the global industrial organization Marmon Holdings—which is backed by Berkshire Hathaway—you’ll be doing things that matter, leading at every level, and winning a better way. We’re committed to making a positive impact on the world, providing you with diverse learning and working opportunities, and fostering a culture where everyone’s empowered to be their best.

Leads Advanced Manufacturing initiatives across supply chain, sustaining engineering, manufacturing engineering, and process development for existing and new mechanical and electromechanical products. Serves as a technical advisor in researching and implementing manufacturing technology and is responsible for assigned elements of new product development under MicroAire Design Controls Procedures. Manages the technical and personnel aspects of facilities maintenance and provides technical leadership in areas critical to MicroAire’s success.

+ Essential Duties and Responsibilities


• Drives the planning and execution of critical Advanced Manufacturing projects for insourcing, automation, and continuous improvement, including cost savings, delivery, and quality.

• Leads or coaches critical continuous improvement, Lean, kaizen, and Blue Belt projects. Coordinates corporate CI tracking and planning, drives the site CI calendar, and tracks and reports savings.

• Supports Supply Chain in the technical aspects of insourcing, alternative sourcing, supplier quality, and supplier continuous improvement. Supports business initiatives such as repairs and service programs.

• Participates and makes recommendations regarding departmental quarterly plans and performs all essential duties and responsibilities within the company’s mission, vision and values.

• Develops career paths for direct reports.

• Provides guidance to manufacturing engineering for new highly critical products and oversees facilities maintenance activities within cross-functional teams consistent with departmental goals and objectives.

• Oversees Engineering activity around investigation and root cause analysis for failures observed in the field that needs Engineering support.

• Serves as the specialized technical expert resource for all project teams for manufacturing engineering projects.

• Provides leadership by taking initiative for existing product modifications.

• Provides guidance on Design For Manufacturing during New Product Development process.

• Interfaces with all departments within the company as well as consultants, vendors, surgeons, and others as required to ensure quality, efficacy, and timely completion of directed projects.

• Proactively works with team members to achieve established goals, budgets and timelines.

• Monitors department budgets closely and takes all necessary actions to ensure budget alignment. Identifies capital needs for production and facilities to provide CapEx recommendations.

• Collaborates with department heads to develop and update engineering standard operating procedures.

• Ensures project compliance with all applicable laws and regulations, especially U.S. FDA regulations and EU Medical Device Regulation supporting Regulatory group.

• Researches and analyzes facility requirements and manufacturing capabilities / capacities around potential acquisition opportunities.

• Provides technical training for engineering and operations personnel. Provides systems training to other functional areas as necessary.

• Identifies Advanced Manufacturing Engineering needs and communicates these needs to Senior Management.

• Manages facilities maintenance activities through prioritization of safety, health and production needs.

• Identifies safety issues in the immediate work environment and other work areas and recommends solutions for improvement.

• Ensures engineering and facilities maintenance activities are in compliance with Quality System requirements.

• Ensures facility maintenance activities are also in compliance with OSHA and other applicable health and safety standards.

• Performs other related duties as required.

Authority and supervision: Directly manages Facility Maintenance and mentors junior engineers. Reviews and approves project team work and exercises sound business judgment, recognizing that errors may significantly affect the company.


+ Education and Experience


Education Requirements: Bachelor’s in Mechanical Engineering or applicable degree.

Experience Requirements: 8-10 years of Engineering (Manufacturing & Design) experience supporting products in post market phases of product lifecycle. 3- 5 years of leadership experience. Five years in medical device industry desirable.


Job knowledge skills and abilities


• Proficiency in 2D drafting and 3D modeling, preferably AutoCAD and SolidWorks.

• Knowledge of ANSI Y14.5 drafting standards.

• Expertise in properties of various materials, such as stainless steel, aluminum and plastics.

• Expertise in part fabrication techniques, such as machining and injection molding.

• Expertise in the factors that affect the life of re-usable surgical instruments, such as corrosion, wear and thermal cycling.

• Thorough understanding of part tolerancing and tolerance stack-up analysis.

• Thorough understanding of mechanical stress analysis.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office, Project and other job associated software.

• In depth understanding of regulatory requirements for medical device design control and manufacturing.

• In depth understanding of various surgical techniques as related to surgical instruments.

• Ability to apply scientific reasoning and to develop test methodologies to resolve complex technical problems.


+ Competencies


Advanced Manufacturing and Technical Leadership

Skills: Automation, insourcing, manufacturing processes, design for manufacturing, mechanical analysis, and root cause investigation.

Behaviors: Leads manufacturing initiatives from planning through implementation; guides technical decisions and resolves complex product and process issues using evidence.


Program Execution and Business Acumen

Skills: Project planning, risk and milestone management, budget control, CapEx evaluation, and cost savings analysis.

Behaviors: Sets priorities, coordinates resources, anticipates risks, and delivers projects within agreed budgets and timelines; connects investment decisions to business results.


People Leadership and Cross Functional Collaboration

Skills: Coaching, delegation, career development, technical training, communication, and stakeholder alignment.

Behaviors: Sets clear expectations, develops direct reports and junior engineers, holds teams accountable, and aligns Operations, Supply Chain,

Quality, and Engineering around shared goals.


Continuous Improvement and Lean Execution

Skills: Lean tools, kaizen and Blue Belt project coaching, CI planning, savings tracking, and process improvement.

title: REGISTRATION REPRESENTATIVE
description:
About Christ Community Health Services

Since 1995, Christ Community Health Services (CCHS) has provided high-quality healthcare to underserved communities through distinctively Christian service. As a faith-based Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC), we serve approximately 60,000 patients each year across our Memphis health centers, offering primary care, dental, behavioral health, pharmacy, and specialty services.

About the Role

Christ Community Health Services is seeking a welcoming, dependable Registration Representative to serve as a first point of contact for patients and support access to care for diverse and underserved populations.

This role manages patient check-in and check-out, registration, appointment scheduling, insurance verification, payment collection, and demographic and financial information, including sliding fee discount eligibility. The Registration Representative maintains accurate information in the electronic health record and supports efficient clinic flow while protecting patient privacy.

Why Join CCHS?

  • Help patients feel welcomed, respected, and supported from the moment they enter the health center.
  • Play an important role in helping underserved patients access medical, dental, and behavioral healthcare.
  • Work closely with clinical, administrative, and care coordination teams.
  • Develop experience in patient access, insurance verification, scheduling, and healthcare operations.
  • Contribute to a culture grounded in compassion, service, excellence, and Christian faith.

Our Core Values - and What They Look Like in This Role

CCHS team members are expected to demonstrate our core values every day. For a Registration Representative, they mean:

  • Intentional Love - Greeting every patient, family member, and colleague with compassion, patience, dignity, and respect.
  • Devoted Service - Providing reliable assistance, clear communication, and thoughtful support throughout each patient interaction.
  • Humble Excellence - Maintaining accurate records, protecting confidential information, and providing excellent service while remaining teachable and Christ-centered.

What You'll Do

  • Greet and check in patients in a courteous, professional, and culturally responsive manner.
  • Register new patients and update existing records with accurate demographic, insurance, income, and contact information in the electronic health record.
  • Verify insurance coverage and determine eligibility for the sliding fee discount program in accordance with HRSA requirements.
  • Collect copayments, account balances, and other patient payments; issue receipts and maintain accurate cash-handling records.
  • Complete end-of-day reports, count collected funds, and reconcile the cash drawer at the close of each business day.
  • Schedule, confirm, reschedule, and cancel appointments while supporting patient access and efficient provider schedules.
  • Complete patient check-out, including scheduling follow-up appointments, providing visit summaries, and coordinating referrals as directed.
  • Safeguard patient confidentiality and comply with HIPAA requirements and organizational privacy policies.
  • Use interpreter services and communication resources to assist patients with limited English proficiency.
  • Respond professionally to questions regarding services, clinic policies, billing, appointments, and other general information.
  • Scan, upload, and manage patient documents in the electronic health record accurately and promptly.
  • Monitor patient wait times and escalate concerns to the appropriate team member to support a positive patient experience.
  • Support care coordination by relaying complete and accurate messages to clinical teams.
  • Make reminder calls for upcoming patient appointments.
  • Participate in quality-improvement efforts focused on patient satisfaction, reduced no-show rates, and improved access to care.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, secure, and welcoming front-desk environment.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What You'll Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Two to four years of clerical experience, preferably in a medical or healthcare setting.
  • Medical Billing and Coding Certificate or Medical Assistant credential preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to provide compassionate, patient-centered service to diverse and underserved populations.
  • Strong verbal communication and listening skills, with the ability to explain information clearly, professionally, and empathetically.
  • Cultural awareness and a commitment to health equity.
  • Understanding of medical, dental, and behavioral health scheduling workflows, terminology, and care coordination processes.
  • Experience using electronic health records, practice-management systems, or call-center platforms with accurate data-entry skills.
  • Strong attention to detail when documenting patient information and verifying program or insurance eligibility.
  • Knowledge of HIPAA, patient privacy, Medicaid, Medicare, commercial insurance, and sliding fee discount programs.

What Success Looks Like

  • Patients receive a courteous, respectful, and welcoming experience at check-in and check-out.
  • Registration, insurance, income, scheduling, and contact information is complete and accurate.
  • Payments, receipts, cash drawers, and end-of-day reports are handled accurately and reconciled promptly.
  • Patient information remains confidential and secure.
  • Appointments and follow-up needs are coordinated efficiently to support access and continuity of care.
  • Patient questions and concerns are handled professionally or directed promptly to the appropriate team member.
  • The front-desk environment remains organized and contributes positively to clinic workflow and team culture.
  • The Christian mission and values of CCHS are reflected in daily interactions and work practices.

Work Environment

This position operates in a clinic setting and involves regular interaction with patients, family members, clinical staff, and administrative team members. The role may involve exposure to infectious or contagious illnesses.

The position requires sitting for approximately 70% of the workday, standing for approximately 15%, and walking for approximately 15%. The employee may occasionally lift, push, or pull boxes or other items weighing up to 15 pounds.

The role requires frequent use of computers, telephones, office equipment, payment-processing equipment, and cash-management systems. Local work-related travel may account for approximately 15% of the position, depending on clinic assignment and operational needs. Specific responsibilities may vary somewhat by location.

What We Offer

  • Competitive pay and comprehensive benefits, including medical, dental, and vision coverage.
  • Generous Paid Time Off, including 120 hours during the first year, plus paid holidays.
  • 401(k) retirement plan.
  • Annual paid Restorative Day supporting wellness and work-life balance.
  • Mission-driven culture and employee recognition programs.
  • Professional development and opportunities to grow within healthcare operations.
  • The opportunity to help expand access to high-quality healthcare throughout Memphis.

Make a Difference Through Patient Service

If you are a compassionate, detail-oriented professional who enjoys helping others and wants to support patients throughout their healthcare experience, we invite you to consider joining Christ Community Health Services.

Come serve with purpose. Come welcome patients with compassion. Come make a difference in our community.

title: Harm Reduction Specialist
description:
Job Title: Harm Reduction Specialist

The Harm Reduction Outreach Specialist provides mobile outreach services in the South Bronx providing health education, risk reduction information and safe injection equipment and other supplies to people who use drugs. Conduct Harm Reduction Services and Syringe exchange program enrollments, including review of substance use history, current drug use practices, medical waste disposal practices, and providing low-threshold counseling and education to participants within the agency and on the mobile unit

Primary Duties & Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Ability to operate a motor-vehicle (vans).
  • Conduct Harm Reduction Services (HRS) and syringe services program enrollment and distribution at sanctioned locations.
  • Collection of syringe litter waste in the South Bronx.
  • Serve as agency liaison at community forums, events, and planning bodies as appropriate and where assigned.

  • Ability to explain, describe, and discuss safer injection practices, other safe drug using strategies, and safer sex options.
  • Provision of and documentation of prevention education, counseling, referrals, safer drug using education, and strategies.

Qualifications/Criteria:

  • A valid NYS driver’s license is required with a minimum of 3 years of driving experience.

  • Bilingual (English and Spanish) preferred.

Education:

  • High School Graduate or GED.

title: Assistant Director of Alumni Relations
description:
The Pingry School, a prestigious K-12 coeducational, independent day school with a rich history dating back to its founding by Dr. John F. Pingry in 1861, stands at the forefront of academic excellence in the United States. With campuses located in Basking Ridge, Pottersville, and Short Hills, New Jersey, Pingry is celebrated for its academic programs, a student-written Honor Code that underpins our community values, and a comprehensive commitment to arts, athletics, community, and civic engagement. Our mission is to inspire in our students a lifelong passion for learning, personal development, and social responsibility, preparing them to be global citizens and luminaries of the 21st century. Rooted in relationships and guided by our foundational philosophy, Pingry is a vibrant community of more than 1,100 students hailing from over 90 towns across New Jersey and New York. At Pingry, we are united by a love of learning and a commitment to preparing students to navigate the complexities of the 21st century with confidence and integrity. For more information, we invite you to visit our website at pingry.org or connect with The Pingry School on Facebook, X, and Instagram to discover why we love school.

Position Summary
Joining a high-performing Institutional Advancement team, this role serves as the essential operational and logistical engine for Pingry’s alumni engagement program, supporting an active network of over 8,000 graduates and a student body of approximately 1,100 K-12 students.

The Assistant Director ensures the flawless execution of traditional alumni events, digital communications, committee administration, and database management. By taking ownership of core logistical workflows and daily constituent touchpoints, this role builds the foundational infrastructure that allows the broader Alumni Relations team to scale its high-impact strategic initiatives.

  • The ideal candidate is a highly organized, detail-oriented project manager and communicator who excels at event coordination, visual design, and data administration.
  • They take pride in behind-the-scenes execution, possess a strong aesthetic eye for digital newsletters and media assets, and demonstrate rigorous database discipline.
  • A collaborative team player, they bring warmth, professionalism, and proactive problem-solving to every constituent interaction, acting as a reliable partner to the Director and Associate Director.

Responsibilities

Event Logistics & Execution:

    • Plan, coordinate, and execute logistics for legacy alumni events, heavily focusing on Class Reunions, Homecoming, and traditional regional receptions.
    • Manage vendor contracts, venue arrangements, catering menus, registration setup, name tags, and on-site event flow.
    • Serve as the primary logistical point of contact for class reunion chairs and traditional event host committees.
  • Digital Communications & Creative Content:
    • Draft, design, and distribute the monthly alumni newsletter and targeted email broadcasts.
    • Create visual assets using design tools (e.g., Canva) for email headers, social media promotion, and digital event invitations.
    • Partner with the Associate Director of Career Development to ensure career-focused programs (like the Mentorship Portal and Networking Workshops) are properly marketed in general alumni communications.

Database Administration & Operations:

    • Ensure data integrity to support the Associate Director's career networking efforts, ensuring alumni industries and job titles are properly logged for the mentorship ecosystem.

Committee Support & Volunteer Coordination:

    • Provide dedicated administrative and logistical support to key alumni committees, specifically absorbing coordination for the Pingry Alumni Association (PAA) Board.
    • Coordinate committee meeting schedules, prepare agendas, record meeting minutes, and track follow-up action items.

Departmental Support & Special Projects:

    • Provide cross-functional support for major Advancement Office events and institutional campaign initiatives as needed.

Qualifications

  • Experience: 1–3 years of professional experience in alumni relations, event management, development operations, marketing, or high-level administrative support.

  • Ability to manage multiple project timelines independently
  • Strong customer-service orientation.

Individuals most suited for magistrate positions possess the ability to exercise sound judgment and to make decisions, are proficient at general office and computer skills, understand North Carolina Court Systems procedures, are team players with the ability to work under pressure, and have the ability to communicate effectively with the general public.

title: Agrichem Controls Technician
description:
About the Role
KSi Conveyors is seeking a Controls Technician to join our AgriChem Business Unit. This position is responsible for the installation, startup, commissioning, troubleshooting, and ongoing service of automation systems used in agricultural chemical and dry fertilizer facilities.

Our AgriChem division provides automation solutions for dry fertilizer blending and handling, liquid chemical batching, mixing, and processing operations. The Controls Technician will work directly with customers, engineering, and field operations to ensure equipment and automation systems are installed correctly, operate reliably, and meet customer expectations.

This is a hands-on technical position where experience with industrial electrical controls, troubleshooting, and automation systems is preferred. The ideal candidate enjoys solving problems, can work independently in the field, and takes pride in delivering excellent customer service.

Travel is estimated at approximately 50%, with overnight travel required during the workweek. Employees can generally expect to be home on weekends, although occasional weekend work may be necessary based on customer needs or project schedules.

Responsibilities
Field Service, Installation & Startup
• Perform field startup, commissioning, troubleshooting, and service of KSi AgriChem automation systems.
• Support automation installations at dry fertilizer blending facilities, liquid chemical processing facilities, and agricultural retail locations.
• Troubleshoot electrical and controls-related issues involving PLCs, HMIs, motor controls, sensors, instrumentation, and industrial communication networks.
• Verify proper operation of automation systems, including motors, conveyors, pumps, valves, scales, flow meters, and associated equipment.
• Work closely with the AgriChem Field Operations Supervisor to coordinate site visits, startup schedules, service requirements, and customer needs.
• Diagnose and resolve equipment issues independently while utilizing engineering and technical support resources when necessary.
• Assist customers and local electricians in identifying and resolving electrical installation and operational issues.
• Perform system testing and verification to ensure installations meet KSi quality and performance expectations.
• Identify opportunities to improve equipment reliability, system performance, and customer satisfaction.

Automation & Technical Support
• Troubleshoot and support PLC-based automation systems, HMIs, VFDs, and industrial motor control systems.
• Diagnose electrical and communication issues using electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and appropriate testing equipment.
• Support dry fertilizer batching, blending, receiving, loadout, and material-handling automation systems.
• Support liquid chemical and fertilizer automation systems, including pumps, valves, metering equipment, and automated batching processes.
• Assist with troubleshooting instrumentation such as flow meters, pressure sensors, level sensors, load cells, and other process control devices.
• Work with KSi engineering and controls personnel to identify software or hardware issues and implement corrective actions.
• Provide phone and remote technical support to customers during peak agricultural seasons, assisting with troubleshooting, operational questions, and resolving automation-related issues.
• Assist with customer phone support outside of peak seasons as needed.
• Participate in technical training to develop knowledge of KSi automation products and evolving technologies.

Customer Service & Project Coordination
• Serve as a professional representative of KSi while working directly with customers in the field.
• Communicate project progress, technical issues, and service needs to the AgriChem team.
• Train customers and operators on proper system operation, troubleshooting, and routine maintenance.
• Complete required service documentation, startup reports, and project paperwork accurately and in a timely manner.
• Coordinate with the Field Operations Supervisor regarding service priorities, scheduling, and required materials.
• Identify equipment or installation quality issues and communicate findings to the appropriate departments.
• Maintain accurate records of service work, parts usage, and company-provided inventory.
• Take ownership of assigned work and follow issues through to resolution

Travel & Work Environment
• Approximately 50% travel, primarily to customer locations throughout the United States.
• Overnight travel is required, generally during the normal workweek.
• Employees can typically expect to be home on weekends. Occasional weekend travel or emergency service may be required.
• Work will be performed in agricultural retail facilities, fertilizer blending plants, chemical processing facilities, and industrial environments.
• Position requires the ability to work around electrical equipment, industrial machinery, and agricultural processing systems while following all applicable safety procedures.
• Must be comfortable working both independently in the field and collaboratively with internal teams.
• Work schedules may vary based on installation timelines, seasonal customer demands, and service needs


Requirements

Required
• Basic understanding of electrical systems and willingness to develop industrial controls and automation skills.
• Mechanical aptitude and familiarity with basic mechanical systems and hand tools.
• Ability to read and understand technical documentation and willingness to learn electrical schematics and wiring diagrams.
• Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving abilities.
• Ability to work independently, determine solutions, and complete assigned work.
• Strong communication, organizational, and customer service skills.
• Ability to communicate technical information clearly to customers and other team members.
• Basic computer proficiency and ability to use service software and electronic documentation.
• Valid driver's license and ability to travel regularly throughout the assigned service territory.
• Willingness to adapt to changing schedules and take ownership of customer issues.

Preferred
• Previous hands-on experience with industrial electrical controls and automation systems.
• Experience troubleshooting electrical control circuits, motor starters, relays, sensors, and related industrial equipment.
• Working knowledge of PLC-controlled equipment and HMI-based automation systems
• Experience with PLC programming, troubleshooting, or software modifications.
• Experience working with variable frequency drives (VFDs), industrial networking, or automation communication protocols.
• Familiarity with industrial instrumentation, including flow meters, load cells, level sensors, and process control devices.
• Experience with agricultural equipment, dry fertilizer systems, liquid chemical processing, or industrial batching operations.
• Previous experience performing field service, equipment commissioning, or industrial automation startups.
• Understanding of three-phase electrical systems, motor controls, and industrial electrical safety practices.

Additional Expectations
The successful candidate will demonstrate a willingness to continually learn, adapt to new technologies, and represent KSi with professionalism. We are looking for someone who takes pride in their work, enjoys solving challenging technical problems, and understands the importance of keeping customers operational.

This position is an important part of the continued growth of the AgriChem Business Unit and will have opportunities to develop technical expertise as our automation offerings expand

Benefits

  • 401(k)
  • 401(k) matching
  • Health Insurance
  • Dental Insurance
  • Vision Insurance
  • Life Insurance
  • Paid Time Off
  • Flexible Schedule​

  • Full Time Hours or open to part time hours.
