title: Residential Generator Apprentice in Atlanta
description:
About Premier Generators, a Power Support Partners Company:

How would you like to be a part of one of the fastest-growing home service companies in Georgia? You will be able to play an important role within the Install Team at Premier Generators, a Power Support Partners Company.

Our company is seeking an Apprentice interested in specializing in whole-home backup power generators. The Residential Generator Apprentice plays a crucial role in supporting the installation of residential backup generators. This position involves assisting the Generator Electrician and Gas Technician in various tasks related to generator installation. The ideal candidate should possess basic technical skills, a strong work ethic, and a commitment to ensuring the reliable operation of backup generators in residential settings. The ideal candidate should want to be a learner first, learn the trade, but then be ready to become a Lead Installer and run their own crew in the future.

Work Location & Schedule:

Our warehouse is located at:

1000 Cobb Pl Blvd NW, Suite 290, Kennesaw, GA 30144

Apprentices typically begin their workday by arriving at the warehouse around 6:30 AM to prepare for the day. This includes reviewing job assignments, loading materials and equipment, confirming project details, and ensuring all necessary tools and safety gear are ready.

After morning preparation, crews travel in company vehicles to scheduled job sites to complete installations and service work. In this role, you will:

  • Design, build, and evaluate multi-step agentic AI systems, including autonomous agents capable of planning, tool use, memory management, and multi-agent collaboration
  • Research and implement state-of-the-art techniques in agentic architectures, such as ReAct, reflection loops, chain-of-thought prompting, and tool-augmented reasoning
  • Develop and maintain agent orchestration frameworks, defining how agents decompose tasks, delegate to sub-agents, and handle failure and recovery

title: Director of Preclinical Operations
description:
Position Summary

RadioMedix is seeking an experienced and strategic leader to serve as Director of Preclinical Operations, overseeing the company's Research & Development (R&D) and preclinical functions, including radiochemistry, biology, and in vivo laboratories.

This position is responsible for advancing early-stage radioligand therapy (RLT) and diagnostic candidates through preclinical development toward IND-enabling studies, ensuring programs are executed efficiently, within established timelines and budgets, and in accordance with applicable regulatory and quality standards.

The successful candidate will bring a demonstrated ability to build, lead, and develop high-performing scientific teams while establishing scalable, GLP-compliant laboratory operations. This individual will drive laboratory modernization through technology, systems, and process improvements while maintaining high standards for scientific integrity, radiation safety, regulatory compliance, and laboratory organization.

About RadioMedix

RadioMedix is a Houston-based, clinical-stage radiopharmaceutical company focused on developing targeted diagnostic and radioligand therapeutic products for cancer and other serious diseases. The company's work spans discovery, preclinical development, clinical studies, and manufacturing, with programs utilizing radioisotopes such as Pb-212, Ga-68, and Cu-64.

Key Responsibilities

1. Team Leadership and Organizational Development

  • Lead, recruit, develop, and retain multidisciplinary R&D and preclinical teams, establishing clear objectives, priorities, and performance expectations.

  • Foster a culture of scientific excellence, accountability, collaboration, operational ownership, and radiation safety.

  • Provide leadership, coaching, and professional development to managers, scientists, and technical personnel.

  • Establish performance management practices, conduct employee evaluations, and support succession planning and career development.

  • Evaluate staffing needs, allocate resources, and balance workloads across concurrent research and development programs.

  • Establish accountability for departmental performance, productivity, and achievement of organizational objectives.

2. Laboratory Operations and Management

  • Oversee the daily operations of radiochemistry, cell biology, and in vivo (vivarium) laboratories.

  • Manage laboratory budgets, capital expenditures, equipment procurement, maintenance, calibration, and inventory management.

  • Coordinate isotope procurement, supply planning, and delivery schedules to support research and preclinical study timelines.

  • Ensure compliance with applicable radioactive materials licenses, ALARA principles, dosimetry requirements, and radioactive waste management practices in collaboration with the Radiation Safety Officer (RSO).

  • Oversee animal research activities and ensure compliance with approved IACUC protocols and applicable AAALAC or OLAW standards, where applicable.

  • Establish and maintain standardized operating procedures (SOPs), data integrity practices, electronic laboratory documentation, and inspection-ready records.

  • Identify and implement opportunities to improve laboratory efficiency, resource utilization, operational performance, and cost management.

3. Laboratory Standards, Organization, and Housekeeping

  • Establish and enforce consistent standards for laboratory cleanliness, organization, safety, and housekeeping across all laboratory, hot cell, and vivarium areas.

  • Assign designated managerial ownership for individual laboratory areas and establish clear accountability for maintaining operational standards.

  • Implement routine laboratory inspections, cleaning schedules, contamination surveys, and corrective action processes.

  • Ensure deficiencies are documented, addressed, and resolved in a timely manner.

  • Maintain continuous inspection readiness for radiation safety reviews, IACUC assessments, GLP inspections, and external partner or client audits.

4. GLP Implementation and Regulatory Readiness

  • Lead the implementation and ongoing development of Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) standards in accordance with FDA 21 CFR Part 58, progressing from initial gap assessment through operational implementation.

  • Establish the necessary GLP infrastructure, including study director and test facility management responsibilities, controlled SOPs, study protocols, amendments, training records, equipment qualification and calibration documentation, and archival procedures.

  • Partner with an independent Quality Assurance (QA) function to establish study auditing procedures, facility inspections, documentation requirements, and a GLP master schedule.

  • Identify which preclinical studies can be conducted internally under GLP requirements and which should be outsourced to qualified contract research organizations (CROs).

  • Develop implementation timelines, resource requirements, and budgets to support GLP readiness.

  • Ensure laboratory practices, study documentation, and data management processes support regulatory submissions and inspection requirements.

5. Laboratory Technology, Systems, and Modernization

  • Evaluate existing laboratory systems and lead the selection, implementation, and optimization of technology platforms, including laboratory information management systems (LIMS), electronic laboratory notebooks (ELN), sample and isotope inventory tracking, equipment scheduling, and imaging and dosimetry analysis tools.

  • Ensure computerized systems and electronic records meet applicable data integrity requirements and FDA 21 CFR Part 11 standards, where required.

  • Lead technology adoption through employee training, change management, and ongoing system utilization monitoring.

  • Identify opportunities to incorporate automation, advanced assay technologies, imaging capabilities, and data analytics, including artificial intelligence (AI), to improve research quality, efficiency, and operational performance.

  • Establish scalable systems and processes that support the company's anticipated growth and evolving R&D requirements.

6. Preclinical Program Development and Execution

  • Direct the design and execution of preclinical development programs for radioligand therapeutics and companion diagnostics.

  • Oversee key preclinical activities, including binding and internalization assays, radiolabeling optimization, stability testing, biodistribution, SPECT/PET imaging, efficacy assessments, dosimetry, and toxicology.

  • Translate scientific and business objectives into structured development plans with defined milestones, budgets, timelines, and go/no-go criteria.

  • Identify, select, and manage CROs and academic collaborators, including oversight of GLP toxicology studies, scopes of work, budgets, deliverables, and data quality.

  • Author and review preclinical sections of IND, IMPD, and other applicable regulatory submissions.

  • Support regulatory interactions and responses to inquiries from the FDA and other regulatory authorities.

  • Monitor program performance, identify potential risks, and provide timely updates and recommendations to executive leadership.

  • Ensure preclinical programs remain aligned with corporate development priorities and strategic objectives.

7. Cross-Functional Collaboration and Business Support

  • Collaborate with CMC, manufacturing, quality, regulatory affairs, and clinical teams to facilitate the progression of development candidates from discovery through first-in-human studies.

  • Support business development and strategic partnership activities through technical due diligence, scientific presentations, and preclinical program assessments.

  • Provide technical oversight and support for collaborative research initiatives and CDMO-related client projects, where applicable.

  • Contribute to grant applications, scientific publications, and presentations at industry conferences.

  • Evaluate emerging targets, chelators, linkers, and radioisotopes to support pipeline expansion and scientific innovation.

  • Provide scientific and operational recommendations to executive leadership regarding R&D priorities, resource allocation, and investment opportunities.

Qualifications

Education

  • PhD in Radiochemistry, Nuclear Medicine, Pharmacology, Molecular Imaging, Cancer Biology, or a related scientific discipline.

  • A Master's degree combined with substantially greater relevant industry experience may be considered.

Professional Experience

  • Minimum of 10 years of pharmaceutical or biotechnology drug development experience, including at least 5 years in radiopharmaceutical development.

  • Demonstrated experience advancing radioligand therapeutics (RLTs) or theranostic agents through preclinical development, preferably through IND submission.

  • Direct experience working within GLP environments, including involvement in establishing, implementing, or maintaining GLP-compliant laboratory operations or study programs.

  • Experience managing CRO relationships, overseeing GLP studies, and contributing to IND or equivalent regulatory submissions.

  • Working knowledge of radiolabeling, biodistribution, SPECT/PET imaging, and dosimetry studies.

Leadership and Operational Experience

  • Minimum of 5 years of progressive leadership experience managing multidisciplinary scientific teams, including experience managing managers.

  • Demonstrated success leading scientific programs, building and retaining high-performing teams, and scaling or improving laboratory operations.

  • Proven ability to manage laboratory operations, including budgets, staffing, equipment, maintenance, housekeeping, safety, and regulatory compliance.

  • Experience establishing performance expectations, operational procedures, and accountability across scientific and technical teams.

  • Demonstrated experience selecting, implementing, or optimizing laboratory software and technology systems, such as LIMS or ELN platforms.

  • Ability to lead organizational change and implement operational improvements that support business growth and scientific objectives.

Technical and Professional Skills

  • Working knowledge of radiation safety regulations, NRC or Agreement State licensing requirements, ALARA principles, dosimetry, and radioactive waste management.

  • Understanding of GLP requirements, FDA regulations, data integrity standards, and applicable electronic records requirements.

  • Ability to evaluate emerging scientific, technological, and regulatory developments and translate them into practical operational improvements.

  • Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving capabilities.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex scientific and operational information to employees, executive leadership, external partners, and regulatory authorities.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working with both alpha- and beta-emitting radioisotopes.

  • Background in therapeutic and diagnostic radiopharmaceutical development, including theranostic pairs.

  • Experience building, restructuring, or scaling a preclinical R&D function within a growing biotechnology or pharmaceutical organization.

  • Previous experience serving as a GLP Study Director or Test Facility Management representative, or leading a laboratory through a GLP inspection or audit.

  • Experience with FDA 21 CFR Part 11 validation of computerized systems, laboratory automation, or implementation of data analytics and AI tools in research environments.

  • Exposure to CMC, GMP manufacturing, or CDMO operations, including an understanding of how preclinical development decisions affect manufacturing scale-up.

  • Experience supporting business development, technical due diligence, strategic partnerships, or fee-for-service preclinical programs.

  • Established publication record in radiopharmaceutical science and active professional involvement in the nuclear medicine community, such as SNMMI.

title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing & Process Engineering
description:
Employer: JFE Shoji Power Canada Inc
Position: Senior Manager, Manufacturing & Process Engineering
Terms of Employment: Full-time / Permanent
Location: Burlington, Ontario
Language: English
Vacancy: Please note that this posting is for an existing role.
Benefits: Eligible for discretionary bonuses and/or salary increases in accordance with company policy. Eligible for RRSP, Pension Plan, Dental Insurance, Medical Insurance and Vision Insurance.
Salary: $160,000 to $180,000 CAD / year (dependent on experience)

About Us
JFE Shoji Power Canada (JSC) is an electrical steel products manufacturer located in Burlington, Ontario. As the largest producer of transformer cores in North America, JSC specializes in wound, amorphous, and step-lap cores for power generation and distribution equipment. Its electrical steel products and magnetic materials are also used in electric vehicle motors and charging station infrastructure, data centres, audio equipment, and other industrial applications.

Since 1972, JSC (formerly Cogent) has grown from a small niche manufacturer to an integral part of the North American electrical steel supply chain with multiple facilities and over 500 employees. JSC is dedicated to meeting the growing demand for electrical energy by providing strategic, innovative, and sustainable solutions to its clients.

What Sets Us Apart?
At JFE Shoji Power Canada, we are more than just a company—we are a community that embraces safety. We have a proactive safety attitude where every team member is empowered to care for each other and take responsibility for keeping everyone safe. By embodying the ICare principles, we ensure that safety is not just a priority but a core value of our culture. Each employee plays an essential role in shaping a workplace where safety is embedded in every action we take, and where incidents are prevented before they happen.

Position Overview:
The Senior Manager, Manufacturing & Process Engineering is responsible for leading all manufacturing engineering, process improvement, automation, capital projects, and continuous improvement initiatives across all facilities. This role drives operational excellence through the development and optimization of manufacturing processes, equipment, systems, and engineering talent while ensuring safety, quality, productivity, and cost objectives are achieved.

The incumbent provides strategic, technical leadership and mentorship to Manufacturing and Process Engineers, oversees major capital investments, supports new product and process launches, and partners cross-functionally with Production, Maintenance, Quality, Supply Chain, and Safety teams to deliver sustainable business results.

Key Responsibilities
Leadership & Team Development
  • Lead, mentor, and develop the Manufacturing & Process Engineering team.
  • Establish departmental goals, priorities, and performance expectations aligned with business objectives.
  • Provide coaching, succession planning, training, and career development opportunities.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, continuous learning, and operational excellence.
  • Support recruitment, onboarding, and performance management activities.
Manufacturing Engineering & Process Improvement
  • Develop and execute strategies to improve safety, quality, productivity, efficiency, and cost performance.
  • Lead process optimization initiatives utilizing Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Kaizen, and other continuous improvement methodologies.
  • Analyze production data and identify opportunities to eliminate waste, reduce downtime, and improve throughput.
  • Establish and maintain manufacturing standards, process documentation, PFMEAs, work instructions, Safety Lock Out Placards and engineering specifications.
  • Ensure manufacturing processes are capable, repeatable, and compliant with quality standards.
Capital Projects & Automation
  • Lead capital equipment planning, justification, procurement, installation, and commissioning activities.
  • Manage engineering projects from concept through implementation, ensuring adherence to budget, timing, and project objectives.
  • Evaluate and implement automation technologies that improve operational performance and reduce risk.
  • Coordinate equipment relocations, upgrades, and facility improvement initiatives.
Operational Excellence
  • Partner with Production, Maintenance, and Quality teams to resolve complex operational issues.
  • Drive improvements in key performance indicators including:
    • OEE
    • Scrap and rework reduction
    • Throughput
    • Labour efficiency
    • Quality performance
    • On-time delivery
  • Lead root cause investigations and corrective action activities related to production, quality, and safety concerns.
  • Champion a continuous improvement culture throughout the organization.
Safety, Quality & Compliance
  • Ensure compliance with all applicable health and safety legislation, company policies, and environmental requirements.
  • Support and promote compliance with quality management systems, customer requirements, and industry standards.
  • Ensure engineering changes and equipment modifications meet regulatory and safety requirements.
  • Participate in audits and support corrective and preventive actions.
Strategic Planning
  • Develop and manage departmental budgets and capital expenditure plans.
  • Support long-term operational and capacity planning initiatives.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies and manufacturing best practices.
  • Present project updates, business cases, and performance metrics to senior leadership.
Knowledge & Skills
  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Industrial, Manufacturing, Electrical, Mechatronics, or a related Engineering discipline.
  • Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) designation, or eligibility for registration with Professional Engineers Ontario (PEO), considered an asset.
  • Progressive manufacturing engineering and leadership experience within a complex industrial or manufacturing environment.
  • Demonstrated experience leading engineering teams and cross-functional improvement initiatives.
  • Demonstrated experience managing significant capital projects from business case through commissioning and operational handover.
  • Experience with automation, robotics, process optimization, and manufacturing equipment integration.
  • Lean Six Sigma certification considered an asset.
  • PMP or equivalent project management certification considered an asset.

title: Senior Database Administrator
description:
At Braze, we have found our people. We’re a genuinely approachable, exceptionally kind, and intensely passionate crew.

We seek to ignite that passion by setting high standards, championing teamwork, and creating work-life harmony as we collectively navigate rapid growth on a global scale while striving for greater equity and opportunity – inside and outside our organization.

To flourish here, you must be prepared to set a high bar for yourself and those around you. There is always a way to contribute: Acting with autonomy, having accountability and being open to new perspectives are essential to our continued success.

Our deep curiosity to learn and our eagerness to share diverse passions with others gives us balance and injects a one-of-a-kind vibrancy into our culture.

If you are driven to solve exhilarating challenges and have a bias toward action in the face of change, you will be empowered to make a real impact here, with a sharp and passionate team at your back. If Braze sounds like a place where you can thrive, we can’t wait to meet you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

The MongoDB Database Administrator (DBA) role is part of the Platform Engineering division within Infrastructure and is responsible for operating, scaling, and securing our internal MongoDB platform. This position supports a growing fleet of MongoDB clusters that back product-critical features, internal systems, and distributed services.

This role partners closely with SREs, application engineers, and the platform security team to ensure MongoDB clusters are performant, resilient, compliant, and well-automated. Our clusters run on a modern Kubernetes-based infrastructure and are managed through GitOps and infrastructure-as-code practices. The DBA will help evolve and mature the platform, support backup and disaster recovery strategies, and assist engineers in designing efficient, durable MongoDB usage.

Cluster Operations & Reliability

  • Operate production MongoDB clusters running in Kubernetes across multiple regions and clouds
  • Monitor cluster health, performance, replication, and storage usage, and proactively address degradation
  • Debug and resolve availability, latency, or data consistency issues in partnership with SREs
  • Participate in on-call rotations as a subject matter expert for MongoDB infrastructure

Automation & Tooling

  • Automate routine operations such as database user management, cluster scaling, version upgrades, and backup restores
  • Maintain and improve internal tooling used for MongoDB observability, lifecycle management, and access control
  • Collaborate with Platform Engineering on Kubernetes-based deployment patterns and GitOps workflows

Backup, Restore & Disaster Recovery

  • Implement and maintain point-in-time recovery, daily snapshots, and cross-region backup strategies
  • Regularly validate restores and participate in resilience exercises and disaster recovery planning
  • Partner with Security and Compliance teams to ensure backups meet RTO/RPO targets and audit requirements

Engineering Support & Best Practices

  • Assist product engineering teams with schema design, indexing strategies, and performance tuning
  • Promote internal best practices for efficient queries, data modeling, and shard key design
  • Document operational runbooks, configuration standards, and performance baselines

WHO YOU ARE

Experience

  • 3–5+ years of experience managing MongoDB in production environments at scale
  • Strong working knowledge of replica sets, sharding, WiredTiger storage engine, oplogs, and journaling
  • Experience operating MongoDB in cloud or containerized environments (Kubernetes preferred)

Skills

  • Comfortable with automation and scripting in languages like Bash, Python, or Go
  • Proficient with MongoDB CLI tools, Atlas APIs, and backup/restore tooling (e.g., mongodump, mongorestore, mongosh, Ops Manager)
  • Familiar with observability stacks (e.g., Datadog, Prometheus, Grafana) and alerting strategies
  • Experience with GitOps workflows and infrastructure-as-code tools (Terraform, Helm, ArgoCD) is a plus

Mindset

  • Detail-oriented and reliability-focused; treats data loss and downtime as unacceptable
  • Strong communicator — able to document clearly, partner cross-functionally, and lead incident response
  • Growth-oriented — comfortable evolving systems, adopting new automation, and supporting other engineers

Bonus

  • Experience with other database platforms (e.g., PostgreSQL, MySQL, DynamoDB)
  • Familiarity with security best practices and compliance frameworks like SOX or SOC 2
  • Contributions to open source MongoDB tooling or community forums

For candidates based in the United States, the pay range for this position at the start of employment is expected to be between $128,842 - $232,200/annually, with an expected On Target Earnings (OTE) between $144,000 - $258,000/annually (including bonus or commission). Your exact offer may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including market location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. In addition to cash compensation, this role qualifies for a comprehensive Total Rewards package that includes equity grants of restricted stock (RSUs) so that you will own a piece of our company.

#LI-Hybrid

WHAT WE OFFER

Braze benefits vary by location, and we encourage you to review our specific benefits offerings for each country at here. More details on benefits plans will be provided if you receive an offer of employment.

From offering comprehensive benefits to fostering hybrid ways of working, we've got you covered so you can prioritize work-life harmony. Braze offers benefits such as:

  • Competitive compensation that may include equity
  • Retirement and Employee Stock Purchase Plans
  • Flexible paid time off
  • Comprehensive benefit plans covering medical, dental, vision, life, and disability
  • Family services that include fertility benefits and equal paid parental leave
  • Professional development supported by formal career pathing, learning platforms, and a yearly learning stipend
  • A curated in-office employee experience, designed to foster community, team connections, and innovation
  • Opportunities to give back to your community, including an annual company-wide Volunteer Week and donation matching
  • Employee Resource Groups that provide supportive communities within Braze
  • Collaborative, transparent, and fun culture recognized as a Great Place to Work®

ABOUT BRAZE

Braze is the leading customer engagement platform that empowers brands to Be Absolutely Engaging™ Braze helps brands deliver great customer experiences that drive value both for consumers and for their businesses. Built on a foundation of composable intelligence, BrazeAI™ allows marketers to combine and activate AI agents, models, and features at every touchpoint throughout the Braze Customer Engagement Platform for smarter, faster, and more meaningful customer engagement. From cross-channel messaging and journey orchestration to Al-powered decisioning and optimization, Braze enables companies to turn action into interaction through autonomous, 1:1 personalized experiences.

The company has repeatedly been recognized as a Leader in marketing technology by industry analysts, and was voted a G2 “Best of Marketing and Digital Advertising Software Product” in 2025.

Braze was also named a 2025 Best Companies To Work For by U.S. News and World Report, a 2025 America’s Greatest Companies by Newsweek, and a 2025 Fortune Best Workplace in Technology™ by Great Place To Work®, among other accolades. Braze is also proudly certified as a Great Place to Work® in the U.S., the UK, Australia, and Singapore.

The company is headquartered in New York with offices in Austin, Berlin, Bucharest, Chicago, Dubai, Jakarta, London, Paris, San Francisco, São Paulo, Singapore, Seoul, Sydney and Tokyo.

BRAZE IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

At Braze, we strive to create equitable growth and opportunities inside and outside the organization.

Building meaningful connections is at the heart of everything we do, and that includes our recruiting practices. We're committed to offering all candidates a fair, accessible, and inclusive experience – regardless of age, color, disability, gender identity, marital status, maternity, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, or status as a protected veteran. When applying and interviewing with Braze, we want you to feel comfortable showcasing what makes you you.

We know that sometimes different circumstances can lead talented people to hesitate to apply for a role unless they meet 100% of the criteria. If this sounds familiar, we encourage you to apply, as we’d love to meet you

At Braze, we’re committed to a fair and transparent candidate experience. To help our recruitment teams focus on what matters most — the person behind each application — we use AI-assisted tools at certain stages of our recruitment process.

title: Senior Compliance Reviewer
description:
What You’ll Do

SourceAmerica is seeking a Senior Compliance Reviewer to conduct comprehensive compliance reviews and provide technical guidance to nonprofit (NPA) agencies participating in the AbilityOne Program. This role is well suited for an experienced auditor or compliance professional who understands the importance of consistent review practices, clear documentation, sound judgment, and practical corrective action.

The Senior Compliance Reviewer will play an important role in supporting SourceAmerica’s mission and responsibilities as a Central Nonprofit Agency. The position will independently conduct Qualification Assessment Reviews, evaluate compliance with applicable AbilityOne Program requirements, document findings, recommend corrective actions, and help nonprofit agencies understand and apply regulatory and program requirements.

Who is SourceAmerica

There are approximately 500 NPAs in the SourceAmerica nonprofit network that provide products or services through the AbilityOne Program and approximately 36,000 AbilityOne employees are in the SourceAmerica nonprofit network. More information can be found at www.SourceAmerica.org/who-we-are

How You Will Spend Your Day ...

  • Independently or collaboratively conduct comprehensive Qualification Assessment Reviews of nonprofit agencies participating in the AbilityOne Program.
  • Review documentation, policies, procedures, labor and wage calculations, site conditions, and other objective evidence to assess compliance with applicable statutory, regulatory, policy, and program requirements.
  • Confirm that Qualification Inspection Packages are complete, accurate, properly documented, and submitted within required timeframes.
  • Identify and document compliance findings, non-conformances, observations, risks, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Prepare clear, accurate, and evidence-supported review reports for internal and external stakeholders.
  • Recommend and assign corrective actions when necessary, clearly communicating remediation requirements and expectations.
  • Evaluate corrective action documentation to determine whether identified compliance concerns have been sufficiently addressed.
  • Provide technical guidance to nonprofit agencies regarding AbilityOne Program requirements, Commission policies, federal regulations, compliance expectations, and related procedures.
  • Participate in readiness reviews to help business partners evaluate compliance preparedness.
  • Gather and analyze information supporting assessments of nonprofit agency qualifications and capabilities.
  • Provide accurate and timely review information to the U.S. AbilityOne Commission to support decisions regarding nonprofit agency eligibility and continued program participation.
  • Identify opportunities to improve compliance review processes, documentation standards, operational efficiency, and consistency.
  • Provide technical support and mentorship to less-senior team members by sharing best practices and promoting consistency in review methods, documentation, regulatory interpretation, and application of compliance standards.
  • Manage multiple reviews, assignments, and deadlines while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Travel approximately 25% to conduct reviews, participate in meetings, and support other operational requirements.

Salary Range

The salary for this position falls in a range between $100,000 - $120,000 depending on your experience and geographic location in the United States.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in compliance, auditing, business administration, public administration, accounting, finance, quality assurance, or another related field.
  • At least five years of relevant professional experience in compliance, auditing, regulatory oversight, quality assurance, inspections, federal contracting, or a related field.
  • Direct knowledge of or experience with the AbilityOne Program, including applicable program requirements, regulations, policies, or nonprofit agency compliance responsibilities.
  • Demonstrated knowledge and application of audit or compliance-review principles, methods, and practices.
  • Experience evaluating objective evidence and developing clear, supportable compliance determinations.
  • Experience identifying non-conformances, documenting findings, and supporting corrective-action processes.
  • Experience writing compliance reports and professional correspondence for internal and external stakeholders, including government or regulatory organizations.
  • Experience conducting or supporting external audits, regulatory reviews, customer audits, or similar assessments.
  • Experience working in a regulated or oversight-driven environment.
  • Strong critical-thinking, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to organize and evaluate complex information.
  • Ability to interpret and explain statutes, regulations, policies, procedures, and program requirements.
  • Ability to build productive working relationships while maintaining independence and objectivity.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple reviews, projects, and deadlines with limited supervision.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, and Word.
  • Ability to travel approximately 25%.

Preferred Qualifications …

  • Quality assurance, audit, and inspection principles.
  • Regulatory and policy interpretation and application.
  • Evidence-based compliance assessment and validation methodologies.
  • Documentation standards and requirements for regulatory and compliance reviews.
  • Development of clear, accurate, and evidence-supported compliance determinations.
  • Corrective action and continuous improvement principles.
  • Risk-based review principles and methods for identifying compliance gaps and areas requiring additional validation.
  • Knowledge of applicable regulatory requirements is strongly preferred:
  • AbilityOne Program requirements, regulations, and policies
  • Applicable provisions of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR)
  • U.S. Department of Labor wage and hour compliance requirements, including the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), Service Contract Act (SCA), Davis-Bacon Act/Davis-Bacon and Related Acts (DBA/DBRA), collective bargaining agreements (CBAs), wage determinations, and applicable requirements for product and service contracts
  • Federal Contractor Code of Business Ethics and Conduct requirements
  • Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) requirements
  • Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) requirements
  • Drug-Free Workplace Act requirements and related compliance standards.

Work Environment

Our organization offers both a hybrid work model—where employees work in our office two to three days per week and work from home the balance of the workweek—as well as a fully remote work model, depending on the job requirements.

Employee Benefits

We offer a comprehensive employee benefits package that includes paid holidays, vacation time, sick leave, medical, dental, and vision insurance, a solid retirement plan, and more!

Accessibility Support

We’re committed to offering reasonable accommodation to job applicants with disabilities. If you need assistance or accommodation due to disability, please contact us at Human Resources (888) 411-8424 or hr@sourceamerica.org.

Equal Opportunity Employment

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. View our EEO Policy .

title: Agrichem Controls Technician
description:
About the Role
KSi Conveyors is seeking a Controls Technician to join our AgriChem Business Unit. This position is responsible for the installation, startup, commissioning, troubleshooting, and ongoing service of automation systems used in agricultural chemical and dry fertilizer facilities.

Our AgriChem division provides automation solutions for dry fertilizer blending and handling, liquid chemical batching, mixing, and processing operations. The Controls Technician will work directly with customers, engineering, and field operations to ensure equipment and automation systems are installed correctly, operate reliably, and meet customer expectations.

This is a hands-on technical position where experience with industrial electrical controls, troubleshooting, and automation systems is preferred. The ideal candidate enjoys solving problems, can work independently in the field, and takes pride in delivering excellent customer service.

Travel is estimated at approximately 50%, with overnight travel required during the workweek. Employees can generally expect to be home on weekends, although occasional weekend work may be necessary based on customer needs or project schedules.

Responsibilities
Field Service, Installation & Startup
• Perform field startup, commissioning, troubleshooting, and service of KSi AgriChem automation systems.
• Support automation installations at dry fertilizer blending facilities, liquid chemical processing facilities, and agricultural retail locations.
• Troubleshoot electrical and controls-related issues involving PLCs, HMIs, motor controls, sensors, instrumentation, and industrial communication networks.
• Verify proper operation of automation systems, including motors, conveyors, pumps, valves, scales, flow meters, and associated equipment.
• Work closely with the AgriChem Field Operations Supervisor to coordinate site visits, startup schedules, service requirements, and customer needs.
• Diagnose and resolve equipment issues independently while utilizing engineering and technical support resources when necessary.
• Assist customers and local electricians in identifying and resolving electrical installation and operational issues.
• Perform system testing and verification to ensure installations meet KSi quality and performance expectations.
• Identify opportunities to improve equipment reliability, system performance, and customer satisfaction.

Automation & Technical Support
• Troubleshoot and support PLC-based automation systems, HMIs, VFDs, and industrial motor control systems.
• Diagnose electrical and communication issues using electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and appropriate testing equipment.
• Support dry fertilizer batching, blending, receiving, loadout, and material-handling automation systems.
• Support liquid chemical and fertilizer automation systems, including pumps, valves, metering equipment, and automated batching processes.
• Assist with troubleshooting instrumentation such as flow meters, pressure sensors, level sensors, load cells, and other process control devices.
• Work with KSi engineering and controls personnel to identify software or hardware issues and implement corrective actions.
• Provide phone and remote technical support to customers during peak agricultural seasons, assisting with troubleshooting, operational questions, and resolving automation-related issues.
• Assist with customer phone support outside of peak seasons as needed.
• Participate in technical training to develop knowledge of KSi automation products and evolving technologies.

Customer Service & Project Coordination
• Serve as a professional representative of KSi while working directly with customers in the field.
• Communicate project progress, technical issues, and service needs to the AgriChem team.
• Train customers and operators on proper system operation, troubleshooting, and routine maintenance.
• Complete required service documentation, startup reports, and project paperwork accurately and in a timely manner.
• Coordinate with the Field Operations Supervisor regarding service priorities, scheduling, and required materials.
• Identify equipment or installation quality issues and communicate findings to the appropriate departments.
• Maintain accurate records of service work, parts usage, and company-provided inventory.
• Take ownership of assigned work and follow issues through to resolution

Travel & Work Environment
• Approximately 50% travel, primarily to customer locations throughout the United States.
• Overnight travel is required, generally during the normal workweek.
• Employees can typically expect to be home on weekends. Occasional weekend travel or emergency service may be required.
• Work will be performed in agricultural retail facilities, fertilizer blending plants, chemical processing facilities, and industrial environments.
• Position requires the ability to work around electrical equipment, industrial machinery, and agricultural processing systems while following all applicable safety procedures.
• Must be comfortable working both independently in the field and collaboratively with internal teams.
• Work schedules may vary based on installation timelines, seasonal customer demands, and service needs

Requirements

Required
• Basic understanding of electrical systems and willingness to develop industrial controls and automation skills.
• Mechanical aptitude and familiarity with basic mechanical systems and hand tools.
• Ability to read and understand technical documentation and willingness to learn electrical schematics and wiring diagrams.
• Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving abilities.
• Ability to work independently, determine solutions, and complete assigned work.
• Strong communication, organizational, and customer service skills.
• Ability to communicate technical information clearly to customers and other team members.
• Basic computer proficiency and ability to use service software and electronic documentation.
• Valid driver's license and ability to travel regularly throughout the assigned service territory.
• Willingness to adapt to changing schedules and take ownership of customer issues.

Preferred
• Previous hands-on experience with industrial electrical controls and automation systems.
• Experience troubleshooting electrical control circuits, motor starters, relays, sensors, and related industrial equipment.
• Working knowledge of PLC-controlled equipment and HMI-based automation systems
• Experience with PLC programming, troubleshooting, or software modifications.
• Experience working with variable frequency drives (VFDs), industrial networking, or automation communication protocols.
• Familiarity with industrial instrumentation, including flow meters, load cells, level sensors, and process control devices.
• Experience with agricultural equipment, dry fertilizer systems, liquid chemical processing, or industrial batching operations.
• Previous experience performing field service, equipment commissioning, or industrial automation startups.
• Understanding of three-phase electrical systems, motor controls, and industrial electrical safety practices.

Additional Expectations
The successful candidate will demonstrate a willingness to continually learn, adapt to new technologies, and represent KSi with professionalism. We are looking for someone who takes pride in their work, enjoys solving challenging technical problems, and understands the importance of keeping customers operational.

This position is an important part of the continued growth of the AgriChem Business Unit and will have opportunities to develop technical expertise as our automation offerings expand

Benefits

  • 401(k)
  • 401(k) matching
  • Health Insurance
  • Dental Insurance
  • Vision Insurance
  • Life Insurance
  • Paid Time Off
  • Flexible Schedule​

title: Events Intern
description:

title: Advisor, CFP
description:
Moneta is an independent Registered Investment Advisor (RIA) wholly focused on going further for our clients. We are one firm with many solutions and we provide a full spectrum of financial advisory services, but our true purpose is centered on building relationships and providing exceptional service to our clients around the globe. For that reason, we’ve built an entrepreneurial business model organized around our clients. Our Partner-led teams are empowered to serve only in the best interest of their clients. Plus, our independence means that we are never beholden to stakeholders or parent companies. We also have the unique ability to trace our history back nearly 150 years, demonstrating our ability to evolve to meet the needs of those we serve.

Job Summary

Join our dynamic team as a Financial Advisor and help clients navigate their financial journeys toward prosperity and security. As a trusted guide, you will provide personalized financial strategies, investment advice, and comprehensive planning, empowering individuals to achieve their financial goals. Leverage your expertise to build strong client relationships, analyze market trends, and deliver tailored solutions that drive financial success. If you're passionate about making a meaningful impact in the world of finance, we invite you to be part of our dedicated team.

Essential Responsibilities

  • Conducting In-depth Financial Analysis: Perform thorough analyses of clients' financial situations, including tax implications, investment strategies, retirement planning, and estate planning.
  • Specialized Investment Strategies: Work closely with the Investment Team to develop and recommend investment strategies that align with the client's specific needs, risk tolerance, and financial goals, taking into consideration their unique technical circumstances.
  • Tax Planning and Optimization: Advise clients on tax-efficient strategies to minimize their tax liabilities, considering various tax codes and regulations that may apply to their specific situation.
  • Retirement and Pension Planning: Assist clients in creating comprehensive retirement plans, including assessing various retirement vehicles, analyzing pension options, and projecting retirement income.
  • Estate and Inheritance Planning: Work closely with the Estate Planning Team to provide guidance on estate planning, including the creation of wills, trusts, and other vehicles to protect and distribute assets according to the client's wishes.
  • Risk Management and Insurance Recommendations: Evaluate clients' insurance needs, including life, disability, long-term care, and liability insurance, and make recommendations to mitigate risks.
  • Business Succession Planning: Advise business owners on succession planning, helping them prepare for the transfer of their business interests to heirs or potential buyers.
  • Customized Financial Reports and Presentations: Utilizing firm platforms including Orion and Money Guide Pro, generate detailed reports and presentations tailored to each client's technical requirements, providing clear explanations of complex financial concepts.
  • Compliance and Regulatory Adherence: Ensure that all recommendations and actions comply with industry regulations, legal requirements, and ethical standards.
  • Collaboration with Legal and Tax Professionals: Work closely with attorneys, accountants, and other professionals to coordinate comprehensive financial strategies for clients.
  • Continuous Learning and Professional Development: Stay updated with advancements in technical financial planning, attending seminars, workshops, and pursuing relevant certifications.
  • Maintaining Client Relationships: Build and nurture long-term relationships with clients, demonstrating trustworthiness, integrity, and reliability in managing their complex financial affairs.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree required
  • Minimum 3-5 years working as a client service advisor or related role
  • CFP, CFA, CPA/PFS with tax expertise, or JD with estate planning experience is a plus
  • A Series 65 or combination of a Series 7 and Series 66 licensing arerequiredwithin60 days of hire if a CFP or CFA designation is not previously held
  • CFP or CFA designation is required within 3 years of hire if not previously held
  • Must be authorized to work in the United States

Additional Information

Moneta is committed to providing the best possible care for our employees; part of this care includes offering comprehensive benefits that enhance the well-being of employees and their families:

  • Paid holidays
  • Paid time off (PTO)
  • Employer cost-shared medical and dental insurance
  • Employer-paid short-term disability, long-term disability, AD&D insurance, and basic life insurance
  • 401k Match – 50% of employee contributions up to 6% of compensation
  • Discretionary annual profit-sharing bonus
  • Paid parental leave
  • Professional development reimbursement
  • Paid volunteer time off (VTO)
  • Employee referral incentive bonus program
  • Onsite wellness programs & rewards
  • Employee engagement activities

Moneta is a fiduciary fee-only Registered Investment Advisory firm and unable to hold securities licenses with the exception of Series 65. We also do not allow outside business activities, insurance commissions, and/or trails.

title: Head of Quality Engineering
description:
At ABB, we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. You’ll be empowered to lead, supported to grow, and proud of the impact we create together. Join us and help run what runs the world.

This position reports to:

Group Research Portfolio Manager

__

Mission of the Role

In this role, you will have the opportunity to conceptualize, identify, explore, and implement world-leading technologies, products, and systems within and across product groups/divisions/business areas. Each day, you will ensure delivery of results, foster innovation, and strategically develop and secure Research and Development (R&D) capabilities with a cost-effective footprint. You will also showcase your expertise by coordinating at various management levels as well as with external partners to enhance and secure ABB´s global position and profitability in the medium and long term.


This role is contributing to the Automation Process Control Platform (AUPCP) globally. Main stakeholders are PCP R&D management team.

The work model for the role is: hybrid or remote.


Responsibilities

  • Provide reliable and scalable shared capabilities for building, integrating, testing and assessing products and product lines across Solution Trains (SLTs) and Agile Release Trains (ARTs).
  • Own shared quality engineering infrastructure and practices.
  • Be responsible for the independent qualification of product and product line deliveries across PCP.
  • Lead the quality engineering team, including test engineering, DevOps and configuration management.
  • Drive the shift from release-based system testing to continuous testing integrated into development.

Requirements

  • M.Sc. or higher degree in Software Development, Engineering or a related field.
  • 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in R&D or a related field.
  • Proven experience leading a complex, global organization with accountability for verification and validation of products and quality compliance.
  • Proven experience implementing continuous testing / quality engineering transformations in one or more companies.
  • Understanding of products, product lifecycle and quality, with the ability to connect technical excellence with business and customer value.
  • Understanding of software verification methodologies, automated pipelines and infrastructure management.
  • Financial, stakeholder and people leadership skills, with experience managing resources and developing high-performing teams across cultures and geographical locations.
  • Hands-on experience with Linux and Kubernetes environments (mandatory).
  • Proven experience driving Quality Engineering (QE) transformation, including leading organizational and process change.
  • Strong communication and cross-cultural collaboration skills, with fluent written and spoken English.

About ABB's Process Control Platform (PCP)

Process Control Platform (PCP) is the technological foundation of Automation's business area, delivering world-class Distributed Control Systems (DCS). Combining proven expertise with innovation, PCP shapes the future of automation and enables industrial digital transformation. by developing safe and reliable control systems.

Its portfolio includes leading systems: ABB Ability™ System 800xA®, ABB Ability™ Symphony® Plus, Freelance and Aprol, along with safety, industrial edge and PLC automation solutions. It also covers a broad base of heritage systems, including Advant Master, MOD 300, Harmony INFI 90 and Melody. Building on this installed base and deep automation expertise, PCP is advancing the next generation of automation through Automation Extended and digital offerings including ABB Ability™ Edgenius and ABB Ability™ Field Information Manager. By expanding the traditional boundaries of automation and building a broader process automation ecosystem, PCP helps customers improve operational performance, extend system lifecycles and outrun their challenges. As a value-generating partner, PCP ensures that its portfolio remains comprehensive and competitive, supports previously released systems and evolves with market demands through close collaboration with the divisions. The organization also manages Quality and Operations and provides essential support in product training, sales enablement and marketing communications.

At its core, PCP fosters a diverse and inclusive environment where employees are empowered to innovate, grow and make a lasting impact on customers, industry and society.

title: Database Analyst / Administrator
description:
Title: Database Analyst / Administrator
Location: Remote, United States
Schedule: Flexible; shift-based and on-call coverage as needed
Pay: $140,000 – $175,000 annually, commensurate with experience

ROLE
KMRG, LLC (KMRG) is a federal services company that hires talented professionals to support Government agencies and the communities they serve. We are hiring a remote Database Analyst / Administrator to support cloud-based database operations and data modernization initiatives for the Administrative Office of the US Courts (AOUSC).

In this role, you will administer production databases, support AWS and Databricks environments, troubleshoot issues, and strengthen data integration, modeling, and analytics capabilities. You will work with technical teams and stakeholders to maintain reliable, secure, and efficient data services.
Applications will be reviewed as they are received. Apply today!

RESPONSIBILITIES
Database Operations & Production Support
  • Install, configure, administer, and maintain mission-critical production database environments
  • Monitor database performance, troubleshoot incidents, and restore services with development and operations teams
  • Perform root-cause analysis and improve database reliability, performance, security, and scalability
Cloud Database & Data Architecture
  • Administer AWS-managed databases, including Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, and support Databricks environments
  • Develop stored procedures, jobs, views, tables, and other database objects using SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS)
  • Design dimensional data models, including star and snowflake schemas, fact and dimension tables, and data marts
  • Support migration of legacy on-premises databases to cloud and hybrid platforms
Data Integration, Analytics & Collaboration
  • Build and deploy ETL packages through CI/CD pipelines and version-control workflows
  • Develop and implement database policies and standards for data integrity, quality, security, and administration, including data accuracy validation
  • Analyze data from multiple sources using statistical analysis, data mining, and predictive modeling to identify trends, inform decisions, and develop KPI visualizations
  • Work with product owners and users to translate business needs into technical requirements and document workflows
  • Participate in Agile planning, daily scrums, peer code reviews, and technical collaboration
  • Use Atlassian development tools; index system and application logs in Splunk and create dashboards, alerts, and reports
REQUIRED BACKGROUND
  • Seven (7) or more years of database maintenance, database analysis, or related experience
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Programming, Computer Engineering, or related field; equivalent experience may be considered
  • Experience supporting production databases, including shift-based and on-call support
  • Proficiency with AWS database technologies (e.g. Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL and other AWS-managed data services)
  • Experience working with Databricks
  • Experience installing, configuring, and administering database environments
  • Knowledge of data warehousing, dimensional modeling, data mapping, data flow diagrams, and data marts
  • Experience architecting and implementing cloud-based database solutions
  • Experience migrating on-premises data to multi-cloud or hybrid-cloud environments
  • Strong analytical, technical, and problem-solving skills
  • Ability to work independently, prioritize tasks, and meet deadlines

Resilience Behavioral Health is a behavioral health treatment organization focused on providing compassionate, individualized care to individuals experiencing mental health and substance use challenges. title: Patient Financial Counselor
description:
Patient Financial Counselor
Description: The Patient Financial Counselor is responsible for supporting the financial experience of patients throughout the continuum of care within a large, multispecialty physician practice. This position serves as a primary resource for patients regarding insurance benefits, estimated out-of-pocket expenses, payment arrangements, and financial assistance options.

The Patient Financial Counselor plays a critical role in the organization's revenue cycle by proactively identifying and addressing financial barriers to care, promoting financial transparency, improving patient collections, and reducing preventable patient accounts receivable. This role collaborates closely with scheduling, registration, clinical operations, prior authorization, billing, and revenue cycle teams to facilitate financial clearance and ensure a seamless patient experience.

The ideal candidate demonstrates strong financial acumen, exceptional communication skills, compassion, and the ability to navigate complex insurance and billing matters while balancing patient advocacy with the financial objectives of the organization.

Responsibilities:
Patient Financial Counseling and Education
  • Educate patients regarding insurance coverage, deductibles, copayments, coinsurance, out-of-pocket maximums, and potential financial responsibility.
  • Provide clear, accurate, and compassionate explanations of patient estimates.
  • Proactively engage patients prior to scheduled services to discuss anticipated financial obligations, available payment options, and collection of estimated liabilities.
  • Assist patients in understanding insurance-related financial responsibilities, including noncovered services.
  • Address patient financial concerns, questions, and disputes professionally, escalating complex issues when appropriate.
  • Promote financial transparency while maintaining a positive, patient-centered experience.

Financial Clearance and Pre-Service Collections
  • Review scheduled appointments, procedures, and services to identify patients requiring financial counseling or financial clearance.
  • Collaborate with scheduling, clinic staff registration, and authorization teams to identify and resolve financial barriers prior to the date of service.
  • Verify available insurance and financial information to support accurate determination of patient responsibility.
  • Prepare, review, and communicate patient cost estimates for diagnostic testing, procedures, and other specialty services.
  • Proactively contact patients with anticipated out-of-pocket expenses to review payment expectations and available financial arrangements.
  • Facilitate collection of applicable copayments, deductibles, coinsurance, and other patient-responsible amounts prior to or at the time of service, consistent with organizational policies and applicable regulations.
  • Identify potential financial clearance issues and coordinate timely resolution with appropriate departments.
  • Document financial counseling activities, patient communications, payment commitments, and unresolved issues within designated systems.

Revenue Cycle Operations and Collaboration
  • Work collaboratively with clinical departments, practice leadership, scheduling, registration, coding, billing, and other revenue cycle functions to support efficient patient financial processes.
  • Support standardized financial counseling and collection workflows across multiple specialties and practice locations.
  • Identify recurring patient billing concerns, insurance issues, and operational barriers that negatively impact financial clearance or collections.
  • Communicate opportunities for workflow improvements and participate in initiatives to enhance revenue cycle performance.
  • Assist with patient account research, financial inquiries, and escalated billing concerns requiring coordination across departments.
  • Maintain familiarity with specialty-specific services, insurance requirements, and financial workflows.
  • Support implementation of organizational policies related to patient financial responsibility, payment arrangements, and financial assistance.
  • Participate in departmental meetings, training, process improvement activities, and other assigned revenue cycle initiatives.

Performance Management and Accountability
  • Meet established productivity, quality, and service expectations related to financial counseling, financial clearance, and patient collections.
  • Support achievement of departmental performance indicators, including:
    • Pre-service financial clearance completion rates.
    • Patient estimate accuracy and timely communication.
    • Pre-service and point-of-service collection performance.
    • Patient payment plan enrollment and adherence.
    • Reduction in aged patient accounts receivable.
    • Timely resolution of patient financial inquiries.
    • Documentation accuracy and compliance with established workflows.
  • Maintain accurate records of patient outreach, financial counseling outcomes, and collection activities.
  • Prioritize assigned work queues and patient accounts to ensure timely follow-up and resolution.
  • Demonstrate accountability for assigned responsibilities while maintaining a high standard of patient service.

Compliance and Patient Confidentiality
  • Ensure all financial counseling and collection activities comply with HIPAA, applicable federal and state regulations, payer requirements, and organizational policies.
  • Maintain working knowledge of applicable CMS requirements, patient financial protections, and No Surprises Act provisions.
  • Communicate patient financial obligations accurately and transparently, including applicable Good Faith Estimate requirements.
  • Maintain confidentiality of protected health information and sensitive patient financial information.
  • Follow established policies regarding financial assistance, payment arrangements, collection practices, and account adjustments.
  • Exercise sound judgment and professionalism when discussing sensitive financial matters with patients and families.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned to support the overall objectives of the Revenue Cycle department.


Requirements:
  • Strong understanding of healthcare revenue cycle operations, including patient access, insurance verification, patient financial responsibility, billing, and collections.
  • Working knowledge of commercial insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, managed care plans, and patient cost-sharing requirements.
  • Ability to interpret insurance benefits, explain complex financial information, and communicate anticipated patient expenses accurately.
  • Demonstrated ability to conduct sensitive financial conversations with professionalism, empathy, and discretion.
  • Strong customer service, interpersonal, problem-solving, and conflict-resolution skills.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to interact effectively with patients, families, providers, and internal departments.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and maintain productivity in a fast-paced, high-volume, multispecialty practice environment.
  • Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and commitment to accurate documentation.
  • Proficiency with electronic health records, practice management systems, patient accounting platforms, and Microsoft Office applications.
  • Ability to independently research patient accounts, identify discrepancies, and coordinate appropriate resolutions.
  • Understanding of patient payment plans, financial assistance programs, and healthcare collection practices.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with multidisciplinary teams.
  • Commitment to patient-centered service, financial transparency, and continuous process improvement.
  • Experience with athenahealth or comparable electronic health record and practice management systems preferred.

Education and Certifications
  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Associate degree in healthcare administration, business administration, finance, or a related field preferred.
  • Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, business administration, finance, or a related field preferred.
  • Certified Revenue Cycle Representative (CRCR) through the Healthcare Financial Management Association (HFMA) preferred.
  • Additional certifications in healthcare revenue cycle management, patient access, or medical billing preferred.
Experience:
  • Minimum of two (2) years of experience in healthcare revenue cycle operations, patient financial services, medical billing, patient access, or a related healthcare financial role required.
  • Experience in patient financial counseling, insurance benefit interpretation, payment collections, or financial clearance strongly preferred.
  • Experience working in a large, multispecialty physician practice, ambulatory care organization, or integrated healthcare delivery system preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience discussing patient financial obligations, establishing payment arrangements, and resolving complex billing inquiries.
  • Familiarity with Medicare, Medicaid, commercial insurance, and specialty-specific billing requirements preferred.
  • Experience utilizing electronic health records, practice management systems, and patient accounting work queues preferred.
  • Experience with athenahealth preferred.
Physical Requirements
  • Work consistently requires walking, standing, sitting, lifting, reaching, stooping, bending, pushing, and pulling.
  • Must be able to lift and support weight of 35 pounds
  • Ability to concentrate on details.
  • Use of computer for long periods of time.

title: IT Support Technician
description:
IT Support Technician

Dougherty Manufacturing - Edgewater, Florida

Full-time, onsite - Non-exempt, hourly - $38,000 to $42,000 per year

Reports to: IT Lead


ABOUT THE ROLE


Dougherty Manufacturing is hiring a full-time IT Support Technician for our

Edgewater, Florida plant. This is an onsite, entry-level to junior role for

someone with about a year of hands-on experience who wants to grow well past

the help desk. You will be the hands in the building: the person who walks to

the machine, the printer or the production floor and fixes it, working

alongside an IT Lead who handles monitoring, diagnosis and higher-tier

remediation remotely.


We run approximately 80 Windows endpoints, six servers, a plant-wide network

and the Infor VISUAL ERP system across an office and an active manufacturing

floor. No two days look the same.


WHAT YOU WILL DO


- Tier 1 and Tier 2 deskside and help desk support across the office and the

production floor.

- Act as onsite remote hands for the IT Lead during remote diagnosis and

remediation.

- Microsoft 365 and Active Directory user tasks: password resets, account

lockouts, multi-factor authentication, user provisioning and deprovisioning.

- Support printers, displays, docking stations, headsets, IP phones and

workstation moves, adds and changes.

- Image, deploy and decommission Windows workstations and laptops from a

standard build, and keep pre-imaged spares ready for break/fix.

- Run the Windows 10 to Windows 11 endpoint refresh: build, migrate, deploy

and retire.

- Patch panel terminations, structured cabling, cable management, server racks

and the IT stockroom.

- Keep ticket documentation and asset inventory records accurate and current.


WHAT YOU NEED


- One year of hands-on IT support experience, including working a ticket queue

in a service desk or help desk environment.

- Accurate execution of directed remediation and precise reporting, including

verbatim error messages. Diagnosis is performed remotely and depends on what

you relay from site.

- Windows desktop troubleshooting: installation, reimaging, drivers, boot

problems and network connectivity.

- Computer hardware repair: memory, storage and power supply replacement.

- Able to work routine requests independently: passwords, lockouts, print

services and new-hire onboarding.

- Triage judgment, including knowing when to escalate.

- Comfortable in a manufacturing environment, willing to wear PPE, able to lift

approximately 50 pounds. Valid driver's license.


NICE TO HAVE


CompTIA A+ certification or active progress toward it. Exposure to Active

Directory, Microsoft 365 administration, networking or Linux. Any experience

in manufacturing, warehouse or industrial IT.


SCHEDULE


Monday through Friday, onsite at our Edgewater plant. An early start is

preferred so that IT support is available when first shift begins. Some

after-hours and weekend work, scheduled in advance and paid as overtime.


WHAT WE OFFER


Exposure well beyond the ticket queue. You will work on servers,

virtualization, backup, endpoint security, ERP support and plant networking,

with direct mentorship from the IT Lead. Certification costs for CompTIA A+

and Network+ are funded. This is a role built to turn a junior technician into

a capable systems administrator.


Compensation: $38,000 to $42,000 per year, depending on experience.

Non-exempt, hourly, overtime eligible.


ALSO SEARCHED AS


IT Support Technician, Help Desk Technician, Desktop Support Technician, IT

Technician, Computer Technician, Tier 1 Support, Tier 2 Support, Service Desk

Technician, Field Service Technician, Junior Systems Administrator, Technical

Support Specialist, PC Technician.


Serving Edgewater, New Smyrna Beach, Port Orange, Oak Hill, Daytona Beach,

South Daytona, Ormond Beach and Volusia County.


Skills: Windows 10, Windows 11, Microsoft 365, Office 365, Active Directory,

Entra ID, help desk, service desk, ticketing system, password reset, MFA, user

provisioning, imaging, deployment, hardware troubleshooting, break/fix,

printer support, networking, structured cabling, patch panel, CompTIA A+,

Network+, manufacturing IT, ERP support, Infor VISUAL.

title: SPED Educational Assistant - Registered Behavior Tech
description:
Job Summary:

This position will implement behavior plans created by a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA by directly working with students exhibiting behavioral challenges to teach new skills, address problematic behaviors, and monitor progress using applied behavior analysis (ABA) techniques. Primary responsibility is to collect data on student behavior, implement treatment plans, and collaborate with other staff to support positive behavior changes.

Qualifications:
  • Certificate, bachelor’s, or associate’s degree in behavioral health or related field.
  • ABA Therapist certification preferred.
  • Must be eligible for a Wisconsin DPI-issued Special Education Educational Assistant license.
  • Proven work experience as a Behavioral Technician or similar role for a minimum of 1-year.
  • Must meet Title One ParaProfessional Highly Qualified Requirements.
  • CPR/First Aid Certification (provided by District).
  • Pro-Act Certification (provided by the District).

Duties/Responsibilities:
  • Follow a personalized behavior plan designed by the District’s BCBA, providing one-on-one support to students by teaching new skills like communication, social interaction, self-care, and adaptive behaviors through positive reinforcement strategies.
  • Accurately record student behaviors during the day, graphing data to track progress and identify areas of improvement, and using this information to adjust interventions as needed.
  • Engaging with students in various activities and settings to practice targeted skills, providing prompts, and reinforcement as necessary, and managing challenging behaviors using appropriate techniques.
  • Maintaining open communication with the BCBA supervisor, reporting progress, discussing concerns, and collaborating with staff and other professionals involved with the student’s plan.
  • Under the direction of the District BCBA, help to educate families on the principles of ABA and how to implement intervention strategies at home to support student progress.
  • Actively supports the West Allis-West Milwaukee School District’s Strategic Plan.
  • Attend meetings and participate in professional development opportunities as required.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:
  • Compassionate nature and empathy towards students in challenging situations is required.
  • Effective oral and written communication skills are required.
  • Must be self-directed.

description:
Sr. Business Director - Strategy & Analytics (Enterprise Supplier Management)

Enterprise Supplier Management (ESM) governs the end-to-end third-party lifecycle from sourcing and onboarding to monitoring, overseeing the annual spend across thousands of partners to power Capital One’s strategic and core business operations. Backed by executive sponsorship from the C-Suite to our Chief Product Officer, we are actively reimagining what modern procurement looks like, capitalizing on deep tech and As the head of our Strategy & Analytics team spanning Data, Financial, and Business Analysts, you will define and deploy our enterprise third-party strategy, while helping the team capitalize on existing opportunities from recently completed integrations and related tech investments.

As a Senior Business Director at Capital One, you will apply your strategic and analytical skills to major company challenges. You’ll team with world-class professionals to develop and test strategies that ultimately impact the bottom line. And you will do it all in a collaborative environment that values your insight, encourages you to take on new responsibility, promotes continuous learning, and rewards innovation.

General Responsibilities:

  • Strategic leadership: Develop business strategies that will drive growth, profitability, and competitive success for Capital One in the face of shifting consumer and regulatory demands
  • Leadership: May manage and develop multiple analysts. Coaching and mentoring associates with a goal of developing and retaining talent at Capital One
  • Product: Develop and implement new product and pricing strategies for various lending products; lead product level data modeling/analytics
  • Marketing: Lead direct-to-consumer marketing efforts for select products, and strategic intent for products distributed through the retail channel. Build targeted insights to inform the design and development of new customer experiences, as well as breakthrough technology and concepts designed to deliver on new go-to-market strategies
  • Credit Risk: Drive step-change improvements in credit performance by connecting drivers of future consumer credit trends to historical behavior, creating risk models, and testing hypotheses using rigorous monitoring and analysis
  • Execution: Manage and sequence delivery of business intent, build business requirements and execute against the product strategy. Oversee multiple projects and programs concurrently
  • Partnership: Work closely with colleagues across Capital One including: IT, Sales, Operations, Finance and others to drive improvement in quality, volume, service, and profitability
  • Strategic; analytic orientation: A proven track record of decision making and problem solving based on analytics. Conceptual thinking skills must be complemented by a strong quantitative orientation, given that a large part of the business is based on rigorous analytic marketing & credit risk management
  • Strong business judgment, leadership and integrity: They should be a tenacious decision maker, able to bring a healthy, aggressive, yet responsible approach to business
  • Solid people leadership experience: Ability to build and leverage the capabilities of a high-performing team, as well as business partners across the enterprise. They should foster innovation, drive critical decisions, hold business partners accountable, and be able to consistently deliver results
  • Strong executive communication skills: Impeccable written and oral communication credentials, coupled with strategic influencing skills and the ability to drive agreement through intellect, interpersonal and negotiation skills
  • Clear results orientation: display an intense focus on achieving both short and long term goals. They should be able to drive and execute an agenda in an uncertain and fluid environment
  • Successful track record of thriving in a fast paced, entrepreneurial and dynamic environment. Previous consulting experience is a plus
