description:
Transitional Case Manager, Exeter
Direct Service - (OPSEU)
Part-Time, Contract (End Date: April 30, 2028)
This posting is the result of an upcoming vacancy.
Exeter, ON (South Huron Zone)
- Application Deadline: November 24, 2026 -

We believe that everyone has the right to live with dignity, autonomy and independence in our community.

Our Case Management Program embodies this belief by supporting individuals experiencing mental illness or addictions to live as independently as possible, while working collaboratively with a Transitional Case Manager to build their support systems. As a Transitional Case Manager, you’ll also focus on assisting clients with connecting to their community and teaching life skills to help them to achieve their recovery goals.

Consider revitalizing your career and making a difference in your community by joining our team!

WHAT WE'RE OFFERING:

  • What you'll be making – Starting rate for this role is $27.14 per hour (Level 1 – Direct Service), with a wage differential, based on regulation ($30.01 per hour for Level 1 – Direct Service, Regulated):
    • Successful candidates who are registered with one of the designated professional colleges (e.g. OCSWSSW, CNO, COTO, CRPO, CPSO, or CPO) will receive the wage differential for regulation
    • Successful external applicants will start at Level 1, with grid progression based on seniority up to Level 8 ($34.41 per hour for non-regulated, and $37.26 per hour for regulated); for internal applicants, grid level placement will occur as per the Collective Agreement
    • Premiums of $2.00 per hour will be applied for eligible Evening/Night (8:00pm – 7:00am) and Weekend Shifts.
  • When you'll work – 40 hours biweekly; Monday to Friday day shifts, between the hours of 8:30am-4:00pm with a 30-min unpaid meal break
  • Your pension plan – Immediately eligible for optional enrolment in the Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan (HOOPP)
  • What your benefits will be – 9% in lieu of benefits

HOW YOU WILL BE MAKING A DIFFERENCE:
Assessment – in collaboration with the client:

  • Assist with short term crisis management by providing an urgent/emergent response to individuals in need of case management supports
  • Engage with clients on a short-term basis to support their immediate needs
  • In collaboration with the client, conduct a variety of assessments (skills, functional ability, needs, barriers, etc.)
  • Assess the adequacy of resources/supports currently available to the client
  • Determine the impact of psychiatric symptoms on functioning
  • Identify risk factors related to client and staff safety as well as relapse
  • Assess barriers to successful community living (e.g. treatment options, transportation, finances, etc.)
  • Obtain information, as needed, from other relevant sources
  • Ensure the assessment incorporates cultural and ethnic factors
  • Identify areas requiring additional assessment

Individualized Goal Setting and Rehabilitation Planning -- Utilizing the information obtained through the assessment process and in collaboration with the client:

  • Assist the client to identify their personal goals and preferences and utilize standardized tool (GAIN, OCAN, etc.)
  • Design rehab plans based on client needs, goals and preferences
  • Assist the client to navigate systems and connect to appropriate resources
  • Assist the client to explore options and consequences of different choices
  • Build on the client’s personal strengths, abilities and resources
  • Help clients work towards their vision of a positive personal future
  • Help clients identify practical strategies for achieving their vision
  • Ensure issues related to transportation are addressed, incorporated into the rehab plan and are consistent with organizational policies and practices
  • Work in partnership with the client in all aspects of planning
  • Identify intervention strategies to meet goals
  • Establish an intervention plan which includes expectations and responsibilities of the client, Case Manager, other

Implementation of Rehabilitation Plan -- Based on identified goals and intervention strategies:

  • Provide individual skill teaching and/or support the client to obtain the necessary skills training from other sources
  • Provide needed information and education about mental illness, coping skills, services, resources, self-help and consumer initiatives/supports
  • Utilize basic communication and intervention skills, supported by empirical validity, practice guidelines and relevant standards of care for different interventions
  • Encourage and facilitate personal growth and development towards rehabilitation and recovery
  • Motivate the client to learn new skills and behaviours
  • Build on client’s personal strengths and adjust interventions based on individual response
  • Support the client to access needed resources
  • Assist the client to identify and connect with personal/natural supports
  • Meet with the client regularly to work on specific goals until other permanent supports are in place

WHAT YOU'LL NEED TO APPLY:

Police Vulnerable Sector Check Requirements
Successful candidates must have a Police Vulnerable Sector Check completed in the last six months. Interested applicants who reside in the City of London and are in need of a Police Vulnerable Sector Check (PVSC) are encouraged to apply for one as soon as possible as PVSCs in the City of London are currently taking approximately 2 weeks to be processed and offers of employment cannot be made without receipt of a PVSC.

We require the following qualifications:

  • Diploma or degree in a health, social service or related discipline (primary proof of credentials will be required during the hiring process i.e. original degree/diploma or official transcript)
  • Current, satisfactory Police Vulnerable Sector Check (PVSC)
  • Valid Driver’s License: G class required
  • Transportation of clients in personal vehicle required; two million-dollar ($2 000 000.00) liability insurance required
  • Demonstrated ability to attend work regularly

We prefer the following qualifications:

  • Experience working with individuals with a serious mental illness
  • Knowledge of serious mental illness and its impact on clients
  • Excellent knowledge of community resources in the Thames Valley region
  • Knowledge/experience working within the criminal justice system
  • Bilingual in both official languages, preferred; Une préférence sera accordée aux personnes possédant des compétences dans les deux langues officielles du Canada

INTERNAL APPLICANTS: To be considered as an internal applicant, current staff members are reminded to apply using their @cmhatv.ca or @slwar.ca email address.

Get your application in by – November 24, 2026

Our recruitment process allows us to learn about your previous work experience, your qualifications and your commitment to fulfilling our vision. While we appreciate the interest of all applicants, only those individuals being considered for a position will be personally contacted by someone from the interview team.

We welcome and encourage applications from all members of our community including persons of any gender, gender identity, gender expression, or sexual orientation, persons with disabilities, Indigenous persons, and members of visible minorities. If you require accommodations related to a disability at any point during the recruitment process, please contact Human.Resources@cmhatv.ca

title: Culinary Manager
description:
ABOUT TOPGOLF

Topgolf is a sports entertainment company that has changed how millions of people experience golf and where you can build a serious career. Our venues are high-energy, high-volume environments where performance matters and results are visible. Every day, we bring together golf, food and beverages, events, and entertainment into one experience that keeps guests coming back.


WHAT WE’RE SEEKING

Do you hold the line on quality even when it is busy? Can you lead a kitchen team through a high-volume service and still have the team better when the shift ends than when it started?


We are looking for a Culinary Manager who leads from the front. Someone who understands food cost and portion control, coaches their team through the work, and takes genuine ownership of the kitchen's performance. Consistency is not lucky. It is what happens when a leader pays attention.

If you run a tight, proud kitchen, this is where those matter.

THE ROLE

The Culinary Manager supports the Executive Culinary Manager in leading all kitchen operations, ensuring best-in-class culinary experiences for every guest. This role requires both culinary expertise and the ability to lead, coach, and develop the kitchen team.

The Culinary Manager may be responsible for day-to-day line operations or events execution. They supervise the kitchen team, manage inventory and product ordering, enforce safety and sanitation standards, and maintain the quality and consistency Topgolf guests expect.

As a leader of a high-energy, guest-facing venue, this role requires a flexible schedule including evenings, weekends, and holidays, with availability to work extended hours during peak periods, special events, and high-volume seasons.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

Lead Kitchen Operations

• Supervise the kitchen team in delivering best-in-class culinary experiences every shift

• Coach and develop Team members and drive engagement across the kitchen

• Delegate tasks effectively and follow up to ensure completion and quality

• Manage day-to-day line operations or events execution as assigned

Maintain Culinary Standards

• Select and develop recipes to corporate approval and standardize production for consistent quality

• Establish and maintain presentation techniques and quality standards

• Plan and cost menus for special events and chef-choice occasions

• Ensure proper equipment operation, maintenance, and cleanliness

Manage Costs and Inventory

• Monitor inventory levels and purchase product within budgetary guidelines

• Maintain food and labor costs according to budget, with a solid understanding of COGS

• Oversee safety and sanitation in the kitchen in compliance with all regulations

Contribute to Team Culture

• Demonstrate Topgolf's core values: Fun, One Team, Excellence, Courage, and Caring

• Support the Executive Culinary Manager in building a high-performance kitchen team

• Participate in team development and model the standards expected of all kitchen team members

CORE COMPETENCIES FOR SUCCESS

Drives Results | Consistently achieving results, even under tough circumstances.

• Demonstrates a strong drive to achieve consistent culinary quality and operational results

• Drives tasks to successful completion each shift — no corners cut

• Shows determination in the face of high volume, obstacles, or short-staffed situations

• Sets high standards for own performance and inspires the same in the team

Customer Focus | Building strong customer relationships and delivering customer-centric solutions.

• Ensures every dish that leaves the kitchen meets or exceeds guest expectations

• Uses guest and internal feedback to continuously improve food quality and presentation

• Independently anticipates and adjusts to evolving event and service needs

• Follows up on any culinary feedback to ensure issues are fully resolved

Decision Quality | Making good and timely decisions that keep the organization moving forward.

• Demonstrates good judgment in routine kitchen decisions — prep, production, quality, and staffing

• Makes sound independent decisions in urgent situations such as equipment failures or staffing gaps

• Considers various inputs and trade-offs to arrive at effective decisions during high-volume service

• Uses good judgment about when to act independently and when to escalate an issue to the Executive Culinary Manager

Communicates Effectively | Developing and delivering multi-mode communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences.

• Communicates clearly and professionally with kitchen team members and venue leadership

• Shares information and production updates with the team in a timely manner

• Listens attentively to the Executive Culinary Manager's direction and translates it into action

• Documents kitchen operations, production notes, and inventory clearly and accurately

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 2+ years of culinary management or supervisory experience in a high-volume restaurant, hotel, or entertainment environment.
  • Culinary degree, professional culinary certification, or equivalent training and experience in a high-volume full-service kitchen and events-driven environment preferred
  • Must be 21 years of age or older as required by state or local law

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Let us be real — this is not your typical desk job! Here is what you will need to do to thrive in this role:

  • Ability to remain on your feet and in motion for extended periods throughout the shift, including standing, walking, and navigating a fast-paced kitchen environment; this role operates in a high-volume kitchen and requires sustained physical stamina throughout the duration of each shift
  • Ability to lift, carry, and move items up to 50 pounds independently and up to 75 pounds with assistance, including food products, equipment, supplies, and delivery transport across multiple levels of the venue
  • Ability to navigate stairs, ramps, and multi-level areas of the venue when transporting food, coordinating events, or overseeing service delivery
  • Ability to work in varying temperature environments on a frequent basis, including hot kitchen conditions, walk-in coolers, and freezers
  • Ability to perform repetitive hand and wrist motions including cutting, stirring, lifting, and operating kitchen equipment throughout the shift
  • Ability to communicate clearly and effectively in a high-energy venue environment that may include moderate to high levels of background noise
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, high-volume environment while maintaining focus, food safety standards, and quality under pressure

Sounds like a fit? We cannot wait to meet with you!


Salary range: $57,904 - $70,672


BENEFITS

Free Play & 1/2 price food! Health, dental, vision, 401(k) team member match, free mental well-being platform – and that’s just for starters for those who qualify. View team member benefits here.


ADA

title: Principal Innovation Engineer
description:

Bowler Pons Solutions Consultants, LLC is looking for a talented and turnkey Innovation Engineer (Hardware/Software). Our innovation efforts support clients and industry partners alike in developing agile, responsive, and integrated solutions that help them rapidly mitigate emerging threats. In this role you will be at the core of innovation, with a wide range of responsibilities, including software development, hardware development, integration, rapid prototyping, robotics/autonomous systems, and electronics.
This position is located at our headquarters office/lab facility in Annapolis, MD and will require periodic travel to customer locations and/or the application sites hosting our exciting technology development efforts. Remote work may be authorized on a case-by-case basis, but candidates should plan to be in the office at least four (4) days per week.
As a small business, we offer a unique opportunity to learn, grow, and take ownership of new projects and concepts and influence the direction of the company’s solution development initiatives. We work fast and have big goals and are looking for team members who thrive in a dynamic and forward-looking environment.

Design, develop, document, test, debug, integrate, and maintain application software, systems, and hardware solutions, including hardware and software integration across sensors, platforms, and networks, as part of a comprehensive threat detection and response suite. Lead the internally funded and customer-sponsored technology development efforts leveraging advanced perception sensing, AI/ML toolsets, automated decision support, UI/UX, and other emerging tech and methodologies.

Minimum Required Qualifications

  • US citizenship and the ability to obtain and maintain a DoW SECRET clearance
  • BA or BS degree in Software Engineering/Development, Computer Science, Electrical, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, or related field (may substitute 5+ additional years of experience in at least two of the below role-specific areas for subject-specific degree)

    • 8+ years’ experience working with object-oriented and procedural programming languages (e.g., C#, C++, JavaScript, and/or Python) and frameworks (e.g., .NET Core, Node, or AngularJS)
    • 8+ years’ experience in building applications with modern software development principles, including Containers, Microservices, and Serverless (e.g., VMWare, Docker, Kubernetes)
  • Hands-on experience developing and deploying software in Linux and Windows environments
  • Experience developing software collaboratively utilizing Git and GitLab/GitHub

  • Knowledge of Objected-Oriented Design Philosophy and ability to identify and isolate software requirements

  • Experience working successfully as part of an Agile and/or Lean project team

Additional Desired Qualifications

    • Strong Linux experience, including mastery of topics such as Linux commands, daemons, and firewalls
    • Raspberry Pi, Arduino, and/or equivalent microcontrollers and embedded devices
    • Control system electronics (e.g., servos, relays, PLCs, analog/digital I/O, FPGAs, HMI, power supplies)

    • Autonomous / Unmanned Systems (UxS) (e.g., UAS, USV, UUV, UGV, quadrupeds, bipeds)
    • Computer Vision and Sensor Fusion
    • Cybersecurity, including OWASP secure coding practices
    • Secure Wireless Communications (e.g., 5G/LTE, WiFi 6, RF planning, encryption/decryption, IoT)
  • Experience with developing proposals in support of Small Business Innovation Research (SBIRs)/Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) as well as Request for Information (RFI) and Request for Proposal (RFP) responses
  • Experience standing up DevOps and Continuous Integration and Continuous Development (CI/CD) environments such as Jenkins, GitLab-CI/Runner, and Hudson

title: A&R Internship | Spring 2027 | Atlanta, GA
description:
A&R Internship – Reach Records

General Information
This internship position will run from Jan 12th - May 1st with the possibility of extension. We are offering a pay of $10 per hour for up to 24 hours per week. Below are the requirements and descriptions for the role. Please read through all of the descriptions and apply if you meet the requirements.

Overview
Reach Records is looking for an A&R Intern to support our A&R team across artist development, content, and day-to-day operations. This role is ideal for a creative, organized self-starter with a strong grasp of social media and a background in content creation who wants hands-on reps inside a working label. The intern will work alongside our A&R team to keep projects moving and contribute to the creative process behind Reach releases.

Description

  • Scout and research emerging artists, producers, and writers across platforms and share standout finds with the A&R team
  • Review demos, submissions, and reference tracks, and prepare notes to support A&R decision-making
  • Support artist development by helping track project timelines, creative goals, and release plans
  • Monitor industry news, streaming data, and genre trends to keep the team informed on what's moving in the market
  • Assist with sessions and listening events, including taking notes and capturing content
  • Create and edit video and visual content, including short-form clips, promo assets, and behind-the-scenes material
  • Use social media insight to spot trends and recommend content ideas that fit our artists
  • Organize and maintain project documents, trackers, research files, and presentations
  • Use Pro Tools and general audio knowledge to help with session files and music review
  • Communicate professionally with artist teams, producers, and label staff
  • Provide general A&R and administrative support across projects

Qualifications

  • Creative, organized, proactive, and eager to learn; you don't need to be an expert in every area, but should have a solid foundation and the ability to grow
  • Basic understanding of Pro Tools and audio engineering
  • Familiarity with Adobe Photoshop
  • Experience with video editing software (CapCut, DaVinci Resolve, or Adobe Premiere Pro)
  • Strong social media IQ: understands how different platforms work, current trends, and what makes content engaging
  • Basic organizational and administrative skills and working knowledge of Google Suite
  • Strong interpersonal skills and a posture of service toward artists and team
  • Must provide your own computer and smartphone
  • Must be located in Atlanta or able to relocate, with reliable transportation
  • Must be available at least 24 hours per week during business hours (9–5pm)

What You'll Gain

  • Hands-on experience inside an active label's A&R department
  • Exposure to how content, artist development, and releases come together
  • Mentorship from working label professionals and direct access to artist projects
  • A real understanding of how records get made and marketed at a label level

Click here to apply to the A&R internship.

Applications will be reviewed the week of December 7, 2026. Candidates selected to move forward will receive an interview invitation via Jobma.

Thank you for your interest. We look forward to reviewing your application!

title: ITS Engineer
description:
Are you a current NJIT employee? Apply here through the Internal Jobs Hub.

Title:

ITS Engineer

Reports To:

Professor

Position Summary:

Under the supervision of the Chair of the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, the ITS Engineer works with faculty, senior engineers, and other research staff on transportation planning analysis tasks related to sponsored research projects, focusing on transportation data development and analysis, use of regional travel demand, traffic and simulation models, and ITS engineering. Under the direction of the Department Chair and Principal Investigators on research projects, the Junior Transportation Engineer participates in a variety of research activities, including performing technical analysis work, preparing documentation, assisting with technology transfer activities, and participating in communication with clients. Duties also include supporting implementation and needs assessment for research tasks to which the incumbent is assigned.

Essential Functions:

  • Supports tasks for sponsored research projects focusing on transportation modeling and systems analysis, traffic engineering, ITS, and transit systems operations.
  • Utilizes and applies travel demand modeling, traffic engineering and simulation, GIS, and other transportation and mathematical modeling and analysis software.
  • Learns and adopts the state-of-the-practice in transportation modeling, traffic engineering and operations, and ITS, including innovations in related software tools, and implements this knowledge in research activities. (55%)
  • Performs literature reviews, data collection, data analysis, and basic analysis of solutions under the guidance of senior team members.
  • Collaborates with faculty, research staff, and students on drafting technical scopes of work for research projects, and assists the Principal Investigators with trackable project schedules.
  • Assists faculty and senior researchers with coordinating technical work in the areas of transportation modeling, systems analysis, traffic engineering, and ITS. (30%)
  • Drafts technical memoranda and progress reports summarizing the results of the technical work.
  • Assists in preparing sections of Final Report documents related to the assigned work tasks, including printed and electronic data and reports for submission and presentation to research clients.
  • Attends meetings as necessary with NJIT faculty and staff, as well as meetings with research clients.
  • Contributes to the preparation of research reports and papers for publication in coordination with faculty. (10%)

Additional Functions:

  • Interacts with and supports graduate students by providing foundational technical assistance and advice in the areas of transportation modeling, engineering, ITS, and data analysis. (5%)
  • Performs other related duties as assigned by the Chair of the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering or Principal Investigators on research projects.

Pre-Requisite Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering, Transportation, Urban Planning, or a closely related field (Master’s degree preferred but not required).
  • 0–2 years of related experience or coursework/internship experience in computer-based transportation modeling, simulation, or systems analysis.
  • Foundational knowledge of regional and local transportation planning and engineering practices, along with basic transportation engineering theory.
  • Academic or internship exposure to computer-based traffic analysis (such as Synchro) or transportation modeling/simulation software (such as Cube, TransCAD, VISUM, Paramics, VISSIM, or CORSIM).
  • Strong computer background, including high-level proficiency with Microsoft Windows and Office software (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Access, and Visio).
  • Familiarity with data analysis tools or a strong willingness to learn datasets such as the New Jersey Congestion Management System (NJCMS), New Jersey Accident Record Database (NJARD), and Census Transportation Planning Package (CTPP).
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Prior internship or academic project experience involving ITS engineering, systems analysis, or GIS mapping is highly preferred.


Skills/Competencies:

  • Strong analytical skill, attention to details, self-motivated and capable to learn independently in adapting new technologies with the fast-growing Intelligent transportation system field.
  • Team oriented with strong capability to work independently.
  • Well organized and detail oriented.
  • Ability to think critically and strategically.
  • Strong background in HCS, Vissim, and Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint).
  • Excellent written and oral communications skills, and a familiarity of industry practices.

Department:

Civil and Environmental Engineering

At the university's discretion, the education and experience prerequisites may be exempted where the candidate can demonstrate to the satisfaction of the university an equivalent combination of education and experience specifically preparing the candidate for success in the position.

Union:

Professional Staff Association (PSA)

Professional Staff -20

$64,978.10 - $105,109.54

title: Enrollment Advisor
description:
Join BoldAge PACE and Make a Difference!

Why work with us?

  • A People First Environment: We make what is important to those we serve important to us.
  • Make an Impact: Enhance the quality of life for seniors.
  • Professional Growth: Access to training and career development.


Competitive Compensation:

  • Medical/Dental
  • Generous Paid Time Off
  • 401K with Match*
  • Life Insurance
  • Tuition Reimbursement
  • Flexible Spending Account
  • Employee Assistance Program

BE PART OF OUR MISSION!

Are you passionate about helping older adults live meaningful, independent lives at home with grace and dignity? BoldAge PACE is an all-inclusive program of care, personalized to meet the individual health and well-being needs of our participants. Our approach is simple: We listen to our participants and their caregivers to truly understand their needs and desires.

ENROLLMENT ADVISOR - REMOTE

JOB SUMMARY

Under the general direction of the Enrollment Advisor Lead, the Enrollment Advisor is the first and primary point of contact for new referrals and early-stage prospects; owning timely outreach, intake, early engagement, and the judgment-based decisions that determine how each prospect advances. Working a high-volume pipeline by phone, text, and email, the Advisor applies independent judgment and proven sales practices to deliver rapid response, run discovery tailored to each individual, sell the value of PACE, determine the right pathway, and advance every prospect toward enrollment readiness with a secured next step.

The Advisor introduces prospective participants and their families to the PACE program, uncovers their needs and challenges, and independently exercises judgment to qualify or disqualify prospects, determine eligibility alignment, and decide the stage and pathway each prospect should follow. The Advisor initiates required documentation and Medicaid verification in coordination with internal partners, maintains accurate and timely CRM documentation, and executes a warm, confidence-building handoff and endorsement to the Enrollment Navigator for a seamless transition.

The Enrollment Advisor represents BoldAge PACE with professionalism and empathy, embodying our values of People First, Seek to Understand, Exceed Expectations, Do the Right Thing, and Be Bold, and plays a critical role in improving speed-to-lead, reducing lost opportunities, and supporting overall census growth.

ESSESNTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Exercise Independent Judgment on Matters of Significance

  • Decide funnel placement. Independently assess each prospect’s circumstances and determine which stage of the enrollment funnel they belong in and how and when to advance them; a decision that directly shapes pipeline accuracy and enrollment outcomes.
  • Determine eligibility alignment. Weigh each prospect’s health, financial, situational, and “why now” factors against PACE program requirements to independently judge whether they are a viable candidate for enrollment, exercising discretion in ambiguous and borderline cases rather than applying a fixed checklist.
  • Disqualify and loss leads. Exercise independent authority to disqualify a prospect or mark a lead lost when judgment indicates they are not the right fit, a significant decision that governs how the organization invests its enrollment resources and protects pipeline integrity.
  • Own the pathway. Independently determine the optimal next step and pathway to enrollment for each prospect, adapting strategy to the individual rather than following a single prescribed track.

Speed to Lead — Be First to Every Referral

  • Own speed-to-lead. Execute rapid first outreach to every new referral within established speed-to-lead expectations (target ≤ 30 minutes), using judgment to prioritize and sequence outreach for best effect.
  • Be the primary point of contact. Serve as the first, professional, and supportive voice for all new referrals and early-stage prospects.
  • Cover inbound. Receive and respond to inbound calls as needed, backing up call center operations while keeping focus on the assigned pipeline.

Engage & Work the Pipeline

  • Engage across channels. Reach prospects and caregivers by phone, text, and email to introduce PACE, build rapport, and open the conversation.
  • Work a high-volume pipeline. Prioritize outreach and follow-up across a large book of early-stage prospects, exercising judgment on where to invest effort to keep every viable prospect progressing.
  • Persistence with purpose. Apply judgment to set and adjust the right follow-up cadence for each prospect to drive engagement and prevent lead attrition.

Discover & Uncover the Pain

  • Run discovery your way. Lead a needs assessment tailored to each prospect, deciding which questions to ask and how to probe — to surface daily struggles, caregiver stress, health and safety concerns, and the “why now” behind the inquiry. Because every participant is different, the Advisor adapts the conversation rather than reading a script.
  • Qualify with care. Exercise judgment to determine general eligibility and alignment with PACE services, surfacing and weighing what matters most to the prospect and family.

Sell the Value of PACE

  • Make the value personal. Connect PACE to the prospect’s situation — independence at home, fully coordinated care, and peace of mind for the family, in terms that matter to them.
  • Educate clearly. Explain PACE services, eligibility criteria, and the enrollment process to prospects, caregivers, and referral sources with clarity and empathy.

Secure the Next Step

  • Ask for and secure the next step. Close every interaction with a defined next commitment — a scheduled call, a document, or an appointment, never leaving a conversation open-ended.
  • Own pipeline movement. Ensure every active prospect has a clearly defined next activity and use judgment to actively advance them from initial contact through enrollment readiness.

Endorse & Hand Off to the Enrollment Navigator

  • Endorse the closer. Actively build the prospect’s confidence in the Enrollment Navigator who will guide them through enrollment and in-person steps; transferring trust so the family never feels handed to a stranger.
  • Execute warm handoffs. Transition qualified, enrollment-ready prospects to the Enrollment Navigator with continuity of communication and a seamless experience, and when in-person support is required.
  • Advance to readiness. Move prospects through intake and qualification to enrollment readiness, initiating coordination with Participant Benefit Specialists along the way.

CRM Discipline, Coordination & Compliance

  • Keep the CRM clean. Receive, review, and accurately enter referrals; maintain detailed, timely documentation of every interaction, judgment call, status update, and next step in Aline.
  • Drive eligibility. Coordinate with Participant Benefit Specialists (PBS) to initiate Medicaid verification and application; in applicable markets, access and review Medicaid eligibility systems to support timely qualification.
  • Collect what’s needed. Initiate collection of required documentation (consents, medical records, forms) telephonically and electronically, coordinating in-person follow-up with the Enrollment Navigator when needed.
  • Keep referral sources in the loop. Maintain responsive communication with referral sources, including acknowledgment of referrals and status updates as appropriate.
  • Stay sharp and compliant. Participate in team meetings, training, and ongoing development; maintain compliance with all PACE marketing, outreach, and communication regulations, permission-based and CMS-defensible.

Represent BoldAge PACE. Support organizational quality initiatives, act with professionalism and integrity, and perform other duties as assigned to support organizational goals and operations

Metrics for Success

To focus on quality and customer satisfaction, all BoldAge positions will have at least one (1) KPI related to job duties in the role. Refer to the BoldAge Intranet site to view specific KPIs for this job description.

EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Healthcare Administration, Marketing, Communications, ora related field preferred; equivalent experience considered.
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in inside sales, healthcare enrollment, patient access, admissions, or a high-volume call center environment.
  • Demonstrated success managing a sales pipeline, qualifying leads, and achieving conversion or enrollment goals.
  • Experience using CRM systems (Aline, Salesforce, or similar) and maintaining accurate documentation.
  • Healthcare, Medicare/Medicaid, PACE, or senior services experience preferred.
  • Bilingual (English/Spanish) preferred, where applicable.

PRE-EMPLOYMENT REQUIREMENTS:

  • Must have reliable transportation, a valid driver's license, and the minimum state required liability auto insurance.
  • Be medically cleared for communicable diseases and have all immunizations up to date before engaging in direct participant contact.
  • Pass a comprehensive criminal background check that may include, but is not limited to, federal and state Medicare/Medicaid exclusion lists, criminal history, education verification, license verification, reference check, and drug scr

title: Extended Day/Afterschool Care
description:
Pax Christi Academies is a community of five vibrant Catholic elementary schools in the Diocese of Orange, united in our mission to educate students in Faith, Intellect, Character, and Citizenship. Our schools provide Christ-centered, academically excellent learning environments that nurture the whole child.

We are seeking an Extended/After School Care staff to join our St Barbara Catholic School in Santa Ana. The extended after-school care position requires the ideal candidate to supervise children during extended hours, supporting academic and social development, and maintaining a safe, engaging environment.

Essential Functions: Because all Pax Christi Academies employees represent the Roman Catholic Church, they are expected to conduct themselves according to the goals and mission of the Church in performing their work.

  • Academic Support: Help with homework, reading, and other academic activities; reinforce program rules and procedures.
  • Activities & Enrichment: Organize games, crafts, and other activities to promote learning and social skills.

  • Strong communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills.

Physical Requirements

Th from 12pm - 6pm

Compensation:

title: Retail General Manager at Oakley
description:
Ohio Valley Goodwill Industries, founded in 1916, is one of the largest providers of rehabilitation services in the State of Ohio. Utilizing our retail store network, we generate sales revenue to support thousands of individuals with disabilities and homeless local veterans.

The Retail General Manager (GM) is responsible for managing daily operations of the retail store including both the production activities and the retail selling floor. This includes customer service, stocking, merchandising, inventory control, budgeting, and record keeping. Also included is the overall production efficiency, housekeeping standards, safety standards, loss prevention, and coordination of merchandise flow. The GM is responsible for clearly defining roles, responsibilities and requirements for their direct reports and hold each accountable by setting specific performance expectations, providing necessary training, and giving consistent feedback.



Required Skills & Qualifications
  • High school diploma or equivalent, some college preferred.
  • Two to three years of previous retail progressive management experience supervising several departments and/or staff of 15 or more employees.
  • Minimum of five (5) years’ experience in retail or equivalent industry.
  • Experience selecting, assessing, coaching, and developing associates, preferably in a retail environment.
  • Full Profit + Loss ownership.
  • Proficiency in setting and managing schedules for store staff.
  • Ability to communicate effectively in English, both orally and in writing.
  • Math and computer skills required.
  • Broad knowledge of the thrift and resale industry and ability to react to competitively.
  • Highly developed sense of customer service and interpersonal skills including high integrity, respect for all individuals (customers, vendors, and employees), strong critical and analytical thinking skills, and appreciation of diversity.
  • Ability to perform the same functions that direct reports perform.
  • Ability to complete necessary paperwork and reports in a timely and efficient manner.
  • Ability to exercise good judgment in handling day-to day situations.
  • Ability to work a flexible schedule to include opening and closing shifts and extended hours during peak business.
  • May be required to work at other locations.
Supervisory Responsibility
This position has supervisory responsibilities over the retail staff including the Retail Assistant Manager, Retail Supervisor, Merchandise Processors & Sales Associates.

Role and Responsibilities
  • Responsible for the overall operation of the retail store, including store opening and closing procedures.
  • Oversee all production levels, and quality of merchandise to the sales floor to optimize revenue generation.
  • Manage inventory levels of all merchandise lines.
  • Monitor and ensure a smooth and effective flow of donations adhering to all published standards, security, safety, and State laws.
  • Maintain staffing levels while attaining budgeted payroll This includes employment hiring, training and managing store employees in accordance with Goodwill policies.
  • Oversee volunteers and/or temporary labor working in store as needed.
  • Perform all requested reporting requirements on a timely basis including but not limited to surveys, production reports and sales reports.
  • Review and analyze profit and loss statements and adjust store operations according to data.
  • Ensure that daily banking requirements are met.
  • Set and manage schedules for store staff so that the store needs are always met.
  • Manage time and attendance through the Company timekeeping program and submit payroll according to established deadlines.
  • Maintain effective email, phone, and face to face communication with all divisions and other stores.
  • Create an atmosphere of ongoing exceptional customer service for both internal and external customers. Serves as point of resolution for customer complaints and grievances.
  • Comply with and enforce organizational policies and standards.
  • Strives to reduce store turnover, through proper training, selection, and motivation of store team.

Physical Requirements

title: Independent Contractor, Egnyte System Administrator / Data Steward
description:
Independent Contractor, Egnyte System Administrator / Data Steward


What You’ll Do

As an independent contractor serving as our Egnyte System Administrator / Data Steward, you will support the day-to-day administration, organization, and governance of Vaniam Group’s Egnyte environment, a key repository for client work, client-facing materials, and audit-related documentation. You will manage user and folder permissions, create and maintain project folder structures, organize and relocate data into the appropriate domains and folders, and respond to data governance and compliance alerts. Working closely with IT Operations, you will take ownership of routine platform administration with limited supervision, balancing user needs with security and governance requirements so employees can access the information they need while sensitive and client data stays appropriately controlled.

A Day in the Life

  • Egnyte Administration and Access Management
    • Process user access and folder permission requests
    • Create, modify, and remove access based on approved requests
    • Apply role-based and group-based permissions following least-privilege principles
    • Support onboarding, offboarding, and changes to user access
    • Help maintain user groups and access across multiple Egnyte domains
    • Conduct periodic permission reviews and identify outdated or unnecessary access
    • Avoid one-off individual grants when group-based access is appropriate, and document justified exceptions
    • Folder and Project Management
    • Create standardized folders for new clients, projects, and initiatives
    • Maintain approved naming conventions, templates, and folder structures
    • Move and reorganize files and folders when information is stored in the wrong domain or location
    • Identify and help resolve duplicate, misplaced, or outdated content
    • Coordinate larger data moves with IT Operations when changes could affect users or active projects
    • Support an organized and intuitive Egnyte environment across business and client areas
    • Data Governance and Compliance
    • Monitor and respond to Egnyte Secure & Govern and platform alerts
    • Review alerts involving unusual access, mass downloads or deletions, sensitive-content exposure, or risky sharing
    • Investigate alerts, document findings, and escalate suspected security incidents to IT Operations promptly
    • Review external sharing links and recommend or perform appropriate remediation
    • Assist with scheduled access reviews and other data governance activities
    • Support established data retention and destruction processes as directed
  • AI Integration
    • Leverage approved AI tools to improve productivity, efficiency, and quality of work.
    • Identify opportunities to streamline workflows and enhance decision-making through AI-enabled solutions.
    • Ensure all AI-generated outputs are reviewed for accuracy, confidentiality, and compliance.
    • Stay current with emerging AI tools and best practices to drive continuous improvement and innovation.
  • Documentation and Operational Support
    • Maintain records of permission, folder, and configuration changes
    • Document completed access requests, alert investigations, and remediation activities
    • Identify recurring access, organization, or governance issues and recommend improvements
    • Provide periodic summaries of access changes, compliance alerts, open risks, and outstanding work
    • Coordinate with IT Operations and business stakeholders to clarify requests and resolve issues
      Additional deliverables may be mutually agreed upon within the scope of this independent contractor engagement.

What You Must Have

  • Education and Experience
    • Direct, hands-on experience administering Egnyte is strongly preferred
    • Experience with Egnyte permissions, user groups, folders, domains, and external sharing
  • Skills and Competencies
    • Understanding of least-privilege access and role-based access control (RBAC)
    • Familiarity with data governance, information security, records management, or compliance practices
    • Strong organizational skills, sound judgment, and attention to detail
    • Ability to work within structured IT request, approval, and change-management processes
    • Ability to independently handle routine administrative work and recognize when escalation is required
    • Ability to respond promptly to higher-priority access, security, or data governance issues

What You Might Have, but Isn’t Required

  • Experience with Egnyte Secure & Govern
  • Experience supporting confidential, regulated, or client-sensitive data

Schedule and Availability

  • Independent contractor engagement with an anticipated commitment of approximately 20 hours per week
  • Coordinate availability with IT Operations to provide reasonable coverage during normal business hours, with flexibility in scheduling

The Team You’ll Work Closest With

You’ll collaborate most closely with IT Operations, the primary point of contact for this independent contractor engagement, along with business stakeholders across Vaniam Group’s business and client areas.

description:
At IMCO, our talent is among the best! IMCO offers a uniquely stimulating and rewarding environment where you can help build and drive organizational transformation, all while seeking to challenge yourself, learn, and grow your career.

Our culture is built on collaboration and passion, with a shared commitment to delivering lasting value to the clients we serve. If you’re looking to use your expertise to drive strategic outcomes, we’d love to hear from you.

‎

This is a 12 month contract position in January 2027.


The Senior Project Manager leads the delivery of strategic, complex initiatives that enable IMCO’s business priorities, with a particular focus on Cybersecurity, Information Security and Technology Risk. Project will require strong partnership and coordination across multiple business and functions.

As a trusted delivery partner to senior leadership, the Senior Project Manager provides structure, direction and momentum across the full project lifecycle. The role operates across multiple levels of the organization, presenting complex information, influencing decisions, building alignment and guiding stakeholders and project teams toward successful outcomes. This requires the ability to navigate differing perspectives, constructively challenge where appropriate and translate complex business, technology and security considerations into clear decisions and actions.

Working collaboratively across IMCO, the Senior Project Manager coordinates the activities required to deliver complex projects successfully. The role provides strong oversight of risks, dependencies, timelines, costs, resources, outcomes and quality, while navigating competing priorities and complex stakeholder environments.

  • Participate in strategic planning and prioritization of portfolio initiatives, with an understanding of competing priorities and interdependencies across business units.
  • Lead end-to-end delivery of projects ranging from targeted initiatives to complex, mission-critical and enterprise-level programs, developing project plans, critical paths and implementation approaches that support quality delivery and operationalization.
  • Partner with Project Sponsors and key stakeholders across IMCO, clients and vendors to understand business objectives and establish clear outcomes, milestones, costs and resource requirements.
  • Define and advise on project scope, plans, deliverables, risks, budgets, communications, resources, objectives and value proposition, building alignment with senior stakeholders and project teams to drive successful outcomes.
  • Tailor the delivery approach to the size, complexity and criticality of each initiative, balancing appropriate planning and governance with agility and predictability.
  • Apply appropriate project management methodologies and delivery strategies to successfully execute projects and realize their intended strategic benefits, in alignment with IMCO’s Project Framework (IPF).
  • Lead through influence across multiple levels of the organization, building alignment among senior leaders, project teams, subject matter experts, vendors and other stakeholders to move initiatives forward.
  • Present project progress, risks, dependencies, trade-offs and recommendations to audiences ranging from project teams to senior leadership and governance committees, tailoring the message and level of detail to the audience.
  • Lead project risk management, including identification and documentation of risks, development and execution of mitigation strategies and contingency plans, and appropriate reporting, escalation and tracking through resolution.
  • Maintain awareness of project, technology and industry risks, issues and dependencies, collaborating with Sponsors, stakeholders and other project teams to assess impacts and determine appropriate options and contingency plans.
  • Build strong relationships across internal and external stakeholder groups, using influence and sound judgment to navigate competing perspectives, resolve issues and maintain momentum toward shared outcomes.
  • Provide clear reporting to Project Sponsors and key stakeholders on overall project health, risks, milestones, dependencies and decisions in accordance with EPMO reporting guidelines, including Working and Steering Committees.
  • Navigate unforeseen changes by working with Sponsors and stakeholders to assess impacts to schedules, costs, capacity and dependencies, and provide recommendations and contingency plans to ensure project outcomes are realized.
  • Guide project teams and stakeholders through complex issues and critical project milestones, providing clarity on priorities, decisions, deliverables and accountabilities.
  • Ensure appropriate project and program artifacts are developed and maintained throughout the project lifecycle, including charters, implementation plans, resource models, requirements, change requests, issue and action logs, communications, change management plans and Technology SDLC artifacts, where applicable.
  • Develop, maintain and monitor project budgets and scope to ensure requirements are delivered within established timelines and budget.
  • Lead assigned project resources and proactively manage capacity plans to ensure appropriate coverage, competencies and skills are in place while optimizing project performance and budget.

What You Need to Succeed

  • 8+ years of progressive project management experience, with experience in Asset Management, Capital Markets, technology, cybersecurity or Private Markets considered an asset.

  • Strong working knowledge of Cybersecurity and Technology Risk, with the ability to coordinate cross-functional teams, manage technical risks and dependencies, and translate complex issues into actionable delivery plans and executive-level reporting.
  • Strong presence and communication skills, with demonstrated ability to present complex information clearly and confidently to audiences at multiple levels of an organization.
  • Proven ability to influence without direct authority, build alignment across diverse stakeholder groups and drive decisions and outcomes in complex environments.
  • Able to guide and constructively challenge stakeholders, bringing structure and clarity to complex issues while maintaining strong working relationships.
  • Organized and deliberate in planning, with the ability to anticipate risks, manage competing priorities and follow through on commitments.
  • Clear and thoughtful communicator who can translate technical, cybersecurity and project risks into clear business implications, decisions and actions for different audiences.
  • Comfortable operating in a complex, matrixed environment with multiple perspectives and decision-makers.
  • Demonstrates sound judgment and professionalism, particularly when balancing pace, risk and quality.
  • Solutions-oriented and adaptable, with the ability to adjust as priorities and circumstances evolve.
  • Acts with integrity and respect, building trusted, long-term relationships.
  • Will lead and steward project activities in accordance with IMCO’s Project Framework (IPF).

- Proven experience managing seller relationships and driving operational performance improvements.

- Strong analytical skills with proficiency in Advanced Excel and Google Sheets.

- Ability to analyse large datasets, identify root causes and translate insights into measurable business outcomes.

- Excellent communication, stakeholder management and problem-solving skills.

- Strong ownership mindset and ability to work in a fast-paced, escalation-driven environment.

title: Electrical Integration Manager
description:
At IEM, we’re not just building innovative electrical distribution systems, we’re shaping the future. IEM is dedicated to delivering world-class solutions for complex power needs. After 75 years, we continue to push the boundaries of what’s possible. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting out, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute, grow, and make a lasting impact on industries that power the world’s most dynamic markets.

Position Summary

IEM is seeking an Electrical Integration Manager to lead the electrical installation and integration of prefabricated electrical houses (e-houses), equipment skids, and related power distribution systems at our San Antonio facility. This role combines extensive electrical trade knowledge with hands-on leadership of electricians, foremen, and supporting personnel. The manager will plan and oversee electrical installation activities, apply electrical codes to practical installation decisions, and ensure work meets safety, quality, and schedule expectations.

The ideal candidate is an experienced licensed electrician who has progressed into a superintendent, supervisor, or management role within electrical contracting, industrial construction, or modular electrical systems integration. This position offers the opportunity to lead construction-style electrical work from a consistent facility location.

This position will be based temporarily in NE San Antonio while our new manufacturing plant is coming online. Our permanent location is approximately 25 minutes away at Brooks, 7515 Inner Circle Dr., San Antonio, 78235. The position is also 100% in-office and does not offer remote work.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage daily electrical integration activities across multiple e-house and skid projects, coordinating crews, work assignments, installation sequencing, labor priorities, and resource needs to support project schedules and prevent delays.
  • Interpret electrical drawings, specifications, equipment layouts, and customer requirements to guide installation decisions, including conduit routing and sizing, conductor selection, circuit distribution, and equipment connections where drawings require further detail.
  • Apply the National Electrical Code (NEC), relevant International Building Code (IBC) provisions, and project requirements to installation planning and execution.
  • Lead, mentor, and develop electricians and electrical team leaders, setting clear expectations for workmanship, accountability, and performance.
  • Maintain a visible floor presence to inspect work, identify deficiencies, and drive timely corrective action; coordinate with Quality and testing personnel on inspection checkpoints, testing readiness, punch-list completion, and project handoff.
  • Partner with Mechanical Integration, Engineering, Operations, Quality, EHS, Materials, and Project Management to coordinate work and resolve barriers to completion.
  • Establish repeatable installation practices and training; track progress, labor productivity, quality issues, and rework to identify improvements that strengthen consistency and execution while accommodating customer-specific requirements.
  • Promote safe work practices and reinforce company safety procedures.
  • Support the development and expansion of the San Antonio electrical integration operation and perform additional duties as needed.

Qualifications

  • Must have an active journeyman or master electrician license.
  • Extensive hands-on experience in industrial or commercial electrical installation, with demonstrated progression into a foreman, superintendent, supervisor, or manager role.
  • Proven ability to lead multiple electrical crews and coordinate work across concurrent projects.
  • Strong working knowledge of the NEC and the ability to interpret and apply code requirements to installation decisions.
  • Experience with conduit systems, conductor sizing, grounding and bonding, power distribution, lighting, and auxiliary electrical systems.
  • Ability to read and interpret electrical drawings, one-line diagrams, schematics, layouts, and technical specifications.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills and the ability to recognize and correct installation issues through direct observation and technical judgment.
  • Experience planning manpower, sequencing work, and coordinating material and equipment needs.
  • Effective communication, coaching, and cross-functional problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work on-site in San Antonio and maintain an active presence throughout the facility.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience integrating e-houses, modular electrical buildings, equipment skids, power distribution centers, or similar packaged electrical systems.
  • Leadership experience with a large electrical contractor or an industrial electrical integration operation.
  • Experience building teams, developing foremen, or establishing electrical installation processes in a growing operation.
  • Familiarity with switchgear, switchboards, transformers, control panels, and related power distribution equipment.
  • Experience coordinating electrical installation with structural, mechanical, and HVAC work.
  • Lean, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement experience.

Workplace Conditions & Physical Demands

  • This position is based on-site at IEM’s San Antonio facility, overseeing electrical installation within a factory environment. The role requires regular floor presence, direct engagement with electrical crews, and close coordination with other operational teams.

Why Join IEM

At IEM, you’ll join a team that powers some of the world’s most ambitious projects. We’re engineers, makers, and problem-solvers who thrive on tackling complex challenges and delivering solutions that keep industries moving forward. title: Counsellor, Crisis Centre Float
company: CMHA Thames Valley Addiction and Mental Health Services
description:
Counsellor, Crisis Centre Float
Direct Service - (OPSEU)
Part-Time, Contract (End Date: January 11, 2027)

This posting is the result of a current vacancy
London, Ontario (London Zone)
- Application Deadline: November 24, 2026 -


Crisis Centre Staff will support individuals accessing services by providing a psychosocial response in order to promote crisis resolution and empowerment for the individual. The Crisis Centre Staff will also work collaboratively with individuals to assess and identify their needs and link them to appropriate supports in the community.

Depending on the program, supports may be provided in-person, via telephone or virtually; Crisis Services programs support individuals on a walk-in basis at the Mental Health and Addictions Crisis Centre; in the community, via mobile response; via phone, text and web chat, and through intensive, short-term stabilization supports.

Consider revitalizing your career and making a difference in your community by joining our team!

WHAT WE'RE OFFERING:

  • What you'll be making - Starting rate for this role is $27.14 per hour (Level 1 – Direct Service), with a wage differential, based on regulation ($30.01 per hour for Level 1 – Direct Service, Regulated):
    1. Successful candidates who are registered with one of the designated professional colleges (e.g. OCSWSSW, CNO, COTO, CRPO, CPSO, or CPO) will receive the wage differential for regulation
    2. Successful external applicants will start at Level 1, with grid progression based on seniority up to Level 8 ($34.41 per hour for non-regulated, and $37.26 per hour for regulated); for internal applicants, grid level placement will occur as per the Collective Agreement
    3. Premiums of $2.00 per hour will be applied for eligible Evening/Night (8:00pm – 7:00am) and Weekend Shifts.
  • When you'll work - 32 hours biweekly; two days weekly from 5pm to 1am.
  • Your pension plan –Immediately eligible for optional enrolment in the Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan (HOOPP)
  • What your benefits will be – 9% in lieu of benefits

HOW YOU WILL BE MAKING A DIFFERENCE:

Direct Service:

  • Complete mental health and addiction assessments based on theory of crisis management including rapid response to identify:
    1. the impact of psychiatric symptoms on functioning,
    2. risk factors related to safety of client and others
    3. opportunities for de-escalation and stabilization
  • Establish a therapeutic relationship to maximize the benefits of engagement with the individual
  • Provide short-term follow-up support to bridge the gap from referral to engagement with a longer-term support service as needed
  • Coordinate and facilitate referrals to internal and external services and supports
  • Advocate as necessary in order to facilitate access to services and supports with the objective of remediating immediate crisis situation
  • Engage emergency services when it is determined that additional intervention is required
  • Assess barriers to successful community living (e.g. treatment options, transportation, finances, etc.)
  • Obtain information, as needed, from other relevant sources
  • Interact and provide support and assessment in a nonjudgmental fashion and provide care that demonstrates sensitivity to individual diversity (e.g. culture, race, age, sexual orientation, gender, beliefs and values).
  • Support the individual in developing skills for self-advocacy to learn new behaviours and develop coping skills fostering healthy interdependence through limit setting.
  • Provide health teaching and information regarding coping techniques and strategies, e.g. grounding, breathing techniques, self-care, nutrition, sleep hygiene, techniques to enhance overall well-being.

24/7 Reach Out Addiction and Mental Health Crisis Line responsibilities:

  • All Crisis Services Staff are to provide support to individuals through Reach Out.
  • Provide crisis intervention services and supports on Reach Out via phone, text and web chat.
  • Respond to voicemails from Reach Out.
  • Establish a therapeutic relationship with individuals accessing Reach Out, and work with individuals to address their immediate concerns.

Crisis Intervention:

  • Provide short-term, psychotherapeutic intervention to assist individuals in gaining insight and improving coping skills within the framework of the crisis model.
  • Perform in a calm, competent and efficient manner in an emergency situation acknowledging the individual’s need for privacy and dignity.
  • Utilize harm reduction principles to identify, reduce and remove risk factors.

Crisis Follow-up:

  • Refer individuals for additional assessments as is determined to be necessary and/or appropriate
  • Assist the individual to identify and connect with personal/natural supports
  • Provide follow-up support and/or check ins to bridge the gap from referral to engagement with a longer-term support service as appropriate

Coordination and Advocacy:

  • Demonstrate knowledge of community resources and its place within the mental health and addiction care system
  • Assist in building positive working relationships across the service system including CMHA and hospital
  • Participate in public education and advocacy
  • When appropriate, act as liaison with caregivers and/or service and support providers who are involved with the individual to facilitate a coordinated approach to service provision

The Crisis Centre Float position requires the staff to provide coverage to the following programs on any given shift depending on need:

  • Crisis Assessment Team (CAT)
  • Crisis Centre First Contact (CCFC)
  • Crisis Response Team (CRT)
  • Crisis Stabilization Space (CSS)
  • Reach Out/988

Additional Program Specific Roles and Responsibilities:

Crisis Assessment Team (CAT)

For our CAT, the following qualifications are preferred:

  • RPN, RN, or Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Occupational Therapy, Social Work, or Psychology or related field
  • Currently registered and in good standing with the Ontario College of Social Workers and Social Service Workers, the College of Nurses of Ontario, the College of Registered Psychotherapists of Ontario, or the College of Occupational Therapists of Ontario

Crisis Stabilization Space (CSS)

  • Complete necessary tasks required to maintain clean and safe residential setting (e.g., laundry, cleaning, disinfecting, security checks)
  • Assist and coach participants in the learning and management/achievement of mental wellness, safety, and activities of daily living such as personal hygiene, daily chores, budgeting, socialization, etc.
  • Maintain alertness (ie. awake, aware) and knowledge of clients and activity within the program to ensure safety and wellness for all

Crisis Response Team

  • Support individuals in the community working in teams of two. Focus is to be on crisis assessment and solutions focused crisis intervention.
  • As necessary, assist individual crisis centre clients with transportation to required mental health services.
  • Work with community partners including London Police Services and London Emergency Medical Services. Maintain consistent communication with community services through dedicated phone line. Assist community services in supporting the mental health of individuals in the community.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED TO APPLY:

Police Vulnerable Sector Check Requirements
Successful candidates must have a Police Vulnerable Sector Check completed in the last six months. Interested applicants who reside in the City of London and are in need of a Police Vulnerable Sector Check (PVSC) are encouraged to apply for one as soon as possible as PVSCs in the City of London are currently taking approximately 5 weeks to be processed and offers of employment cannot be made without receipt of a PVSC.

We require the following qualifications:

  • College Diploma or University Degree in a mental health or addictions related field or a minimum of 3 years of experience in a direct-service role and some post-secondary education in a mental health or addictions related field (primary proof of credentials will be required during the hiring process i.e. original degree/diploma or official transcript)
  • Valid Driver’s License, adequate insurance and access to a vehicle to carry out job duties
  • Current, satisfactory Police Vulnerable Sector Check (PVSC)
  • Demonstrated ability to attend work regularly

We prefer the following qualifications:

  • First Aid & CPR, WHMIS Training
  • Training in crisis intervention and crisis resolution, including ASIST training program
  • Minimum of 3-5 years’ experience working in mental health
  • Minimum of 2 years’ experience in mental health crisis intervention
  • Experience with, and detailed knowledge of, mild, moderate & serious mental illnesses, usually gained by several years of working with this population
  • Experience working in a community-based setting; preferably with an established network of service & support resources
  • Extensive knowledge of community resources, service & support programs, and barriers participants face in accessing same
  • Working knowledge of a variety of treatment, intervention, and support strategies
  • Bilingual in both official languages, preferred; Une préférence sera accordée aux personnes possédant des compétences dans les deux langues officielles du Canada


INTERNAL APPLICANTS: To be considered as an internal applicant, current staff members are reminded to apply using their @cmhatv.ca or @slwar.ca email address.

Get your application in by – November 24, 2026

Our recruitment process allows us to learn about your previous work experience, your qualifications and your commitment to fulfilling our vision. While we appreciate the interest of all applicants, only those individuals being considered for a position will be personally contacted by someone from the interview team.

We welcome and encourage applications from all members of our community including persons of any gender, gender identity, gender expression, or sexual orientation, persons with disabilities, Indigenous persons, and members of visible minorities. If you require accommodations related to a disability at any point during the recruitment process, please contact Human.Resources@cmhatv.ca

title: Sr. Engagement Manager (Professional Services)
description:
Sr. Engagement Manager

The Team + The Role

Pendo's Professional Services team accelerates time to value for our customers, helping them realize the full potential of their investment in Pendo. We combine implementation expertise, strategic guidance, and proven best practices to deliver measurable customer outcomes. Our goal is to exceed customer expectations in every engagement while building the foundation for long-term success.

As a Sr. Engagement Manager, you own the delivery of enterprise-level SaaS implementations from kickoff through completion. You partner with executive sponsors, IT leaders, and business stakeholders to align implementation strategy with customer goals, manage complex workstreams, and drive measurable value. You serve as a trusted strategic advisor while working across Pendo's Professional Services, Sales, Customer Success, Product, and Support teams to deliver successful outcomes and continuously improve how we serve customers.

This is a role based in-office in San Francisco, Raleigh, or New York, or Remote in the United States.

What this looks like day-to-day

  • Enterprise implementation leadership: Lead complex, enterprise-level SaaS implementations from kickoff through completion, ensuring customer objectives are clearly defined and reflected in project outcomes. Own delivery execution across multiple workstreams while maintaining alignment on scope, milestones, and success criteria.
  • Executive stakeholder partnership: Build trusted relationships with executive sponsors, IT leaders, and business stakeholders throughout the implementation lifecycle. Drive alignment, manage expectations, and navigate competing priorities to support customer adoption and long-term success.
  • Cross-functional delivery: Partner with Pendo Consultants to deliver solution design, configuration, enablement, and rollout planning. Coordinate with Sales, Customer Success, Product, and Support to keep teams aligned and resolve delivery challenges.
  • Project governance and execution: Own project governance, stakeholder communications, and execution across multiple concurrent initiatives. Apply structured project management practices to maintain accountability, manage dependencies, and keep implementations progressing toward agreed outcomes.
  • Strategic customer advisory: Guide enterprise customers on how to leverage Pendo to improve user engagement, product adoption, and customer experience. Connect implementation decisions to customer business objectives and opportunities for measurable value realization.
  • Performance and value tracking: Track key project milestones, deliverables, and KPIs throughout the engagement. Communicate progress, delivery performance, and value realization to customer stakeholders and internal teams.
  • Post-implementation continuity: Coordinate successful handoffs to Customer Success and Support teams as implementations conclude. Ensure relevant project context, customer objectives, and implementation outcomes are communicated to support a seamless transition.
  • Delivery methodology improvement: Develop reusable documentation, playbooks, and implementation best practices that strengthen Professional Services delivery. Share knowledge and identify opportunities to improve team scalability, consistency, and customer value.

Who You Are

Beyond the qualifications, we hire through a specific lens. These aren't buzzwords; they're the things we'll actually look for in how you talk about your work.

You're a builder, not a maintainer.

You're most energized when there isn't a clear path yet, and you get to define it. You don't wait for direction; you identify gaps, shape solutions, and drive them forward. At Pendo, great Sr. Engagement Managers don't just follow instructions; they operate as strategic advisors, influencing decisions, guiding stakeholders, and elevating how we work.

You're AI-curious - genuinely.

You're not using AI tools occasionally. You're rewiring how you work around them. You're faster, sharper, and more prolific because of it, and you bring that energy to everything — how you approach your work, how you prep, how you communicate, how you think. We want someone who sees AI as a multiplier, not a shortcut.

Must-haves

  • 6–8 years of experience in Professional Services or enterprise implementation roles within a B2B SaaS company.
  • Demonstrated success leading enterprise-scale software implementations across multiple stakeholders, departments, and workstreams.
  • Expertise in project management methodologies and tools, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent initiatives while maintaining delivery quality and accountability.
  • Strong executive presence and communication skills, including direct experience engaging VP- and C-level stakeholders and managing expectations across complex organizations.
  • Deep understanding of SaaS delivery models, enterprise customer dynamics, and how implementations contribute to customer adoption and measurable value realization.
  • Experience operating in a billable, utilization-driven Professional Services environment with a demonstrated focus on client satisfaction and delivery excellence.

Nice-to-haves

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field; an MBA or other advanced degree is a plus.
  • Relevant professional certifications such as PMP, CSM, Prosci, or Implementation Specialist.
  • Familiarity with digital adoption, product analytics, user experience (UX), or product-led growth strategies.
  • Proficiency with project management tools such as Asana, Trello, or Jira.
  • Experience contributing to delivery methodology development, internal enablement, or knowledge-sharing initiatives.

About Pendo

Pendo was founded in 2013 by former product managers, who combined their heads and hearts to build something they wanted but never had as product managers: a simple way to understand and attack what truly drives product success. Our mission is to improve society's experience with software. Come join one of the fastest-growing startups, supported by best-in-class institutions like Battery Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, Spark Capital and Meritech.

Pendo Core Values: Bias to Act, Hone Your Craft, The Team is Pendo, and Maniacal Focus.

Location: Pendo is a hybrid culture. In-office 3 days per week unless designated remote.

Compensation: The expected salary range for this role to be performed in the United States is $136,000 - $168,000.

Benefits: Highly competitive, employer-heavy coverage (including $0 premium options), strong 401(k) match, equity, and flexible time off.

EEOC: We are an equal opportunity employer and believe having diverse teams where everyone brings their whole self to Pendo is key to our success. We welcome all people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives.

Accessibility: Pendo is committed to working with, and providing access and reasonable accommodation to, applicants with mental and/or physical disabilities. If you think you may require an accommodation for any part of the recruitment process, please send a request to: accommodation@pendo.io. All requests for accommodations are treated discreetly and confidentially, as practical and permitted by law.

description:

Who we are:

TKD is currently maintaining a hybrid schedule structured as Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays in-office with the option to be remote Mondays and Fridays.

What you'll love about us:
We care about your professional and personal growth. Training and developing our team members are at the heart of everything we do. We are committed to cultivating development opportunities for you and helping you achieve your targeted career goals. The firm values your unique characteristics. We foster an inclusive and diverse environment where multiple perspectives are appreciated as we understand that our employees play an intricate role in the expansion and success of our firm.

Compensation & benefits:
The good faith base annual salary range for this position is a minimum of $130,000 to a maximum of $215,000. Reach Records is looking for a Label Operations & Publishing Intern to support sync, publishing, and day-to-day operations across our roster.
