Liberty Tire Recycling is a high-growth company and the premier provider of tire recycling services in North America with operations throughout the United States and Canada. Liberty Tire annually transforms more than 210 million tires into raw materials for smart, sustainable products that improve our environment and people’s lives. With innovative tools, technologies and processes, Liberty Tire is a revolutionary American conservation enterprise – from coast to coast, and from whole tire to end products. title: Safety & Social Enterprises Coordinator
description:
Job Title: Safety & Social Enterprises Coordinator

Department: Human Resources

Reports To: VP, Human Resources and AVP, Facilities & Social Enterprise

Location: 760 E 160th, Bronx, NY 10456 with travel to Argus locations


JOB SUMMARY:

The Safety and Social Enterprises Coordinator oversees workplace safety, emergency preparedness, regulatory risk mitigation across all multi-site facilities and programs, and development of social enterprise initiatives and client centered opportunities. Reporting directly to the Vice President of Human Resources, with dotted line to AVP Facilities & Social Enterprises, this role fosters a culture of safety, health, and dignity for both staff and the individuals served by our residential, clinical, and community-based programs.

The Coordinator is responsible for standardizing safety protocols across all properties, maintaining compliance with federal, state, and local regulatory mandates (FDNY, NYC Department of Buildings, NYS DOH/OASAS/OMH), conducting regular site audits, leading safety training, managing injury prevention initiatives alongside workers' compensation claims analysis, and participating in community and client events to strengthen relationships.


PRIMARY DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

• Design, implement, and maintain comprehensive Workplace Safety, Hazard Communication, Emergency Action, and Environmental Health programs across all organizational sites.

• Ensure full compliance with OSHA, NYC Department of Buildings (DOB), Fire Department of New York (FDNY), NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH), and state regulatory licensing bodies (e.g., OASAS, OMH, DOH).

• Serve as the primary point of contact for government inspections (FDNY, OSHA, DOB, DOHMH) and direct corrective action plans for any identified violations or notices.

• Oversee site fire/life-safety equipment maintenance schedules, including sprinkler systems, fire alarms, extinguishers, commercial kitchen hood systems, and emergency lighting.

• Conduct routine unannounced and scheduled safety audits and risk evaluations across all residential and outpatient facilities.

• Identify physical hazards, building maintenance safety risks, and operational vulnerabilities; collaborate with Site Directors and Facilities teams to ensure prompt resolution.

• Maintain site-specific emergency response plans, evacuation diagrams, and active shooter/de-escalation safety protocols adapted to community human service environments.

• Partner with HR and workers’ compensation carrier tools to investigate workplace injuries, near-misses, and occupational safety incidents.

• Conduct root-cause analyses of workplace accidents and develop targeted injury-prevention and ergonomic initiatives to reduce claims and lost time.

• Co-chair the agency-wide Safety Committee alongside HR and operational representatives, organizing quarterly meetings, tracking metrics, and driving continuous improvement.

• In coordination with HR Learning & Development, develop and deliver mandatory safety onboarding and annual refresher trainings (e.g., Bloodborne Pathogens, Hazard Communication/SDS, Fire & Life Safety, Workplace Violence Prevention, Ergonomics).

• Coordinate required site safety drills (Fire Drills, Disaster Evacuations, Active Shooter) in compliance with NYC fire codes and regulatory standards.

• Maintain centralized safety logs, OSHA 300/300A/301 logs, inspection records, Safety Data Sheets (SDS), and certificate tracking across all locations.

• Monitor site compliance with FDNY Certificates of Fitness (e.g., F-02, F-08, S-95, G-35) held by site staff and track renewals.

• Participate in program expansion or site renovation planning to ensure safety standards and building codes are incorporated prior to occupancy.

• Establish and maintain relationships with businesses, community organizations, vendors, and other external partners to create opportunities for client participation, vocational training, employment exposure, and skill development.

• Coordinate with program leadership to facilitate client participation in social enterprise activities while ensuring that all initiatives align with individual program objectives, client needs, safety requirements, and applicable regulations.


QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS

Education & Experience:

• Bachelor’s degree in Occupational Health & Safety, Environmental Science, Risk Management, Human Resources, Public Health, or a related field is preferred (or equivalent combination of education and experience).

• Minimum of 2+ years of experience managing safety, environmental health, or occupational compliance.

• Familiarity with NYC-specific codes and regulatory agencies, including FDNY, DOB, OSHA guidelines.


Certifications:

• Valid NYS Driver’s License and willingness to travel frequently across NYC sites.

• Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Associate Safety Professional (ASP), or Certified Protection Professional (CPP) – Willingness to obtain within the first year

• FDNY Certificates of Fitness (e.g., F-02, S-95, F-89/F-08). – Willingness to obtain within the first year

Working Conditions & Special Requirements:

Because this program operates continuously to support vulnerable populations, this role is classified as essential. Staff occupying this title may be required to work alternative shifts, stay over for incoming shifts during staffing shortages, or report during city/state weather travel advisories.

title: Law Fellow – HPC 2027 Summer Fellowship Program
description:
Applications due by January 3, 2027

The Massachusetts Health Policy Commission (HPC) seeks an exceptional law student for its annual Summer Fellowship Program within the Office of the General Counsel (OGC).
The law fellow will join the HPC’s 2027 Summer Fellowship cohort, which will include up to 10 fellows and run from May 31, 2027 through August 13, 2027.

The Office of the General Counsel is responsible for supporting the HPC’s policy and legal work, including the development of regulations and support of agency compliance functions, and provides counsel on a wide range of strategic, policy, and operational topics.

The fellowship will provide the opportunity for a law student to gain in-house government legal experience and exposure to innovative health policy work. The law fellow will work on a wide array of legal matters in support of the HPC’s mission, including conducting legal research and drafting memoranda, analyzing and drafting materials related to legislation, reviewing and preparing contract documents, supporting the HPC’s data privacy and security program, and assisting with other special projects and duties as assigned. The law fellow may also provide support to the Office of Patient Protection, which works to safeguard health care consumer protections in the Commonwealth. The law fellow will have the opportunity to attend internal and external meetings and events with lawyers in adjacent fields.

The law fellow will, with support from their supervisor, guide a legal research or policy project from inception to completion. HPC Summer Fellowship Program reports contain reflections from past fellows, as well as summaries of prior fellow projects.

Qualifications
Applicants must currently be enrolled full-time in a J.D. program at an accredited law school and eligible to work in the United States. Additional qualifications include:
  • Demonstrated interest in health policy and health care;
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills;
  • Excellent legal research skill, with demonstrated proficiency in legal research methods;
  • Strong attention to detail and problem-solving skills;
  • Self-motivation and the ability to work as part of a team;
  • A strong interest in public service and working to advance affordable, high-quality, equitable health care for all Massachusetts residents; and
  • Prior work experience in health care or government is strongly preferred.
The HPC operates a hybrid work schedule, with employees and fellows splitting their time between the downtown Boston office and remote work.

Compensation
Fellows are expected to work full time (37.5 hours per week) Monday through Friday for 10 weeks. Fellows are paid $32/hour for a total summer payment of up to $12,000. The program begins on May 31, 2027 and concludes on August 13, 2027, with two holidays and three days off of the fellow’s choosing. These five days are unpaid.

About the Hiring Process
Applicants must submit a cover letter detailing the reason(s) the applicant would like to work for the HPC, a resume, and a legal research memorandum writing sample of at least three pages. Applications submitted without all three components will not be considered.
Applications must be submitted by January 3, 2027.

Interviews will be conducted virtually in late January. Selected candidates will be required to provide contact information for three references during the interview process. Following successful reference checks, candidates who receive an offer of employment will be required to sign a contract regarding the obligations of the program. After offers have been extended and accepted, candidates will also be required to complete a background check.

About the Fellowship Program
Now entering its thirteenth year, the annual Health Policy Commission (HPC) Summer Fellowship Program has dual goals of helping to achieve the Commonwealth’s health care reform and cost containment goals while simultaneously providing hands-on educational opportunities to the next generation of health policy leaders. Summer fellows engage daily with their assigned department to guide a project from inception to completion, while also exploring the intersection of HPC goals and their own academic interests. Past fellowship projects have ranged from conducting research and analysis using data from the All-Payer Claims Database to tracking and reporting on legislative activity in the Commonwealth. In addition to their primary projects, fellows participate in an orientation program and a series of educational and networking activities throughout the summer.

Our Commitment
The HPC is committed to a policy of non-discrimination and equal employment opportunity. We recognize that diversity in the workplace is a source of strength, vital to its ability to effectively advance its mission. The HPC is committed to:
  • Actively promoting diversity in our workforce, including greater racial and ethnic diversity, at all levels of the organization;
  • Fostering a work environment in which all employees are inspired to do their best, strengthened by their different perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences;
  • Ensuring that no employee’s growth, achievement, or advancement is hindered because of race, ethnicity, sex, sexual orientation, religion, age, genetic information, gender identity, pregnancy, veteran status, or disability;
  • Holding ourselves to a high standard of inclusion and opportunity that will serve as a model for other public and private employers throughout the Commonwealth;
  • Promoting our core values of equal opportunity, equal justice, and inclusion in HPC actions and initiatives.

title: Senior Technical Project Manager
description:
Overview

Bowler Pons Solutions Consultants, LLC is looking for an experienced Senior Technical Project Manager to lead a multidisciplinary team supporting government and industry customers. You will manage personnel, project execution, cost, schedule, technical performance, and customer engagement while fostering accountability, teamwork, and a commitment to mission success.
You will work alongside the Principal Innovation Engineer, who leads solution design, prototyping, and integration. You will lead project delivery, staffing, and customer coordination and work directly with the team when projects need hands-on support. Experience leading technical programs and contributing to software development or systems integration is especially valuable in our small-business environment.

Job Responsibilities

  • Project and Program Management
    • Lead multiple projects, contracts, and task orders from initiation through closeout. Manage scope, cost, schedule, quality, and technical performance.
    • Develop and maintain project execution plans, integrated master schedules, budgets, resource allocations, risk registers, and performance metrics. Identify and mitigate programmatic, technical, schedule, and financial risks.
    • Lead project reviews, milestone assessments, status meetings, and executive briefings. Develop statements of work, technical approaches, and customer deliverables, and meet contractual and reporting obligations.
    • Serve as the primary customer interface. Coordinate engineering, operations, software, test, logistics, and business support teams and maintain relationships with subcontractors, partners, and stakeholders.
    • Support business development, capture, and proposals, including preparation of technical volumes.
  • Personnel Leadership and Staff Management
    • Lead, mentor, and evaluate technical and administrative staff. Set performance objectives, provide feedback and career guidance, and conduct annual performance reviews.
    • Manage staffing plans and assignments. Support recruiting, interviewing, onboarding, and retention, and promote growth through training and certifications.
    • Oversee and steer Innovation Team’s Internship Program, working with colleges, universities, and state-sponsored grant programs (e.g., MTIP, Lighthouse Industries and AI Internship Grant).
    • Build trust through hands-on problem-solving and ownership of results. Foster a team culture that values accountability, integrity, and practical execution.
  • Technical and Operational Leadership
    • Participate in requirements development, systems integration, testing, operational assessments, and deployment as needed. Support design and technical reviews, verification and validation, and operational demonstrations.
    • Help teams resolve technical, operational, and customer challenges. Review technical documentation, test plans, reports, and deliverables for quality and completeness.
    • Use project performance and operational data to recommend improvements that support organizational goals and improve execution.

Minimum Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Development, Systems Engineering, Program Management, or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible experience in project, program, or operations management.
  • Minimum 5 years of direct personnel management or team leadership experience.
  • Demonstrated experience managing project cost, schedule, scope, and risk.
  • Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary teams in a fast-paced environment.
  • Experience developing and managing project schedules, budgets, and customer deliverables.
  • Strong oral and written communication skills with experience briefing customers and senior leadership.
  • Demonstrated success leading projects from planning through execution and closeout.
  • Experience coordinating activities among internal teams, subcontractors, and external stakeholders.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, Project, PowerPoint, and collaboration tools.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance.

Additional Desired Qualifications

  • Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Development, Systems Engineering, Program Management, or a related discipline.
  • Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
  • Active Secret security clearance.
  • Experience supporting the DoW.
  • Experience managing Research & Development (R&D), technology transition, test and evaluation, or systems integration programs.
  • Technical background in software development, software engineering, DevSecOps, Agile development, data analytics, Power BI, cloud technologies, or systems architecture.
  • Experience leading multidisciplinary engineering or software development teams.
  • Familiarity with requirements management, systems engineering processes, verification and validation methodologies, and operational testing.
  • Experience developing proposals, capture strategies, and technical solutions for new business pursuits.
  • Working knowledge of government contracting, FAR/DFARS requirements, task order management, and subcontractor oversight.
  • Experience supporting emerging technologies including artificial intelligence, automation, unmanned systems, sensors, biometrics, physical security systems, or command and control platforms.

About Bowler Pons

Bowler Pons Solutions Consultants, LLC is a fast-growing Minority-Owned, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned 8(a)-certified Small Business based in Annapolis, MD. As a solutions provider, we provide cutting-edge technology and comprehensive support for our client's toughest challenges in the fields of physical and cyber security, IT and network administration, and systems engineering. As an employer, we pride ourselves on providing best-in-class benefits, including paid healthcare options for employees, generous tuition reimbursement, paid leave, and opportunities for mentorship and professional development, in combination with the personal connections and visibility within a small business. Find out more at www.bowlerpons.com

title: Sr. Director, International Markets
description:
Axogen is committed to building and maintaining a strong and gratifying company culture that fosters professional growth. Our hands-on and personal approach makes transitioning to a new job a seamless and enjoyable process. Most benefits are effective on day one!

Axogen is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate against applicants on the basis of race, color, creed, religion, ancestry, age, sex, marital status, national origin, disability or veteran status.

Why you’ll love working at Axogen:

  • Friendly, open, and fun team culture that values unique perspectives
  • Company-wide dedication to profoundly impacting patients’ lives
  • Comprehensive, high-quality benefits package effective on date of hire
  • Educational assistance available for all employees
  • Matching 401(k) retirement plan
  • Paid holidays, including floating holidays, to be used at your discretion
  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan
  • Referral incentive program

Axogen Mission and Business Purpose

Our business purpose is to restore health and improve quality of life by making restoration of peripheral nerve function an expected standard of care. We aim to lead the markets we serve by always requiring the solutions we offer patients and caregivers provide an improved benefit-to-risk profile as compared to existing standards of care. To ensure we deliver improved benefit-to-risk solutions, we will guide and expect the market and design requirement specifications underlying our engineering, business development, and clinical research activities, objectively target advancements in standards of care.

Job Summary of the Sr. Director, International Markets

The Sr. Director, International Markets will lead the development and execution of Axogen's international commercial strategy across markets outside the United States. This leader will be accountable for developing, executing and driving strategic plans that result in sustainable revenue growth, strengthened distributor performance, expanded clinical adoption, improved market access, and developing the organizational capabilities required to scale Axogen's international business.

The role will lead Axogen's distributor and channel strategy while building strong relationships with surgeons, key opinion leaders, professional societies, health systems, and market access stakeholders. The Senior Director will translate Axogen's global and portfolio strategies into market-specific operating plans that address commercial execution, clinical education, reimbursement, regulatory access, product availability, pricing, and profitability.

Working across Commercial, Marketing, Product Management, Professional Education, Medical Affairs, Health Economics and Reimbursement, Regulatory, Quality, Legal, Finance, and Operations, this leader will serve as the voice of international markets and establish the operating discipline required to develop international into a scalable and profitable growth platform.

Requirements of the Sr. Director, International Markets

  • Bachelor's degree in business, life sciences, healthcare, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
  • At least 10 years of progressive commercial, market development, or sales experience in medical devices, biologics, or life sciences.
  • Significant experience leading international markets and distributor or channel relationships.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and execute strategic commercial plans that drive revenue growth and market expansion.
  • Experience working directly with surgeons, KOLs, distributors, and cross-functional corporate partners.
  • Strong understanding of international medical device market access, reimbursement, regulatory pathways, and hospital procurement.
  • Demonstrated success launching new technologies or expanding clinical adoption in international markets.
  • Experience with forecasting, budgeting, pricing, distributor economics, and performance analytics.
  • Ability to operate strategically while maintaining a hands-on presence in priority markets.
  • Fluency in English required; additional language capabilities preferred.
  • Ability to travel extensively internationally (~35%).

Key Competencies

  • Strategic market development leadership
  • Commercial and financial acumen
  • Distributor and channel management
  • Executive communication and influence
  • Surgeon and KOL relationship development
  • Cross-functional leadership
  • Market access and reimbursement understanding
  • Cultural adaptability
  • Negotiation and conflict resolution
  • Data-driven decision-making
  • Change leadership
  • High integrity and compliance orientation

Responsibilities of the Sr. Director, International Markets

The specific duties of the Sr. Director, International Markets include but are not limited to:

  • Develop and execute the international market development strategy aligned with Axogen's corporate and portfolio priorities that exceed revenue goals.
  • Establish market priorities based on revenue potential, distributor readiness, reimbursement pathways, regulatory feasibility, KOL development, and strategic importance.
  • Own international revenue planning, forecasting, budgeting, and performance reporting.
  • Develop market-specific growth plans, pricing strategies, and investment recommendations.
  • Monitor revenue, gross margin, product mix, market access, competitive activity, and key business risks.
  • Prepare international operating plans, business reviews, and recommendations for senior leadership.
  • Evaluate opportunities to evolve markets from distributor-led models to hybrid or direct commercial structures when appropriate.

Distributor Leadership and Commercial Execution

  • Lead the selection, onboarding, development, and ongoing management of international distributors and channel partners.
  • Establish annual business plans, quarterly business reviews, scorecards, forecasts, and action-tracking processes for priority distributors.
  • Assess distributor performance across revenue growth, forecast accuracy, account development, product mix, KOL activity, education execution, compliance, and market development progress.
  • Partner with distributors to identify growth opportunities, targeted accounts, market barriers, and required support.
  • Conduct field visits with distributor teams to support surgeon engagement, account development, and commercial execution.
  • Recommend where distributor relationships should be expanded, improved, renegotiated, or replaced.
  • Ensure distributor partners are appropriately trained on Axogen products, clinical evidence, compliance requirements, and market development expectations.

Surgeon, KOL, and Market Development

  • Develop relationships with leading surgeons, clinical advocates, and other stakeholders in priority international markets.
  • Build country-level KOL, faculty, and professional education plans that support sustainable clinical adoption.
  • Partner with distributors and internal teams to develop peer-to-peer education, advisory activities, visiting surgeon programs, and society engagement.
  • Represent Axogen at international congresses, distributor meetings, and strategic customer engagements.
  • Gather market insights from surgeons, distributors, and healthcare stakeholders to inform commercial strategy, product development, and portfolio planning.
  • Support the introduction of new nerve repair applications and products within international markets.

Market Access, Portfolio, and Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Partner with Health Economics and Reimbursement teams to develop country-specific reimbursement roadmaps, value materials, budget impact tools, and evidence priorities to become the standard of care in peripheral nerve repair.
  • Work with Regulatory and Quality teams to prioritize market entry pathways and maintain appropriate product access.
  • Integrate international requirements into product development, labeling, claims, launch planning, and evidence generation activities.
  • Coordinate with Finance and Operations on pricing, inventory, demand planning, distributor economics, and gross margin improvement.
  • Establish a cross-functional international operating cadence with clear priorities, owners, decisions, and escalation pathways.

Operational Excellence and Compliance

  • Establish dashboards and performance measures covering revenue, forecast accuracy, margin, distributor execution, market access, regulatory progress, product access, KOL development, and education activity.
  • Maintain accurate international business, distributor, account, and KOL records within applicable company systems.
  • Ensure distributor and commercial activities comply with company policies, applicable quality requirements, industry codes, and global anti-corruption requirements.
  • Provide regular market intelligence regarding competitors, pricing, reimbursement, regulatory changes, and emerging opportunities.
  • Demonstrate strong fiscal discipline through effective budget, expense, inventory, and resource management.
  • Comply with all company policies, procedures, and SOPs.
  • Perform other duties as directed by the supervisor.

Location

111 West Oak Ave., Tampa, FL 33602

Benefits/Compensation

This position is eligible for an annual bonus.

Benefits offered for this position include Health, Dental, Vision, Matching 401K, Paid Time Off, 9 Paid Holidays + 3 Floating Holidays, Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts, Medical Flexible Spending Accounts, Tuition Reimbursement, Paid Parental Leave, Paid Caregiver Leave, Basic Life Insurance, Supplemental Life Insurance, Employee Stock Purchase Plan, and Disability Insurance, as described in more detail in summary plan descriptions.

Salary Range
$168,828—$211,034 USD

Company Statements

Axogen follows healthcare system guidelines with respect to credentialing, vaccinations and other employment/compliance related requirements, as well as CDC guidance. Axogen reserves the right to amend its policies from time to time in its sole discretion.

As AI is becoming a common tool throughout the application process, we want to be clear about its appropriate use at Axogen. Using AI to support resume writing, research or interview preparation is perfectly acceptable, provided the content is accurate and genuinely represents your qualifications and skills. For other key parts of your interview process, however, it is important that the ideas, communication, and work you share reflect your own voice, experiences, and thinking. We ask that you participate in our live interviews and complete any assessments without AI assistance unless instructions explicitly indicate otherwise or a specific exception is discussed and approved in advance. This approach ensures fairness, celebrates your individuality, and allows your authentic perspective to shine. Behaviors that do not align with these guidelines may result in disqualification from the hiring process or termination of employment if later discovered. We appreciate your understanding and look forward to learning about the unique contributions only you can bring to Axogen.

No agency solicitation. We kindly request that recruiting agencies, staffing firms, and third‑party vendors do not contact us regarding this posting. Unsolicited résumés will not be considered.

title: Base Access & Badging Specialist
description:
Title: Base Access & Badging Specialist
Location: Naval Submarine Base Kings Bay, Kings Bay, GA 31547
Schedule: Full-time, Monday–Friday; 7:30 a.m.–4:00 p.m. core coverage
Pay: $18.49–$23.91/hour

ROLE
KMRG, LLC (KMRG) is a federal services company that hires talented professionals to support Government agencies and the communities they serve. We are hiring a Base Access & Badging Specialist to support Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Southeast’s Resident Officer in Charge of Construction (ROICC) at Naval Submarine Base Kings Bay, Georgia.

In this role, you will provide administrative security support for Navy construction projects. You will verify personnel background determinations, process installation access and badging requests, coordinate with base security personnel, and protect sensitive information.

Applications will be reviewed as they are received. Apply today!

RESPONSIBILITIES
Personnel Security & Background Verification
  • Review and validate security clearance qualifications and background determinations using the Defense Information System for Security (DISS)
  • Verify background and security eligibility for contractor personnel, NAVFAC employees, and designated site visitors
  • Coordinate with authorized Government security personnel on access requirements and supporting documentation
Base Access & Badging

  • Coordinate with installation security to follow and enforce approved badging procedures

Administrative Security & Information Protection
  • Process background and base-access paperwork accurately and within required timelines
  • Maintain accurate access records and supporting security documentation
  • Use Microsoft Word, Excel, and approved Government systems for administrative processing
  • Safeguard Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and personally identifiable information (PII)
  • Communicate professionally with NAVFAC staff, installation security, contractors, and visitors
  • Perform related administrative security duties within the scope of the position

REQUIRED BACKGROUND
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Knowledge and experience with Department of War installation access procedures
  • Familiarity with NBIS and SWFT and ability to obtain the required system accounts
  • Knowledge of computer systems and administrative processing software
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Word and Excel
  • Ability to follow established administrative policies and procedures
  • Strong communication, multitasking, and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to adapt to changing workflows, systems, and procedures

title: IT and Cybersecurity Administrator
company: South Dakota State University Alumni & Foundation
description:
Position Summary
The IT and Cybersecurity Administrator serves as the SDSU Alumni & Foundation’s onsite technology lead and primary liaison to the managed IT service provider (MSP). This position executes onsite IT assistance, serves as the internal expert for institutional IT knowledge, provides hands-on support for staff and events, manages SharePoint systems, facilitates IT and software governance, supports technology planning and budgeting, oversees elements of security policy and organizational awareness, and coordinates incident response. Additionally, this position works directly with the MSP to ensure they deliver contracted day-to-day help desk support, remote monitor patching, endpoint protection, security monitoring, backup management, and vulnerability remediation. This role further ensures that all sensitive organizational information, including donor and alumni information, remains secure and intact.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Onsite Technology Support and Managed Services Coordination
  • Serve as the onsite point of contact for staff technology needs, directing day-to-day support requests to the MSP through its established support channels, and personally handling issues that require hands-on assistance such as hardware swaps, printer and peripheral setup, and conference room and event technology.
  • Manage the full lifecycle of technology assets, including purchasing, onsite setup and deployment of new laptops and devices, inventory tracking, warranty shipping and returns, and decommissioning and secure disposal, in coordination with the MSP’s device management and deployment processes.
  • Oversee the managed services relationship by reviewing ticket metrics, service level performance, and recommendations, escalating concerns, and participating in regular business reviews.
  • Coordinate IT elements of staff onboarding and offboarding, including account requests, device issuance and return, phone setup, and access approvals.
  • Serve as the onsite hands for MSP engineers when physical access is needed, such as installing network and power equipment or supporting scheduled maintenance.
  • Manage the annual technology plan, IT budget, technology purchasing, renewals, and software licensing.
  • Manage relationships and contracts with technology vendors, such as donor and finance system providers, internet and phone carriers, copier and audio-visual vendors, and serve as support for line-of-business applications.
  • Work occasional evenings and weekends to support events, maintenance windows, or security incidents as needed.
Cybersecurity, Vulnerability Management, and Incident Response
  • Lead the cybersecurity program at the governance level, developing and maintaining IT and security policies and procedures (such as acceptable use, access control, passwords and multifactor authentication, vendor security, and disaster recovery) and reviewing them at least annually.
  • Participate as a member of the organization’s Data Governance Committee.
  • Serve as the designated technical and approval contact for vulnerability remediation, reviewing monthly vulnerability and remediation reports, approving remediation activities and maintenance windows, communicating blackout periods and change freezes in advance, and confirming that business applications work as expected after changes.
  • Review and act on security alerts and notifications escalated by the MSP, make business decisions on risk acceptance and exceptions, and ensure that hardware and software remain within vendor-supported lifecycles.
  • Champion security awareness across the organization by ensuring completion of monthly training and simulated phishing campaigns, coaching staff who need additional support, and reinforcing safe handling of data.
  • Lead completion of cyber insurance applications, audit and compliance questionnaires (including payment card requirements for gift processing where applicable), and periodic reviews of user and administrator access.
  • Serve as the internal incident response coordinator by maintaining the technology incident response plan, contact lists, and escalation procedures, and act as the primary liaison with the MSP, the cyber insurance carrier, breach counsel, and other outside parties during a security event.
  • Coordinate internal decisions and communications during an incident, including leadership notification, staff guidance, and documentation, and lead the post-incident review and follow-up.
  • Participate in annual incident response tabletop exercises and breach readiness activities and track remediation of identified gaps.
  • Maintain business continuity and disaster recovery plans, confirm with the MSP that critical systems and data are backed up, and coordinate periodic restore testing.
Microsoft 365 and SharePoint Administration
  • Serve as the internal administrator for Microsoft 365, including SharePoint Online, Teams, and OneDrive, managing user access, groups, and permissions in line with the organization’s security standards.
  • Maintain the SharePoint and Teams site structure, file storage, and data retention practices, keeping information organized, secure, and easy for staff to find.
  • Create and configure new sites, Teams, and shared resources as requested by departments, and monitor storage usage and licensing.
  • Train and support staff on Microsoft 365 collaboration tools and best practices, and coordinate with the MSP on advanced configuration, integrations, and workflows.
Other Duties
  • Other duties may be assigned to meet the organization’s needs.
Education and Previous Experience
Associate or bachelor’s degree in information technology, cybersecurity, or a related field is preferred but not required. At least three years of professional experience in a related field (such as IT support, systems coordination, or cybersecurity) is required. Hands-on Microsoft 365 and SharePoint administration is preferred.

Additional Qualifications
Qualified individuals will possess the following:
  • Authorization to work in the United States for any employer on a full-time basis.
  • Demonstrated problem-solving, troubleshooting, and analytical skills, with the ability to explain technical issues in plain language.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft 365 administration, including Entra ID (Azure AD), Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Teams, OneDrive, and Intune.
  • Solid understanding of cybersecurity fundamentals, including multifactor authentication and conditional access, endpoint protection, email security, vulnerability management, and data protection.
  • Familiarity with recognized security frameworks such as the NIST Cybersecurity Framework or CIS Controls, and with incident response principles.
  • Familiarity with Windows and Mac computers, networking basics (Wi-Fi, switches, firewalls, VPN), printers, and audio-visual and conference room technology.
  • Ability to manage vendors and service providers, understand contracts and service agreements, and hold partners accountable to service levels.
  • Enhanced ability to interpret descriptions of problems, troubleshoot and provide solutions, and document interactions, processes, and system configurations.
  • Ability to write clear policies, procedures, and end-user guidance.
  • Ability to build and maintain positive relationships while demonstrating responsiveness, professionalism, empathy, and clear communication.
  • A high level of interpersonal skills, both in person and by phone, to handle sensitive and confidential situations with varied internal and external constituencies.
  • Customer service skills requiring clear communication in person, on the phone, and in writing are essential.
  • A high level of integrity, including ability to treat confidential information with discretion.
  • Ability to be organized and resourceful to locate and compile information and accomplish projects with minimal supervision.
  • Consistent attention to detail in composing and proofing materials, establishing priorities, and meeting deadlines.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment with demonstrated ability to juggle multiple competing tasks and demands.
  • Ability to work independently as well as in a collaborative team environment with professional demeanor, self-reliance, and resourcefulness.
  • Dependability and punctuality.
  • High energy, positive attitude, and high degree of initiative.
  • Proficient experience using the most recent versions of computer software applications including word processing, spreadsheets, database and presentation software (i.e. MSWord, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint).
Typical Physical Demands
Requires sitting, standing, bending, reaching, and lifting and moving computer equipment. Requires manual dexterity sufficient to operate computers, telephones, and other office equipment. Requires normal range of hearing and vision.

Employee Statement of Understanding
This job description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the employee occupying this position. All requirements are subject to possible modification to reasonably accommodate individuals with disabilities. Regular attendance is required in this job. This document does not create an employment contract, implied or otherwise, other than an “at will” employment relationship. The SDSU Alumni & Foundation is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

About the South Dakota State University Alumni & Foundation
The South Dakota State University (SDSU) Alumni & Foundation is an independent 501(c)(3) not-for-profit organization. The Alumni & Foundation strives to engage alumni, friends and business partners with SDSU through events, strategic communication and outreach, and serves as the exclusive provider of fundraising and financial management of private gifts designated for the university.
The SDSU Alumni & Foundation was formed on January 1, 2026, through the consolidation of the university’s two largest supporting organizations: the SDSU Alumni Association and the SDSU Foundation. The Alumni Association was founded in 1889; the Foundation was formed in 1945.
The governing boards of both organizations voted unanimously on October 10, 2025, to consolidate into the SDSU Alumni and Foundation. Together, the organization is an influential force in keeping SDSU’s traditions alive and advancing South Dakota State University.

title: Backend Data Platform Engineer [Senior/Expert]
description:
Python or Java | SQL | TB-scale flight data | Aviation AI

At StorkJet, we build software that helps airlines reduce fuel consumption and CO² emissions by processing high-volume flight and operational data. This is not a pure maintenance role. We are looking for a senior/expert engineer who wants to modernize and evolve production backend/data-processing systems, improve architecture, and work on performance-heavy data workflows used by airline customers.

You will work with real aviation data, including second-by-second flight recorder data, and help turn it into reliable products used by airlines, pilots, fuel-efficiency teams and operational experts.

What you will own

  • Design, build and modernize backend services and data-processing components in Python and/or Java.
  • Work on incremental rewrites and modernization of selected production systems, with a focus on reliability, testability and maintainability.
  • Build and optimize batch and real-time data processing pipelines for high-volume aviation datasets.
  • Work deeply with relational databases: query optimization, indexing, partitioning, schema design, bulk loading, migrations, data retention and performance monitoring.
  • Build secure APIs and integrations with airline/customer systems.
  • Improve observability, CI/CD and customer onboarding automation.
  • Collaborate with backend engineers, data scientists, aviation experts and product people to design algorithms and workflows that optimize airline operations.

Our stack and technical area

  • Python: SQLAlchemy, Pandas, data-processing scripts and services.
  • Databases: MariaDB, SQL performance tuning, indexing, partitioning, query plans, schema design, migrations, replication, large-table operations.
  • Data and integration: batch processing, real-time workflows, ETL/ELT, CDC/binlog-based processing, bulk data loading, data validation, data quality checks, idempotent pipelines, orchestration, Data Warehouse and OLAP workloads.
  • Data domains we work with: flight and aircraft operational data, geospatial data, OpenStreetMap, weather data including ECMWF, currency and external reference-data feeds.
  • Operations and observability: Docker, Linux, Bash, GitLab CI/CD, ELK, Grafana, application performance monitoring, logs/metrics/tracing, production troubleshooting.
  • Infrastructure exposure: Ansible, VMware/Proxmox, networking basics, IPSec/VPN-based customer integrations, secure system-to-system connectivity.

What we expect

  • 5+ years of commercial backend/software engineering experience.
  • Strong production experience in Python or Java.
  • Willingness to work across both ecosystems; expertise in both is welcome but not required from day one.
  • Strong SQL skills and practical experience with production databases.
  • Experience designing, debugging and improving systems running in production.
  • Ability to reason about performance, reliability, data quality and security.
  • Ownership mindset: you can break down ambiguous modernization work, propose trade-offs and deliver safely.
  • Good communication skills in English, B2+.

Nice to have

  • Experience with TB-scale relational databases, large tables, analytical workloads, partitioning, indexing and query optimization.
  • Experience with high-volume ETL/ELT, batch processing, CDC, replication or binlog-based workflows.
  • Experience with Kafka or other message/event-processing systems.
  • Experience with Data Warehouse / OLAP concepts, data modelling, aggregation pipelines or reporting-oriented datasets.
  • Experience with production observability, performance debugging, profiling, alerting and incident analysis.
  • Familiarity with GitLab CI/CD and secure deployment practices.

What do we offer

  • A real say in tech decisions and space for your ideas.
  • Possibility to join the Employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP).
  • Training budget, language classes, internal tech talks, referral program.
  • Flexible hours and a modern office in the heart of Katowice.
  • Fully equipped kitchen (with an oatmeal station – we take breakfasts seriously).
  • Private healthcare and/or Multisport card.
  • Regular, unconventional company events, friendly atmosphere – we’re not a corporation.

title: Communications Intern
description:

About the Opportunity

Communications Intern

David Zwirner New York’s Communications team is seeking a motivated intern to support day-to-day operations. This role offers hands-on experience within an internationally recognized gallery committed to advancing its artists, exhibitions, and publishing arm, David Zwirner Books, within the broader contemporary cultural landscape.

title: Distribution Center Manager
description:
Style Crest is seeking an experienced and results-driven Distribution Manager to lead our largest distribution operation in Fremont, Ohio. This key role will oversee all distribution and transportation activities, directly supporting seamless order fulfillment, private fleet delivery to customers in the Northern Region, as well as managing full truckload orders and internal inventory transfers to our branches across the country.

As the Distribution Manager, you will be responsible for leading a diverse team of 50+ distribution associates and 15+ drivers across multiple shifts and facilities. This role presents an exciting opportunity to make a lasting impact on our operations and drive the success of the organization. Your leadership will inspire, engage, and retain a dedicated team, ensuring they are aligned with operational goals and fully committed to delivering outstanding results for the company.

Why Join Us?

At our Style Crest, we believe in fostering a culture of growth, innovation, and collaboration. As the Distribution Manager, you’ll play a key role in shaping the future of our largest distribution operation and making a tangible impact on our organization’s success. We offer a collaborative work environment, competitive compensation, and opportunities for professional growth. Style Crest has a 50-year tradition of growth and innovation in the building products industry. The organization has a commitment to the manufactured housing industry and the residential exterior market with an extensive product offering and a dedicated service platform that customers count on to support the success of their businesses.

Responsibilities

  • Accountable for the successful execution of the day to day operational activities to support customer order fulfillment and delivery, internal inventory transfers, customer TL and LTL orders, routing and dispatching of deliveries, equipment upkeep and availability, receiving and replenishment, inventory control and management, workforce planning, safety, facility organization and housekeeping as well as the shuttle and warehouse support for the plant.
  • Provides leadership and direction either through supervisors or directly to associates to ensure a consistent understanding and adherence to job and customer service expectations; the achievement of operational standards and efficiencies; the development and retention of talent to support the business needs; the optimization of resources (labor, equipment, etc.); the adherence to operational processes and policies; and enforcement of all company, safety, DOT, and federal/state regulations.
  • Drives individual and team engagement to achieve daily work expectations, desired customer service goals, and deliver operational improvements. Demonstrates the ability and passion for hiring, developing, and retaining a talented workforce by being a visible and engaged leader who coaches, supports, and holds the team accountable for their actions and results. Develops and executes a workforce plan that can properly support our sales, service, and financial goals. Maintains a positive work environment and culture for our associates to be successful.
  • Leads with a strong passion for continuous operational and customer service improvement. Challenges the current state to identify opportunities to improve productivity, efficiency, processes, and costs to drive effective and sustainable changes that deliver exceptional customer service and enhanced operational results. Works with cross functional leaders to implement improvement initiatives that yield positive operational efficiencies and financial results.
  • Analyzes distribution expenses as well as the costs associated with service errors such as inaccurate picking and receiving, damages, inventory shortages, returns, product movements, internal transfer processes, etc. to make positive improvements in the operation. Addresses service failures immediately with corrective action.
  • Analyzes fleet costs, routing processes, delivery commitments, customer constraints, and inventory transfer processes to recommend adjustments to improve overall efficiency and costs. Works with sales and cross functional leaders to ensure sound decisions are consistently applied to improve the overall cost to serve the customer. Ensures the operation has adequate back-up delivery options to meet our promised delivery dates. Ensures all fleet assets (tractors, trailers, ELD equipment, forklifts, etc.) are well maintained. Provides the on-site leadership for fleet safety and the adherence to DOT regulations, delivery expectations, and fleet policies.
  • Oversees the management of and the inventory control procedures for all products and materials in the facility. Assists with cycle counts and physical inventory. Ensures all inventory discrepancies are communicated and resolved. Works with Purchasing to achieve the targets for inventory turns. Ensures the condition of the inventory is maintained and implements corrective action to address issues. Ensures customer returns are processed timely and in adherence with policy. Determines root causes for these returns and implements corrective action. Ensures product is inspected and product returned into inventory or moved to QA timely.
  • Evaluates warehouse layout, organization, and cleanliness to eliminate potential inefficiencies and reduce any safety hazards. Actively promotes, trains, and enforces a positive safety & housekeeping culture.
  • Ensures our ERP technology and associated equipment is being used correctly to support our distribution and transportation activities. Identifies opportunities for enhancements to drive productivity and service improvements.
  • Communicates frequently with leadership to provide an overview of the operational successes and challenges, significant service failures, performance efficiencies, customer issues, large facility or equipment expenditures, and inventory concerns. Recommends and implements solutions to continually improve the operation.
  • Actively participates in the budget process and monthly financial review to understand key cost drivers impacting the operation to manage adherence to the operation’s budget to ensure P&L success for the activities serviced by Ohio. Recommends capital expenditures to increase efficiency, replace equipment, or solve capacity constraints.
  • Maintains a security program that ensures the company’s products, materials and equipment are always secure and report any unauthorized entries at the facility. Immediately reports and investigates security issues including theft, vandalism, or missing inventory. Works with Corporate Operations to resolve issues.

Requirements

  • At least 7 years of management experience in a distribution pick/pack environment with a direct delivery platform.
  • Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, operations, and/or business in a related field or equivalent work experience.
  • Proven ability to lead and manage a team to achieve operational goals in a fast pace and complex operation.
  • Prior experience with managing a private fleet with knowledge of DOT regulations is preferred.
  • A customer service focused individual who operates from a clear set of positive values and principles.
  • Excellent communication (verbal and written) skills at all levels in the organization.
  • Demonstrated success developing and leading significant operational improvement projects.
  • Strong analysis skills to identify opportunities and solutions.
  • Ability to use logical judgment to make sound decisions and appropriately resolve problems and conflicts.
  • Demonstrated success developing and motivating a high-performance team that achieves results.
  • Ability to foster a positive work environment and culture that drives retention of a talented team.
  • A strong background in inventory management and control process to achieve order fulfillment goals.
  • A visible leader with a collaborative approach who is committed continuous improvement across the operation.
  • Organized individual with the ability to successfully lead multiple priorities across multiple shifts and facilities.
  • Flexible, adaptive, approachable, and capable of leading through times of uncertainty, change, and significant growth.
  • Experienced managing an operation through an ERP implementation.

title: Crossville Residential Generator Installer
description:
About Premier Generators, a Power Support Partners Company:

How would you like to be a part of one of the fastest-growing home service companies in Tennessee? You will be able to play an important role within the Install Team at Premier Generators, a Power Support Partners Company.

A Residential Generator Installer is responsible for expertly installing, maintaining, and servicing backup generators for residential properties. This role involves working with electrical systems, ensuring proper generator functionality, and providing homeowners with a reliable source of backup power during outages. The Residential Generator Installer collaborates with clients, project managers, and team members to deliver seamless generator installations that prioritize safety and client satisfaction.

Work Location & Schedule:

Our warehouse is located at:

232 Northside Ln, Crossville, TN 38571

Team members typically begin their workday by arriving at the warehouse around 6:30 AM to prepare for the day. This includes reviewing job assignments, loading materials and equipment, confirming project details, and ensuring all necessary tools and safety gear are ready.

After morning preparation, crews travel in company vehicles to scheduled job sites to complete installations and service work. Workdays may vary depending on project scope and customer needs, but punctuality and preparedness are essential to maintaining our high standards of service and efficiency.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Installation: Skillfully install residential backup generators in compliance with manufacturer specifications, local electrical codes, and safety guidelines.
  • Site Assessment: Conduct thorough on-site assessments to determine the most suitable location for the generator, considering factors such as proximity to the main electrical panel, noise considerations, fuel sources, and proper ventilation.
  • Electrical Connections: Connect the generator to the main electrical panel through an automatic transfer switch (ATS) or manual transfer switch, ensuring correct wiring, load balancing, and circuit protection.
  • Mechanical Assembly: Assemble and install generator components, including engines, alternators, exhaust systems, and fuel systems, following manufacturer guidelines and best practices.
  • Fuel Source Integration: Integrate the generator with the appropriate fuel source, such as natural gas lines or propane tanks, and ensure efficient fuel delivery to the generator system.
  • Testing and Commissioning: Thoroughly test and commission the generator to ensure it functions reliably, automatically starts during power outages, and supplies the required power to essential circuits.
  • Client Education: Educate homeowners about the generator's operation, maintenance requirements, and emergency procedures. Address any client inquiries and concerns regarding the system.
  • Documentation: Maintain accurate records of installations, maintenance activities, repairs, and client interactions. Complete necessary paperwork and reports for both clients and internal use.
  • Safety and Compliance: Adhere strictly to safety protocols, electrical codes, and relevant regulations to ensure the safety of yourself, clients, and team members.
  • Team Collaboration: Collaborate effectively with project managers, fellow installers, and support staff to ensure smooth project coordination and successful installations.

Qualifications and Skills:

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Basic mechanical and electrical knowledge or willingness to learn
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills
  • Willingness to work outdoors in varying weather conditions
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Ability to follow instructions and work effectively in a team
  • Working knowledge of computers and mobile devices

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation package based on experience and qualifications
  • 10 paid-time-off (PTO) days for vacation, sick leave, and personal days
  • 9 paid holidays to observe major national holidays
  • 401(k) retirement plan with company matching
  • Comprehensive health, vision, and dental insurance coverage
  • Opportunities for career growth and professional development

title: Cloud Operations Engineer
description:
About :

is the world’s leading commerce partnership marketing platform, transforming the way businesses grow by enabling them to discover, manage, and scale partnerships across the entire customer journey. From affiliates and influencers to content publishers, brand ambassadors, and customer advocates, impact.com empowers brands to drive trusted, performance-based growth through authentic relationships. Its award-winning products - Performance (affiliate), Creator (influencer), and Advocate (customer referral) - unify every type of partner into one integrated platform. As consumers increasingly rely on recommendations from people and communities they trust, impact.com helps brands show up where it matters most. Today, over 5,000 global brands - including Walmart, Uber, Shopify, Lenovo, and Fanatics - rely on impact.com to power more than 350,000 partnerships that deliver measurable business results.

Your Role at :

The Cloud Operations Engineer will work within Impact's Data Group and is responsible for designing, scaling, and maintaining the infrastructure powering our core Data Platform. Working alongside our senior engineers, the individual will operate within a high-throughput Google Cloud Platform (GCP) environment, supporting squads across the R&D organization. Key responsibilities include administrating high-volume event streaming platforms (Cloudera Kafka), optimizing distributed databases (SingleStore, Bigtable), provisioning secure application access paths, and automating deployment workflows using modern Infrastructure as Code (IaC) principles. The individual will also spearhead platform observability initiatives for high-throughput data architectures—integrating telemetry, centralized logging, and proactive alerting across Kafka, SingleStore, and adjacent GCP environments—to bolster system resilience and streamline incident remediation workflows.

What You'll Do:

  • Cloud Infrastructure & Networking: Manage daily operations, networking configurations, and infrastructure projects in Google Cloud Platform (GCP). Design and implement Private Service Connect (PSC) endpoints, Internal Application Load Balancers (ILBs), Serverless Network Endpoint Groups (NEGs), custom firewall rules, and DNS configurations.
  • Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Standardize and deploy all cloud resources programmatically using Terraform, managing states and pipelines across staging and production workspaces via Terrakube.
  • Access Control & Secrets Management: Securely manage project-level IAM, Google Groups access structures, and workload authorization. Implement Workload Identity Federation (WIF) for secure cross-organization data exchange and CI/CD pipelines, configure Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) for internal tools, and manage production credentials utilizing HashiCorp Vault.
  • Streaming & Distributed Data Systems:

title: Senior Documentum/ Java Developer
description:

Project Background:
The IT Compliance organization, Compliance Operations, Legal Systems Section, supports the Office of Chief Counsel (OCC), is the chief legal officer of the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and serves as counsel and legal advisor to the IRS Commissioner on all matters pertaining to the administration and enforcement of the Internal Revenue laws and related statutes, as well as non-tax legal questions. The IT Enterprise Operations Group (EOPS) and User and Network Services (UNS) teams operate and maintain a nationwide technical infrastructure in support of the OCC’s mission- critical automation activities.

The scope of this support effort for the Office of Chief Counsel systems and components, also referred to as the Counsel Automated Legal Systems - CALS:

  • Counsel Automated Systems Environment Management Information System (CASE-MIS).
  • Chief Counsel Macros (CCMACROS).
  • Chief Counsel Check (CCACHECK).
  • Electronic Tax Court Services (eTCS).
  • Electronic Word (eWord).
  • electronic Counsel Inventory Tracking Environment (eCITE).
  • Intelligent Document Management System (IDMS).

For each of the applications outlined above as part of the CALS project, the support team will collaborate with the CALS government team, IT partners, Business Systems Planning (BSP), and Chief Counsel end users to provide application maintenance and change request support.

This includes the following for each application:

  • Break-fix: Analyze, remediate, test, and support deployment of any application Production defects.
  • IT Mandates: Support hardware and software upgrades as dictated by IT to remain in compliance, including Product upgrades of Oracle, Windows, Linux, Documentum, and .NET. This also includes application/platform modernization efforts deemed necessary by IT and Chief Counsel constituents.
  • Tax Reform Updates: Support software upgrades, including design, development, and testing, in support of any mandated tax law or tax code changes. Several changes are initiated annually by US Tax Court and require updates to the eTCS application.
  • Technical Lead: Collaborate with the CALS Government management team to provide support in the following areas: scheduling, Scrum Master activities, One Software Development Life Cycle OneSDLC activities including annual milestone reviews, and Agile, DevOps, and CI/CD methodology and tool adoption.

  • Security Management: Collaborate with the CALS Government team and BSP Security Program Management Officer (SPMO) to review monthly security audit scans, prioritize findings, and work with the appropriate IT partners to remediate and validate the fixes.

title: Construction Project Manager
description:
Are you passionate about your work and seeking a new community? At SEG, we’re not just focused on where we’ve been, but where we’re headed. We offer a welcoming environment where success is celebrated together. Join us in our journey of growth with a sense of belonging.

SEG is a leading Engineering and Construction firm specializing in design build, government construction projects. With a track record of delivering high-quality projects on time and within budget, we are committed to excellence and innovation in every aspect of our work.

We are currently seeking a talented Construction Project Manager Position to join our team and a grow with the company.

SEG’s Project Manager 1 must demonstrate the ability to manage the cradle-to-grave aspects of the entire life-cycle of a commercial and/or institutional design/build project. The position includes an understanding of process management and the ability and agility to perform work that is contracted through a variety of delivery methods that include: indefinite delivery indefinite quantity (IDIQ), Lump-Sum Contracting and Design/Build contracts. The Project Manager 1 accomplishes work by means of subcontractors; however, the Project Manager 1 must have the ability to manage self-performed construction activities where those resources may benefit the project.

Scope of Project Manager 1 Position
Manages all aspects of project management for multiple small projects or a mid-sized project with an approximate annual volume of $2–17 million.

Essential Functions of Project Manager 1 Position
Good working knowledge of civil, architectural, mechanical or electrical discipline and a basic understanding of the other disciplines. Good analytical skills and the ability to effectively use a variety of estimating, scheduling and reporting software tools. The ability to effectively communicate with management, subcontractors, customers and peer groups. Ability to travel to different jobsites within a designated geographical area.

Project Manager 1 Responsibilities

  • Manage the construction workflow process starting in the project origination phase, to include negotiation, contracting, buyout, construction administration, financial management and closeout;
  • Support efforts to meet with Owners and Design Professionals to determine project requirements, manage client satisfaction, and take immediate action to help resolve problems and concerns;
  • Acquire and manage all building permits and other regulatory prerequisites;
  • Visit project work sites as needed and coordinate with project superintendent to support field efforts;
  • Evaluate projects for constructability and value-engineer cost savings;
  • Establish, monitor, communicate and maintain project schedules utilizing contemporary scheduling software;
  • Develop and implement strategies to self-perform work and to outsource the various aspects of a project to achieve the projects objectives of price, schedule and quality;
  • Support the effort to negotiate contracts, subcontracts and purchase orders to assure that all project goals are being addressed;
  • Proactively identify issues that could lead to problems and facilitate solutions;
  • Conduct and document project progress meetings;
  • Determine and implement the appropriate level of project control (i.e.: submittal logs, change order logs, etc.);
  • Manage project costs to ensure budgets are maintained. Document and manage changes in the work to ensure the interests of all stakeholders in the project are reasonably met;
  • Create and follow up on monthly requisitions to the Owner and maintain a regular dialogue with the project(s) vendors to ensure all financial matters are kept within contract terms;
  • Ensure that all aspects of the project are compliant with all contract terms and legal requirements that govern the project and the community in which the project(s) takes place;
  • Administer client-specific programs, such as CQM, Safety, etc.
  • Document substantial completion; manage the project closeout process to ensure timely completion;
  • Support the Corporate Estimating Department with overall strategy, RFI process, scope summary sheets, subcontractor outreach and others aspects that will ensure the team’s success;
  • Provide training, mentoring and coaching to assist and develop other members of the project team;

Minimum Qualifications

  • B.S. degree in Engineering or Construction Management with 5-7 years of experience with a commercial and/or industrial general contractor or 10+ years of directly related experience with no degree.
  • Demonstrated experience managing self-performed work activities and subcontracted work.
  • A good working knowledge of construction means and methods associated with the renovation of commercial and institutional buildings and site work related thereto.
  • High level of proficiency with spreadsheets, email and other software used in the construction industry.
  • A minimum of 3 years of experience in government contracting is preferred.
  • Current safety credentials to include OSHA 30, First Aid and CPR.
  • Current CQM certification issued by USACE / NAVFAC.
  • Professional credentials – either Engineer in Training (EIT) or Project Management Professional (PMP) desired.

  • Paid Time Off
  • Continuing Education Assistance

  • E-ZPass to assist with commute expenses

Work Environment:
The role involves working on construction sites, in offices, and traveling to different project locations. Involves exposure to construction site conditions, including weather, noise, and potential hazards.

title: JP Morgan Chase - Payments Data Scientist Associate
description:
About ChaseNet:

ChaseNet is JPMorganChase's proprietary closed-loop payments network that connects Chase-issued cardholders directly with merchants acquired by Chase Merchant Services. By routing eligible transactions through a single Chase-owned rail rather than the traditional open-loop network, ChaseNet simplifies the economics of card acceptance, enables customized pricing constructs, and delivers richer transaction data to both merchants and the firm. ChaseNet supports some of the largest merchants in the United States and plays a central role in Chase's merchant services growth strategy.

As a ChaseNet Data Scientist, Associate in the ChaseNet Analytics team, you will work with large and complex payments datasets to generate insights that inform pricing strategy, merchant profitability, portfolio performance, and strategic decision-making.

Job Responsibilities:

- Manage, transform, and analyze large payments datasets to support ChaseNet pricing, profitability, and portfolio optimization initiatives.

- Design, build, and maintain recurring and ad-hoc reporting that provides visibility into ChaseNet performance, revenue drivers, and merchant economics.

- Develop analytical frameworks and models to evaluate pricing scenarios, interchange impacts, repricing opportunities, and merchant business cases.

- Partner with product, pricing, finance, and relationship management teams to translate business questions into structured analyses and clear recommendations.

- Write efficient, well-documented SQL and Python code to extract, process, and analyze data from large-scale payments platforms.

- Support governance, quality control, and process improvement across analytics workflows, including automation and documentation.

- Communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences through written narratives, visualizations, and presentations.

- Contribute to innovation initiatives, including the use of AI and emerging technologies to improve analytical capabilities and decision support.

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills:

- Degree with 3+ years of experience.

- Understanding of SQL-based coding and Python.

- Consulting orientation with the ability to influence both internal and external business partners.

- Understanding of the payments value chain, including merchants, brands, acquirers, networks, and issuers.

- Proven experience working in large teams in an advanced analytical environment.

- Proven experience with emerging technologies related to insights and the ability to do rapid prototyping (in Tableau).

- Ability to synthesize data sets into streamlined, clear, and actionable messages.

- Experience creating business initiatives and communicating ideas with a digitally focused and data-driven mindset.

- Proven ability to develop relationships with a wide array of partners, executives, and customers.

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills:

- AI/ML and automation skills, AI/ML solutions creation, and software engineering skills preferred.

- Experience in the payments industry and/or technology-enabled industries (preferred but not required).

- Working knowledge of the credit card value chain, including the roles of issuers, acquirers, networks, processors, and merchants.

- Familiarity with network fees and interchange economics, including how interchange categories, assessments, and network-level fees are structured.

- Familiarity with processing fees and merchant pricing constructs such as interchange-plus, blended pricing, and tiered pricing.
